0354c832e0d018af:04.statement:

Every cap containing an endpoint centroid has $q_i<\gamma_dc$ and misses the lifted middle centroid. Let $I_0$ be the nonempty set containing the lifted middle centroid. For $i\in I_0$, $q_i\ge\gamma_dc$ and $U_i+V_i<\gamma_d\min(a,b)$.

For a body $D$ and $u\ne0$ write $S_D(u)=\sup_s\mathcal H^{d-1}(D\cap\{u\cdot x=s\})/\|u\|$. A cap of mass $w<\gamma_d|D|$ misses $g_D$ by a signed functional deficit at least $(\gamma_d|D|-w)/S_D(u)$. Put $D_i^-=(\gamma_da-U_i)/S_A(u_i)$, $D_i^+=(\gamma_db-V_i)/S_B(u_i)$ on $I_0$. Then $-u_i\cdot(m-g)\ge(D_i^-+D_i^+)/2$ there. Write $\ell_i^-=u_i\cdot(g_A-y)-\beta_i$, $\ell_i^0=u_i\cdot(g-y)$, $\ell_i^+=u_i\cdot(g_B-y)+\beta_i$. Their respective $\lambda_i$-weighted sums are $-\Delta,0,\Delta$. Set $P_\pm=\sum_i\lambda_i(\ell_i^\pm)_+$. Then
$
\begin{aligned}
P_-&\ge \Big(\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_iD_i^--\Delta\Big)_+,
& P_+&\ge \Big(\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_iD_i^++\Delta\Big)_+,\\
P_-+P_+&\ge\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_i(D_i^-+D_i^+),
& \sum_i\lambda_i\big(u_i\cdot(m-g)\big)_+
&\ge\tfrac12\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_i(D_i^-+D_i^+).
\end{aligned}
$

$$D(y_1)\ge V(\Gamma b^d+\lambda a^d),\qquad D(y_2)\ge V(\Gamma+\lambda h^d).$$
For $M=V(a^d+b^d+1+c^d)$ and $J=(1-R^{-1/p})^{-p}$,
$$\max\{D(y_1),D(y_2)\}\ge\Gamma M/2+\frac{\Gamma V}{2t}[(t-1)(1-b^d)-tJx^d].$$
The sharper clipped loss over $0\le v\le b$ in the scalar certificate can replace $Jx^d$. In particular one of these two centroids reaches normalized depth $\Gamma/2$ whenever
$$\frac{1-b}{b}\le(1-R^{-1/p})\left[\frac{d(t-1)}{t(2d/(d+1))^d}\right]^{1/p}.$$

03cc52bdd22fe702:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $t>1$, $1/2<b\le1$, $p=d-1$, $R=2t-1$, and $x=2d(1-b)/(d+1)$. Write $B=b^d$, $S=1-B$, $A_{\max}=(2b-1)^d$, $Z=A_{\max}-S/t$, and $H=[c-x]_+^d$. For $0\le A\le A_{\max}$ and $0\le c\le b$, put
$$G(A,c)=\max\{B+tA,1+tH\}-(A+B+1+c^d)/2.$$
Its minimum over $A$ is attained at $\widehat A=\min(A_{\max},H+S/t)$ and satisfies
$$2G(\widehat A,c)=-c^d+\max\{S-A_{\max}+2tH,(1-1/t)S+RH\}.$$
If $x\ge b$, take $c=b$ to minimize over $c$. If $0<x<b$, write $H_\alpha=x^d/(\alpha^{1/p}-1)^d$ for $\alpha>1$. The minimum over $c$ is attained at
$$H=\min\{(b-x)^d,\max\{H_{2t},\min\{Z,H_R\}\}\},\qquad c=x+H^{1/d}.$$
If $b=1$, the overall minimum is zero.

For every $x\ge0,\alpha>1$, the sharp loss over $v\ge0$ is
$$\max_{v\ge0}\{v^d-\alpha[v-x]_+^d\}=x^d(1-\alpha^{-1/p})^{-p}.$$
Over $0\le v\le b$, use the same value if $x\le b(1-\alpha^{-1/p})$ and use $b^d-\alpha[b-x]_+^d$ otherwise. If $L$ is this clipped loss with $\alpha=R$, then
$$G(A,c)\ge\frac{(t-1)S-tL}{2t}.$$
In particular $G(A,c)\ge0$ uniformly in both endpoints whenever
$$\frac{1-b}{b}\le(1-R^{-1/p})\left[\frac{d(t-1)}{t(2d/(d+1))^d}\right]^{1/p}.$$

$$

04fb8b3cc0275a7f:02.statement:
Let $B$ be a positive-length interval, $k\ge1$ an integer, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf1_B\,dx$, and $\eta(B)=\alpha|B|$ with $\alpha\in[0,1]$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf1_B\,dx+k\eta$. Denote by $\Psi_k(\alpha)$ the infimum of $(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$ over all such $B,\eta$ and all closed line halfspaces $H\ni g$. Then $\Psi_1(\alpha)=(1+\alpha^2)/2$. For $k\ge2$ set $L_k=(\sqrt{(k+1)/3}-1)/k$ and $U_k=(\sqrt{k(k+1)}-1)/k$. Then
$$
\Psi_k(\alpha)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \alpha+\frac{1+k\alpha^2}{2(1+k\alpha)},&0\le\alpha\le L_k,\\
\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{(1+k\alpha)^2+k+1}-3-k\alpha}{k},&L_k\le\alpha\le U_k,\\
\displaystyle \frac{k\alpha^2-(k-1)\alpha+k}{k+1},&U_k\le\alpha\le1.
\end{cases}
$$
The branches agree at the junctions and indicator bands attain the values. The endpoint values are $\Psi_k(0)=1/2$ and $\Psi_k(1)=1$. The minimum over $\alpha$ is $1/2$ uniquely at $\alpha=0$ for $k=1$, and $(\sqrt{3(k+1)}-2)/k$ uniquely at $\alpha=L_k$ for $k\ge2$. For $k\ge2$ an upper-end band of relative mass $L_k$ attains this minimum.

$$
\sum_i\mu(H_i)\ge 4a/3+\min(2b/3,k/27)>4a/3.

D=\left\{x: 0\le x_1\le\frac{11}{18},\
0\le x_i\le\frac19\ (2\le i\le8),\
\frac7{18}\le\sum_{i=1}^8x_i\le1\right\},\qquad
C=2\lambda\operatorname{diag}(q,1,\ldots,1)D,

05d41ace8d693538:01.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with an interior point $y$ of barycentric coordinates $y_i$. For each $i$, let an actual cap cut $T$ in a cap containing $v_i$ strictly and excluding all other vertices strictly. Suppose its own proper section has centroid $y$. Use unit continuous inward normals $u_i$, own section areas $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(T\cap\partial H_i)$, and positive response weights $\theta_i$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Assume $\sum_i\theta_iS_iu_i=0$, as holds if all response coarea is on this fiber.

Put $r_i=1-dy_i$, $q_i=|T\cap H_i|/|T|$, and $B=\sum_i r_i/q_i$. Then $r_i>0$, $q_i=\prod_{j\ne i}dy_j$ and $\theta_i=(r_i/q_i)/B$. The mean of $W=\sum_i\theta_i\mathbf1_{H_i}$ with respect to uniform surface measure on **each** full facet of $T$ is
$$
\frac1B=\frac{\prod_i(1-r_i)}{1-\sum_i r_i^2}\ge\Gamma_d,\qquad
\Gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d .
$$
Equality is precisely uniform $r$ for $d\ge2$, and the ratio is always $1/2$ for $d=1$. Use endpoint counting measure for $d=1$. An admissible nonnegative field, convex in the physical coordinates for each fixed normal, whose measured boundary trace is a positive constant on one entire own facet and zero elsewhere, has this same weighted capture efficiency.

09cd5673b7dfb72e:6.statement:
Let $D$ be a nonempty compact convex planar set with horizontal projection $I=[a,b]$, and let $E=\{0\}\times[e_-,e_+]$ with $e_-\le e_+$. Let $A(t)$ be the area of $D+tE$ intersected with finitely many halfplanes $p_ix+q_iy\ge h_i+k_it$, each with nonzero normal. For $x\in I$, take the lower section bound $L_t(x)$ as the maximum of the lower endpoint of $D+tE$ and all lower bounds from $q_i>0$, and $U_t(x)$ as the corresponding minimum for the upper endpoint and $q_i<0$. At $t=0$ let $\dot L$ be the maximum velocity of the active lower bounds, and $\dot U$ the minimum velocity of the active upper bounds. Write $g_0=(U_0-L_0)_+$. The function $\dot g$ is $\dot U-\dot L$ where $U_0>L_0$, zero where $U_0<L_0$, and $(\dot U-\dot L)_+$ at equality.

The vertical cuts and the two bounds $a,b$ give a feasible horizontal interval with lower endpoint $a_t$ the maximum of the affine lower bounds and upper endpoint $b_t$ the minimum of the affine upper bounds. Compute $\dot a,\dot b$ by maximum and minimum of the corresponding tied endpoint velocities at zero. Then
$$
A'(0+)=
\begin{cases}
0,& a_0>b_0,\\
(\dot b-\dot a)_+g_0(a_0),&a_0=b_0,\\
\displaystyle\int_{a_0}^{b_0}\dot g(x)\,dx+\dot b\,g_0(b_0)-\dot a\,g_0(a_0),&a_0<b_0.
\end{cases}
$$
If $I$ is a singleton the area is identically zero.

0ab50bc17861492a:01.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, $H>0$ and $0<U<H$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le U$, $|x|\le r(z)$, use the measure of density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. For a finite slope $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. A law's record is the average of $(P,C,M)$, and a law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero.

Given any probability law on finite slopes $s\ge0$, let $\phi$ be the mixture of the uniform probabilities on $[-s,s]$, with the layer at $s=0$ interpreted as $\delta_0$. 0ab50bc17861492a:03.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, $H>0$ and $0<U<H$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le U$, $|x|\le r(z)$, use the measure of density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. Set $a=r(U)$, $T=U/a$, $t=a^d=[H/(B+T)]^d$, $V_0=B/d$, and $V=(1-t)V_0$. The associated cone has the same density formula on $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, and mass $V_0$.

For a finite slope $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. A law's record is the average of $(P,C,M)$, and a law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero.

Write $R_f(s)=(P_f(s),C_f(s),M_f(s))$ for the frustum record and $R_c(s)$ for the cone record. Every finite slope has positive frustum and cone coarea. The frustum records have a limit $R_f(\infty)=(V/2,0,0)$, which defines the record at the optional endpoint $\infty$.

If $T\le1$, then $M_f(s)<0$ for every finite $s>0$. Each centered law on $[0,\infty]$ is supported on $\{0,\infty\}$ and its averages obey $P-cC=V/2$ with the same $c=(P_f(0)-V/2)/C_f(0)$ for all such laws.

If $T\ge1$, the bounded cone and frustum records and the finite frustum tail satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_f(s)&=R_c(s)-(tV_0,0,0) &&(0\le s\le T),\\
R_f(s)&=\frac Ts R_f(T)+\left(1-\frac Ts\right)R_f(\infty) &&(T\le s<\infty).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus every probability law on $[0,\infty]$ has a representative supported on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ with the same frustum records. If the original law is centered and the representative has positive finite mass, its conditional finite law is centered for the cone as well as for the frustum.

For $T\ge1$, let $\mu,\nu$ be separately centered probability laws on cone slopes $[0,T]$. Use $P_\mu^c,P_\nu^c,C_\mu,C_\nu$ for their averaged cone cap and coarea records. If $P_\mu^f,P_\nu^f$ denote the corresponding frustum cap records, the coareas are the same, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_c&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^c+C_\mu(V_0-P_\nu^c)}{V_0(C_\mu+C_\nu)},&
\omega&=\frac{C_\nu}{C_\mu+C_\nu},\\
\beta_f&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^f+C_\mu(V-P_\nu^f)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
       =\frac{\beta_c-t\omega}{1-t}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For arbitrary separately centered frustum laws, use their record-preserving representatives on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ and write $\lambda_\mu,\lambda_\nu$ for their finite masses. If both are positive, let $\beta_f$ in the next formula be the bounded frustum ratio of their conditional finite laws, and $C_\mu,C_\nu$ their conditional finite coareas. The ratio for the original pair is

$$
\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\mu\lambda_\nu(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
{\lambda_\mu C_\mu+\lambda_\nu C_\nu}\left(\beta_f-\frac12\right).
$$

If exactly one law has zero coarea, the ratio is $1/2$. If both have zero coarea, the literal quotient has zero denominator, and its continuous extension has value $1/2$. Each cap record in that case is $V/2$. For $T\le1$ the positive-denominator ratio for any separately centered pair is $1/2$, with the same extension at zero total coarea.

0da12d076aef855c:01.statement:
Let $r\ge2$ and let $f$ be a nonnegative Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^r$ of mass in $(0,\infty)$ with full-dimensional positive support. Assume the extended function $g=f^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex, taking value $+\infty$ where $f=0$. Translate an arbitrary interior anchor to $0$ and write $U=\operatorname{int}\{f>0\}$. The radial body $B$ has radii
$$
\rho_B(u)^r=r\int_0^\infty t^{r-1}f(tu)\,dt,\qquad u\in\mathbb S^{r-1}.
$$
Then $B$ is a compact convex body containing $0$ in its interior, with volume equal to the mass of $f$, and it preserves every through-anchor closed halfspace mass. If $B$ is a simplex, let $p_B$ denote its Minkowski gauge. In that case there are a linear functional $\ell$, $R\in(0,\infty]$ and a positive continuous $F$ on $[0,R)$ such that $h=F^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex and nondecreasing and
$$
r\int_0^R t^{r-1}F(t)\,dt=1.
$$
If $R<\infty$, then $R\max_B\ell\le1$. If $R=\infty$, then $\ell=0$. The map $\Phi(b)=b/(1-\ell(b))$ is a bijection from $\{p_B<R\}$ onto $U$, with inverse $\Psi(x)=x/(1+\ell(x))$ and positive denominators on their domains. On $U$,
$$
f(x)=(1+\ell(x))^{-r-1}F\!\left(\frac{p_B(x)}{1+\ell(x)}\right).
$$
Equivalently, $f(x)\,dx$ is the pushforward of $F(p_B(b))\,db$ restricted to $\{p_B<R\}$. Boundary values are immaterial. The functional $\ell$ is uniquely determined: for $L(x)=g'(0;x)/g(0)$, where the derivative is one-sided, $L=\ell+c p_B$ with $c\ge0$. If $v_i$ are the vertices and $0=\sum_i\alpha_i v_i$ is the strictly positive barycentric row of $0$, then $c=\sum_i\alpha_i L(v_i)$.

Conversely, every compact convex body $B$ containing $0$ in its interior and every triple $(\ell,R,F)$ meeting the displayed conditions gives by this construction an integrable density of mass $|B|$ with convex extended inverse $(r+1)$st root and radial body $B$. The finite endpoint equality $R\max_B\ell=1$ is allowed.

For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, let $\mu_K$ be the measure obtained by summing $d$-dimensional volume on its integer fibers. Let $B$ be the standard $4$-simplex, of volume $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_4$, where $\lambda_1=x_1$. Put

m=\frac{|L|}{V}=\left(\frac{83}{100}\right)^4-\left(\frac{800001}{1000000}\right)^4.
$$
Set $Q=m^{-1/4}$, $r=2-Q$, $A=rL$, $C_+=QL$, and $a=(2m^{1/4}-1)^4$. Let $K$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $A,B,C_+$ at levels $-1,0,1$, respectively. Its integer fibers are precisely $A,B,C_+$ with masses $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-8}$.

Its mixed mass is $(1+a)V>(2+a)V/2$ and its mixed centroid is $(0,c)$, where
$$
\lambda_1(c)=\frac15-4e,\qquad \lambda_i(c)=\frac15+e\ (i\ne1),\qquad
e=\frac{(83/400-h/5)a}{1+a},\qquad \frac a5\le e\le\frac{83a}{400}.
$$

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,c)$ has $\mu_{K'}$-mass at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)V$. The normalized depth of $(0,c)$ in $K'$ is at least $\Gamma_4$, and its normalized depth in $K$ is at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)/(2+a)>\Gamma_4/2$.

0de198a47cdc74fc:02.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact sets. Write $\mu$ for the sum of the $d$-volumes of their integer fibers. Order the nonempty fiber bases of each input by one linear functional injective on each base set. Denote the respective fiber volumes by $a_i$ and $b_j$, allowing zero volumes. For every full monotone path $P$ from $(1,1)$ to $(m,k)$ in this ordered grid, using steps $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$,
$$
\mu(A+B)\ge\sum_{(i,j)\in P}(a_i^{1/d}+b_j^{1/d})^d.
$$
If both base sets lie in one common parity coset, the corresponding bound for $\mu((A+B)/2)$ has an extra factor $2^{-d}$. In particular, if $A$ is supported on one parity coset and is contained in a compact convex set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}$, then
$$
\mu(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d))
\ge \mu((A+A)/2)
\ge \sum_{i=1}^m a_i+\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}\left(\frac{a_i^{1/d}+a_{i+1}^{1/d}}2\right)^d.
$$

0e1bf4bac5d35265:07.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For every such $U$ and every $\sigma\in\mathcal W$ one has
$$
\frac1M\int_S\log(U/L)\,dm
\le\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i\log\frac{U(Y_i)}{l_i}.
\tag{2}
$$
This also holds for continuous nonnegative concave $U$ on $C$ that are positive in the interior of every sampled fiber and have integrable sampled $\log U$. If $U(Y_i)\le l_i$ for all $i$ and the left-hand side is zero, then $U=L$ on every closed sampled fiber.

The function $H_C$ is finite, concave, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on the positive orthant, with $H_C(cb)=H_C(b)+\log c$ for $c>0$. One has $H_C(l)=0$, attained by $L$, and
$$
\partial^+H_C(l)=\left\{\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\right)_{i=1}^k:\ \sigma\in\mathcal W\right\},
\tag{3}
$$
where $\partial^+$ consists of the supergradients for the concave function. In particular $\mathcal W$ is compact and convex, and for every $h\in\mathbb R^k$ and $t\downarrow0$,
$$
H_C(l+th+o(t))=t\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i \frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}+o(t).
\tag{4}
$$

0e4cb84a76d46e82:01.statement:
Let $\Phi(h,\theta)$ be the original mixed cap mass of a finite-dimensional body family at a specified source in one fixed integer fiber, with $\theta$ a local chart of through-source nonvertical normal directions. Suppose $\Phi$ is $C^2$ near $(h_0,\theta_0)$, $\Phi_\theta(h_0,\theta_0)=0$, and $K=\Phi_{\theta\theta}(h_0,\theta_0)$ is positive definite. There is a unique nearby stationary branch $\theta(h)$, a strict local minimum in $\theta$. With $V(h)=\Phi(h,\theta(h))$, $A=\Phi_{hh}$ and $B=\Phi_{h\theta}$ at the base, one has $DV=\Phi_h(h,\theta(h))$ and $D^2V(h_0)=A-BK^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}$.

Suppose moreover that a fixed compact set of normal parameters gives the full minimum for all nearby $h$, that cap mass is jointly continuous there, and that its complete minimizing menu at $h_0$ is finite. If each member is interior to a chart in that domain and satisfies the preceding differentiability and positive-definiteness hypotheses, the full minimum near $h_0$ is the minimum of the corresponding local branches.

0e4cb84a76d46e82:02.statement:
For a symmetric matrix $K\succeq0$, set $b=B^{\mathsf T}v$ and $q(w)=v^{\mathsf T}Av+2b^{\mathsf T}w+w^{\mathsf T}Kw$. The infimum of $q$ is finite exactly when $b\in\operatorname{ran}K$. Then it equals $v^{\mathsf T}Av-b^{\mathsf T}K^\dagger b$ with minimizers $-K^\dagger b+\ker K$, where $\dagger$ denotes the Moore–Penrose inverse. This need not give the Hessian of a truly optimized cap or of a general optimized smooth function.

If $K\succ0$ and $Rw=d(v)$ is feasible, the minimum of the same quadratic under that constraint is
$$
v^{\mathsf T}Av-b^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}b+e^{\mathsf T}(RK^{-1}R^{\mathsf T})^\dagger e,
\qquad e=d(v)+RK^{-1}b.
$$
The constraint rows may be redundant.

$$

At the identical family the normal Hessian in $(\alpha,\theta)$ is $\operatorname{diag}(2,3)$. For a two-sided compatible linear velocity $(\rho_j,P_j,Q_j)_j$ of $(r_j,p_j,q_j)_j$, set $A_j=2\rho_j+P_j$. The reduced branch Hessian on this velocity is

0e807db2bba0c137:02.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $v$, and put $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K$ with summed fiber volume $\mu$ and mass $M=2^n v$. Write $H_j$ for the altitude from vertex $v_j$, $\lambda_j$ for its barycentric coordinate, $g$ for the centroid, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $N_0=2^n(d+1)$. Consider finite full covers of $S$ by $N$ closed ambient caps with margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, $\lVert u_i\rVert_2=1$, each of mass at most $\gamma_d v$. Each feasible cover contains, for every binary $p$ and each $j$, a distinct cap with own-fiber margin $H_j(\lambda_j(x)-1/(d+1))$ and zero cap volume on all other fibers. Thus $N\ge N_0$, and at $N=N_0$ these are exactly all the caps. For every $N\ge N_0$ the exact attained minimum is
$$
\min\sum_i\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu
=\frac{M d\gamma_d}{(d+1)^2}\sum_{j=0}^d H_j.
$$
Every feasible cover at $N=N_0$ has this value. For a regular simplex of inradius $r$ it is $M d r\gamma_d$.

0f025bdf9a51573b:03.statement:

Testing the simultaneous condition on the finite torsion subgroup is sufficient and necessary.

For any affine $h$ on the relative physical space put $C_t=C\cap\{L+th\ge0\}$ and $S_t=S\cap C_t$, for $t>0$. P(a,b)\ge\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\frac{b_j}{\sum_i a_i}\right)^{-1}

191a0eb2244ea4a9:06.statement:

$$
\frac{|C|_d}{|T|_d}\ge \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.
$$
Equality holds exactly when $p=1$ and all $q$ strictly negative margins are equal. For each $d$ and $1\le q\le d$ the bound is attained. If $p>1$ is fixed as well with $p+q\le d+1$, the bound is the infimum and is never attained.

For $d\ge2$, a proper closed centroid cap containing at least two vertices has fraction at least $\Gamma_{d-1}>\Gamma_d$. This bound is attained exactly when one vertex has positive margin, one has zero margin, and the remaining $d-1$ have equal negative margins. In dimension one, each proper closed centroid cap is a half-interval of relative length $1/2$ and contains exactly one vertex.

191a0eb2244ea4a9:09.statement:

193aa5f5cdaa5457:01.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite. Let $K_z=B_z\times[-H_z,H_z]$, $H_z>0$, be the actual sampled fibers of a canonical convex hull, where each $B_z$ is a positive $(d-1)$-dimensional compact convex body. For $d=1$, use a singleton of measure one. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ for the placed sampled fibers, $\mu$ for their summed original mixed $d$-volume, $M=\mu(S)$ for its mass, and $\eta$ for summed roof area at the points $s=(\xi,H)=(z,X,H_z)$ with $X\in B_z$.

Let $\Pi(ds,ds')=\nu(ds)P_s(ds')$ be any finite martingale coupling from a measure $\nu$ on this same roof to $\eta$. Let $t$ have the uniform probability law $dt/2$ on $[-1,1]$. Under the joint measure $d\Omega=2H'\,d\Pi\,dt/2$ define $w=(\xi,tH)$ and $w'=(\xi',tH')$. Its target is exactly $\mu$ and its source, denoted $\mu_\nu$, is the column lift of $2H\nu$ by the uniform law of $t$. Both masses equal $M$. If $d\nu=f\,d\eta$, then $d\mu_\nu(w)=f(z,X,H_z)\,d\mu(w)$.

The physical conditional drift of $w'$ from $w$ is
$$
\left(\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_{P_s}(\xi',H')}{H},
      \frac{t\,\operatorname{Var}_{P_s}(H')}{H}\right).
$$
The lift is a physical martingale exactly when $H'=H$ $\Pi$-almost everywhere, equivalently when $\int H^2\,d(\eta-\nu)=0$. The target-minus-source first moment of $\xi$ is $2\int\operatorname{Cov}_{P_s}(\xi',H')\,d\nu(s)$ and both vertical first moments vanish. In the projective coordinates $(\xi/H,y/H,1/H)$ the lift is always a martingale. The resulting convex order in those coordinates also follows directly by a perspective test on the roof.

Put $t_0=\varepsilon/3$, $Y=(0,t_0)$, $A=1+\varepsilon^2/3$, $V=9A$ and $Q=4A$. Take $n_1=(1,0),n_2=(0,1),n_3=(-1,-1)$ and $N_i(\beta)=(n_i,\beta)$. The closed cap $H_i(\beta,c)=\{W:N_i(\beta)\cdot(W-Y)\ge c\}$ has the unique raw $Q$-quantile threshold
$$
c_\beta=2-\beta t_0-\sqrt{4-4\beta t_0-\beta^2/3},
\quad |\beta|\le1/8.
$$
Near this threshold its raw mass is $Q+(A/3)\beta^2-(4-2\beta t_0)c+c^2$. Its section coarea in the displayed normal units is $S_\beta=2\sqrt{4-4\beta t_0-\beta^2/3}$. Also $0\le c_\beta\le13\beta^2/108$, with equality to zero only for $\beta=0$, and $c_\beta=(A/12)\beta^2+O(\beta^3)$ as $\beta\to0$.

The intersection of all inequalities $N_i(\beta)\cdot h\le c_\beta$ for this range of $\beta$ is $\{0\}$, and every point $Y+h$ of raw depth at least $Q$ satisfies them. For $g>0$, $\beta>0$, the positive coefficients $g/(3\beta)$ combine the displayed normals to $g e_t$ and the thresholds to $gc_\beta/\beta=(gA/12)\beta+O(\beta^2)$. Negative tilts recover $-g e_t$ with coefficients $g/(3|\beta|)$. For unit normals at positive tilt the total coefficient is $g[2\sqrt{1+\beta^2}+\sqrt{2+\beta^2}]/(3\beta)$ with the same combined threshold. Any nonnegative combination of unit normals with vertical components bounded by $\eta>0$ in magnitude and vertical sum $g$ has total coefficient at least $|g|/\eta$.

19899b61b9ca5f3a:04.statement:
Use raw summed volume of a finite family of compact convex fibers with positive $d$-dimensional volume, and let $Y$ be interior to its own fiber with raw depth $Q$. Let finitely many nonvertical critical closed caps through $Y$ have mass $Q$ and continuous normals $u_j$ positively balanced by weights $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j=1$. Linearly perturb their full normals to $N_j+sN'_j$ with continuous parts $u_j+s w_j$. Define $m_j(W)=N_j\cdot(W-Y)$, $\ell_j(W)=N'_j\cdot(W-Y)$ and $F_j(s,c)=\mu\{m_j+s\ell_j\ge c\}$. Assume $F_j$ is $C^2$ near $(0,0)$ and $S_j=-\partial_cF_j(0,0)>0$. Put $A_j=\partial_{ss}F_j(0,0)$. Then $\partial_sF_j(0,0)=0$, $A_j\ge0$, and the actual raw $Q$-quantile threshold is
$$
c_j(s)=\frac{A_j}{2S_j}s^2+o(s^2).
$$
For $s>0$ the coefficients $\rho_j/s$ combine the continuous normals exactly to $\sum_j\rho_jw_j$ and the thresholds to $(s/2)\sum_j\rho_j A_j/S_j+o(s)$. If the missing components of unit representatives have magnitude $O(s)$, recovering a nonzero component there requires total positive coefficient $\Omega(1/s)$. With a $C^1$ cap map the scalar inversion still gives $c_j(s)=o(s)$ and the same normal identity with threshold sum $o(1)$.

Under local coarea moment regularity, writing $d\sigma$ for the sum of fiber-section areas divided by $|u_j|$, the first normal derivative is $\int_{m_j=0}\ell_j\,d\sigma$, and $A_j=-\partial_c\int_{m_j=c}\ell_j^2\,d\sigma|_{c=0}$. In particular the identities hold for stable proper, strictly full or strictly empty cuts of finite polytopal fibers whose varying planes avoid the vertices. If a continuous direction $e$ satisfies $u_j\cdot e=0$, $w_j\cdot e\ne0$ and $A_j>0$ for some $j$, then
$$
h_\mu(Y+he)\le Q-\frac{S_j^2(w_j\cdot e)^2}{2A_j}h^2+o(h^2).
$$

Use the triangle frustum, marks, normals and exact near-quantile caps of the preceding lemma, with $\gamma=Q/V=4/9$. For a bounded inward speed $v$ continuous on each closed body facet (traces on adjacent facets may differ), set
$$
D=\int_{\partial K}v\,d\mathcal H^2,\quad
L_i(\beta)=\int_{\partial K\cap H_i(\beta,c_\beta)}v\,d\mathcal H^2,\quad
R_\beta=\frac13\sum_iL_i(\beta)-\gamma D.
$$
The first cap losses below are in raw volume units after subtracting the target-level loss $\gamma D$; the corresponding probability losses divide by $V$. Where the facet speed is used for an actual deformation, assume the first losses on fixed caps and on the whole body are given by these boundary integrals. $$
R'_0=\frac13\sum_{i,F}\int_{\Gamma_i\cap\operatorname{relint}F}
\frac{v(X,t)(t-t_0)}{a_{iF}}\,d\mathcal H^1.
$$
For $g>0$ the positive normal-recovery weights give fixed-cap response $gR_\beta/\beta$ as $\beta\downarrow0$. This tends to $gR'_0$ when $R_0=0$. The actual convex erosion $K\cap\{t+e\|X\|^2\le1\}$ for $e\ge0$ has $D=(9/2)(1+\varepsilon)^4$ and $R_0=-(2/9)(1+\varepsilon)^4$, so its response tends to $-\infty$.

The actual coarea first moment about $Y$ on the near-quantile section is
$$
M_i(\beta)=\bigl(-2c_\beta v_i,\ 2t_0c_\beta+(2A/3)\beta\bigr),
$$
where $v_i$ is the corresponding triangle vertex. At a fixed $\beta$, when the mark moves at velocity $(\xi,h)$, the normal at bounded velocity $B_i(\beta)$, and the threshold relative to the mark is fixed, the first cap loss is $L_i(\beta)+S_\beta N_i(\beta)\cdot(\xi,h)-B_i(\beta)\cdot M_i(\beta)$. For an actual deformation in this assertion take compact convex bodies $K_e$ with $d_H(K_e,K)=O(|e|)$ in addition to the assumed fixed-cap first losses. $$
gR'_0+4gh-\frac{2gA}{9}\sum_i B_{i,t}(0).
$$
With normals and mark fixed, a separate retuning to the moving normalized level $\gamma$ forces threshold velocity $-[L_i(\beta)-\gamma D]/S_\beta$ for each cap.

The normalized depth at the affine-image mark is unchanged.

19aecfceb071d1da:01.statement:
Let $K=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, of volume $V>0$, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $j=0,\ldots,d$ take the proper caps $H_j=\{x:u_j\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}$ with unit normals. Each $H_j$ contains $v_j$ strictly and no other vertex strictly. Assume the normals span $\mathbb R^d$ with a positive dependence $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, $\rho_j>0$. Let $E_j=K\cap\partial H_j$, $S_j=\mathcal H^{d-1}(E_j)$, and let $g_j$ be its centroid. Use counting measure for $d=1$.

Let $\theta_j>0$ sum to one, $W=\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf1_{H_j}$ on $\partial K$, and $\beta>0$. Suppose that for every affine field $X(x)=a+B(x-y)$,
$$
\int_{\partial K} X(x)\cdot n_K(x)\,[W(x)-\beta]\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)=0.
$$
Then every $g_j=y$ and no cut contains another vertex even on its boundary. With $y_i$ the barycentric coordinates of $y$, put $r_i=1-dy_i>0$ and $q_j=|K\cap H_j|/V$. The cut on edge $v_jv_i$, $i\ne j$, is at fraction $dy_i$ from $v_j$, and
$$
q_j=\prod_{i\ne j}dy_i,\qquad
\theta_j=\frac{r_j/q_j}{\sum_i r_i/q_i},\qquad
\beta=\sum_j\theta_j q_j=\frac{\prod_i(1-r_i)}{1-\sum_i r_i^2}
\ \ge\ \Gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
$$
For $d\ge2$, equality holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid, each cap has section parallel to its opposite facet, and the weights are uniform. For $d=1$, $\beta=1/2$ and any interior mark is consistent with the hypotheses.

1a4f9cc73e4a014c:02.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ in its interior. Suppose the endpoints of the $K$ chords on the negative $y$-axis and on the positive-$x$ ray of $x+y=0$ are $(0,-\beta)$ and $(\rho,-\rho)$, with $\beta,\rho>0$. In the coordinates $u=-y$, $v=x+y$, the sector $K\cap\{y<0<x+y\}$ lies in
$$

$$
When $\beta>\rho$, its area is at most $\beta\rho^2/[2(\beta-\rho)]$. Equality holds exactly when the closure of the sector in $(u,v)$ is the corresponding closed triangle. 1d1be0b22c707856:01.statement:
Let $T\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$, centroid $g$, and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For a unit vector $u$, set $b=u\cdot g$, $\ell=\min_T u\cdot x$ and
$$
f(u)=\frac{|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge b\rbrace|}{V},\qquad
R(u)=\frac{|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge 2b-\ell\rbrace|}{V},\qquad
\rho_d=\min_{\lVert u\rVert=1}[f(u)-\Gamma_d+R(u)].
$$
Then $f(u)\ge\Gamma_d$, with equality precisely for the $d+1$ unit normals in the directions of $\nabla\lambda_i$. The constant $\rho_d$ is affine invariant; $\rho_1=0$, and for $d\ge2$,
$$
0<\rho_d\le\left(\frac{d-1}{d+1}\right)^d<\Gamma_d.
$$
Equivalently, $\rho_d$ is the minimum of $\Phi_r(\bar r)+\Phi_r(2\bar r)-\Gamma_d$ over $r=(r_0,\ldots,r_d)\in[0,1]^{d+1}$ with $\min_i r_i=0$, $\max_i r_i=1$, where $\bar r=\sum_i r_i/(d+1)$ and $\Phi_r(s)=\Pr(\sum_i r_i\lambda_i(X)\ge s)$ for $X$ uniform on $T$. In dimension two this minimum equals $2(\sqrt{10}-3)/9$ and its normalized vertex levels are $(0,1-\sqrt{2/5},1)$ up to permutation.

Let $v_0,\ldots,v_d$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero, $y_0\in\operatorname{int}K$, $s_i^0=v_i\cdot y_0$, and $h_i=h_B(v_i)$. $$
|K_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge s\}|+|A_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge 2s-h_i\}|
=Q-(k_i+2\sigma_i)(s-s_i^0)+t\eta_i+o(t),

where $k_i,\sigma_i$ are the old proper section areas on $K,A$ divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Set $\lambda_i=(k_i+2\sigma_i)^{-1}$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $q_{\rm shape}=\sum_i\lambda_i\eta_i/\Lambda$, $r=Q/M$, and $C=q_{\rm shape}-rD$.

Its common raw cap mass is $Q+t(q_{\rm shape}-vJ(q))+o(t)$ and bounds every middle depth. $$
C+v(drb-J(q)),\qquad -r[D+dv(a+k)],

$$

\left[\frac{\mu_-(B(x,a))^{1/\delta}+\mu_+(B(y,b))^{1/\delta}}2\right]^\delta.
$$

Pass to a subsequence with fixed retained labels and, for every retained cell, put $b_{ij}=\max_{C_{ij}}A_{ij}$ and $R_i=\lim_j\lambda_j(-\log b_{ij})_+$. \gamma_i(r)(\theta U+(1-\theta)V)^{1/(d-1)}

21545f87e4705da7:04.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of volume $k>0$, $d\ge1$, and $0\le\eta\le L\mathbf1_K\,dx$. Write $\alpha=\eta(K)/k$, $\delta=L-\alpha$, and let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf1_K\,dx+2\eta$. For any closed through-$g$ cap put $s=|K\cap H|/k$, $r=\eta(H)/k$, and $q=1+1/d$. Then $\max(0,\alpha-L(1-s))\le r\le\min(\alpha,Ls)$, and if $L>0$,
$$
q(1+2\alpha)s^{q-1}\ge1+2L^{1-q}r^q+2L[s+(\alpha-r)/L]^q-2Ls^q.
$$
Let $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Every closed cap containing $g$ has $s\ge b$ and $s+r\ge b+\max(0,Lb-\delta)$, where
$$
b=\Gamma_d\left(\frac{1+2L(\alpha/L)^{1+1/d}}{1+2\alpha}\right)^d
$$
for $L>0$, and $b=\Gamma_d$ when $L=0$. The bound for $s+r$ is attained when $\alpha=L$ by a simplex centroid cap.

If $2\delta\le d(1+2\alpha)$, every such containing cap satisfies
$$
s+r\ge\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}(1+2\alpha)+E_d(L,\delta),\qquad
E_d(L,\delta)=\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}-\delta\left[1-\Gamma_d+
\frac{2\Gamma_d(1+L)}{1+2L-2\delta}\right].
$$

The total volume derivative in any radial direction $\delta$ is $L_0(\delta)=\sum_{z,F}|F|\delta_z(n_F)$. On a coincident facet the term is $|F|\min(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when the body lies in the cap and $|F|\max(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when it lies on the outside. $$
L_0=\sum_j\lambda_j L_j-\eta^\top A_0 .

Here $L_j$ uses the exact noncoincident coefficients and a coefficient $\theta_{jzF}|F|$, $0\le\theta_{jzF}\le1$, at each coincidence.

\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j s_{jz}u_j z^\top=0,\qquad
dM=d\sum_j\lambda_j\mu(H_j)+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j t_j(z)s_{jz}.

If all active masses are $\beta M$, the last identity is $1=\beta\sum_j\lambda_j+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_jt_j(z)s_{jz}/(dM)$. Facet and section areas in $d=1$ use endpoint counting.

2b7d1c7e003a98d0:1.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.

2b7d1c7e003a98d0:7.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

Let $\alpha_p$ be the unique relative minimizer and $M_p=\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z$. For $p\in Q$ define
$$
T_p=\max_{\substack{0\le q_z\le m_z\\\sum_{z\in P}q_z(z-p)=0}}\sum_{z\in P}q_z,\qquad
D_p=\min_{H\ni p}\sum_{z\in P\cap H}m_z,
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed affine halfspaces in $\operatorname{aff} Q$, with the whole-space trace allowed, including rank zero. The capacity and the halfspace depth are unchanged on restriction to $P_p$ in $\operatorname{aff}F_p$. With $a$ ranging over $\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$,
$$
T_p=\inf_a\sum_{z\in P}m_z(1+a\cdot(z-p))_+,\qquad
E_p\ge T_p\ge D_p .
$$
Writing $b_N(L)=L^{-N}-(1-N(L-1))_+$ for $L>0$, one has
$$
E_p-T_p\ge\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z b_N(L_z(\alpha_p)),\qquad
E_p=T_p\ \Longleftrightarrow\ p=M_p^{-1}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z z .
$$
At equality $E_p=T_p=M_p$.

The escort masses $e_z=m_z L_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$ and zero off $P_p$ are dominated by the $m_z$ exactly when $\alpha_p=0$. The largest scalar $c\ge0$ with $c e_z\le m_z$ for all $z$ is $c=\min_{z\in P_p}L_z(\alpha_p)^{N+1}$. The resulting dominated row has total mass $cE_p$ and mean $p$. On the whole of $Q$, $E_p\le M$ with equality exactly at the original weighted base mean. If this mean is occupied and the compatible-fiber assumptions of the face-attainment result hold with $m_z=|K_z|$, its escort-selected continuous coordinate equals the original volume-weighted fiber centroid.

2be89ee8039bb5fd:05.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a convex body centrally symmetric about zero, $m\ge1$, and let $H>0$, $d=m+1$, and $B=H+1$. Put $K=\operatorname{conv}(D\times\{-1\},\{(0,H)\})$, with $d$-volume $V=B|D|/d$. For $a\in\mathbb R^m$, let $A=D\cap\{b:a\cdot b\le1\}$ and $N=(a,1)$. The section $K\cap\{(X,z):z+a\cdot X=0\}$ has parameterization
$$
X=\frac{Hb}{B-a\cdot b},\qquad z=-a\cdot X,\qquad b\in A.
$$
Its measure $d\mathcal H^m/\lVert N\rVert_2$ pulls back to $H^m B(B-a\cdot b)^{-d}\,db$. Write $C_a$ for this section measure divided by $V$, $p_a$ for the fraction of $K$ in the cap $z+a\cdot X\ge0$, and $C_0=dH^m/B^d$. Then
$$
C_a=\frac{dH^m}{|D|}\int_A(B-a\cdot b)^{-d}\,db,\qquad
p_a=\frac Hd C_a+1-\frac{|A|}{|D|}.
$$
The section has centroid zero if and only if $\int_A b(B-a\cdot b)^{-d-1}\,db=0$. In that case $\ell=-a/B$ minimizes the projective-energy integral on $A$ at zero, and $C_a/C_0=E_A(0)/|D|$.

2bf98ea275da010b:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}C_1$, $d\ge2$. Given unit $u$ and $b_\pm\ge0$, use the pair $\pm u\cdot x+b_\pm(z-1)\ge0$. Put $J=\{-b_-\le u\cdot x\le b_+\}$, $E=C_1\cap u^\perp$, $z(t)=-t/(1-t)$, $A_t=(1-t)C_{z(t)}$ and $D_t=A_t\cap J$. The closed version of the missed pair residual at $z(t)$ equals $D_t/(1-t)$ up to null boundaries. For $0\le s<t<1$ with $C_{z(t)}\ne\varnothing$, one has $A_t+(t-s)C_1\subseteq A_s$, $D_t+(t-s)E\subseteq D_s$, and the same latter inclusion on each nonempty $u$-coordinate slice. In particular $D_t\subseteq D_s$.

Put $p=d-1$, $a=t-s$, and $e=|E|_p^{1/p}$, where $|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-dimensional volume on $u^\perp$. If $D_t$ has positive $d$-volume $V$ and $u$-width $w$, put $A=(dV/w)^{1/p}$. Then
$$
|D_s|\ge w\,\frac{(A+ae)^{p+1}-(ae)^{p+1}}{(p+1)A}.
$$
If $D_t$ is nonempty with zero $d$-volume and positive width $w$, one has $|D_s|\ge a^p|E|_p w$. In dimension two the formula is $|D_s|-|D_t|\ge(t-s)|E|_1 w$, also valid for zero width or an empty remote residual. At integer sites $-j$, $j\ge1$, write $V_j$ and $w_j$ for the ordinary area and $u$-width of the unscaled closed residual, setting width zero for the empty set. Whenever the sections in question exist,
$$
(j+1)^2V_{j-1}-j^2V_j\ge j|E|_1w_j .
$$
The positive-volume bound is sharp in every $d\ge2$ even for actual adjacent globally deepest marks at $0$ and $1$, a genuine critical pair at $1$ and a genuine critical triple at $0$, with each integer fiber lighter than half the total.

$$
For every $\varepsilon\ge0$ the family $s_zK$ is compatible and preserves $M$ and each canonical budget $\gamma_dM$. A vertex acceleration gives second derivative $-\gamma_dH/2$ in every aggregate cap and $H/2$ in the total volume. For $d=1$ both fixed canonical cap budgets cannot be lowered while increasing total volume.

Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and let $C$ be the canonical convex hull of a finite compatible family of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ at bases $P$. Write $B=\operatorname{conv}P$, $V_z=|K_z|$, $M=\sum_{z\in P}V_z$, and $E(z,x)=E_{C_z}(x)$ for ordinary projective energy, extended by zero at the own-fiber boundary. In each fiber, a positive $C^1$ function satisfies $\nabla_x f=fa$ throughout its interior exactly when $f(z,x)=c(z)E(z,x)^{1/N}$ with $c(z)>0$ independent of $x$.

If $\ell$ is a positive continuous concave function on $B$, then $f_\ell=(\ell E/M)^{1/N}$ is jointly concave and continuous on $C$, vanishes at the own-fiber boundaries and satisfies this alignment. When $\ell$ is affine and $\sum_{z\in P}V_z\ell(z)=M$, its parameter domain is
$$
\ell(z)=1+b\cdot(z-\bar g)>0\text{ on }B,\qquad
\bar g=M^{-1}\sum_{z\in P}V_z z,\qquad b\in\operatorname{span}(B-B).
$$
The domain is bounded and its closure is the compact domain with $\ell\ge0$.

Write $F=E^{1/d}$. At a sampled own-interior mark $(p,y)$, let $L_F$ be a nonnegative affine upper tangent ratio, meaning $F(z,x)\le F(p,y)L_F(z,x)$ and $L_F(p,y)=1$. Such a ratio exists. If $\ell$ is positive affine, an affine upper tangent ratio for $f_\ell$ is
$$
L=\frac{d}{N}L_F+\frac1N\frac{\ell(z)}{\ell(p)}\ \ge\ \frac{\min_B\ell}{N\ell(p)}>0.

On the source fiber this is exactly $1+a(p,y)\cdot(x-y)$.

311680d006cf5fea:01.statement:
Let an actual planar convex body have positive integer interval fibers $I_i=[l_i,r_i]$ of widths $w_i>0$ at $i=0,\ldots,N-1$; other fibers have zero length or are empty. Put $M=\sum_i w_i$ and $R_*=\max_{j,y\in I_j}\sum_i|I_i\cap(2y-I_{2j-i})|$, with zero terms for missing or null fibers. For each $j$, let $K_j=\min(j,N-1-j)$, $N_j=2K_j+1$, $C_j=\sum_{0\le 2j-i<N}w_iw_{2j-i}$, and $\Delta_j=N_j w_j^2-C_j$. Then
$
(N_jw_j-R_*)_+^2\le N_j\Delta_j,\qquad
R_*\ge N_jw_j-\sqrt{N_j\Delta_j}>\frac{C_j}{2w_j}.
$
With $s_k=(w_{j-k}+w_{j+k})/2$ the defect decomposes as
$
\Delta_j=2\sum_{k=1}^{K_j}(w_j-s_k)(w_j+s_k)
+\tfrac12\sum_{k=1}^{K_j}(w_{j-k}-w_{j+k})^2.
$
In particular $R_*<M/2$ implies $\Delta_j\ge (N_jw_j-M/2)_+^2/N_j$, strictly when $N_jw_j>M/2$. 3121a9d11f167d7d:01.statement:
Let $\mu=\sum_z\mu_z$ be a finite positive measure supported on finitely many compact fibers, with $\mu_z$ lifted to its labeled base and of positive mass $w_z$. Write $g_z$ for its normalized fiber barycenter and $g$ for the global barycenter. On any oriented spanning tree of the labels let $G_e$ have incoming-minus-outgoing divergence $w_z(g_z-g)$. For $L(w)=a\cdot w$, write $\nu_z=L_\#\mu_z$, $m_z=a\cdot g_z$, $m=a\cdot g$, $F_e=a\cdot G_e$, and
$$
P_z(t)=\nu_z([t,\infty))/w_z,\qquad
\kappa_z(t)=\int_{[t,\infty)}(x-m_z)\,d\nu_z(x),\qquad
J(t)=\sum_e F_e(P_{\rm head}(t)-P_{\rm tail}(t)).
$$
Then $\kappa_z\ge0$ and $J(t)=\sum_z w_z(m_z-m)P_z(t)$ is independent of the tree. On a consecutive directed path through $z_1,\ldots,z_N$, $F_j=\sum_{i\le j}w_{z_i}(m-m_{z_i})$. For every real $t$, with the threshold atom included,
$$
\int_{L\ge t}(L-m)\,d\mu=\sum_z\kappa_z(t)+J(t).
$$
For every $C^1$ function $\phi$ on a neighborhood of the compact scalar support interval,
$$
\int(L-m)\phi(L)\,d\mu
=\int\sum_z\kappa_z(t)\phi'(t)\,dt+\sum_e F_e(\mathbb E_{\rm head}\phi(L)-\mathbb E_{\rm tail}\phi(L))
=\int[\sum_z\kappa_z(t)+J(t)]\phi'(t)\,dt.
$$
For any coupling $\pi_e$ of the normalized tail and head scalar laws, the edge expectation difference equals
$$
\int\int_0^1(x'-x)\phi'((1-r)x+rx')\,dr\,d\pi_e(x,x').
$$
In the distributional sense, $d\kappa_z=(m_z-t)d\nu_z$, $dJ=-\sum_z(m_z-m)d\nu_z$, and $d(\sum_z\kappa_z+J)=(m-t)d\sum_z\nu_z$.

For ordinary $d$-volume on full-dimensional convex fibers and continuous normal $u\ne0$ in $L(z,x)=v\cdot z+u\cdot x$, write $f_z(t)=\mathcal H_{d-1}(K_z\cap\{L(z,x)=t\})/|u|$, $f=\sum_z f_z$, and $R=\sum_z(m_z-m)f_z$. Almost everywhere, $P_z'=-f_z/w_z$, $(\sum_z\kappa_z)'=(m-t)f+R$, and $J'=-R$. On any open positive-density interval away from scalar fiber endpoints, $\tau=(\sum_z\kappa_z+J)/f$ obeys $(\tau f)'=(m-t)f$ almost everywhere.

For a finite menu of closed caps $H_j=\{a_j\cdot w\ge b_j\}$ and weights $\lambda_j\ge0$, use the same $G_e$ throughout. Let $P_{zj}=\mu_z(H_j)/w_z$ and $\kappa_{zj}=\int_{H_j}a_j\cdot(w-g_z)\,d\mu_z$. Then
$$
\sum_j\lambda_j\int_{H_j}a_j\cdot(w-g)\,d\mu
=\sum_{z,j}\lambda_j\kappa_{zj}
+\sum_eG_e\cdot\sum_j\lambda_j a_j(P_{{\rm head},j}-P_{{\rm tail},j}).
$$

316afa5f01281a91:01.statement:
Let $K_-,K_0,K_+\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(K_-+K_+)/2\subset K_0$. Let $n:U\subset\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb S^{d-1}$ be a $C^2$ injective immersion of rank $k$ on an open set, let $m=d-1-k$, and assume $h_i(t)=h_{K_i}(n(t))$ is $C^2$ for each body. Suppose the actual support faces at $n(t)$ have affine dimension $m$, and their relative interiors give regular boundary patches with the indicated unique normal and ordinary surface measure given by the area Jacobian of the one-to-one affine-face parametrizations below. Use common orthonormal frames $N(t)$ of $\operatorname{im}Dn(t)$ and $E(t)$ of $L(t)=\ker n(t)^{\mathsf T}\cap\ker Dn(t)^{\mathsf T}$ locally. For the canonical perpendicular origins $a_i(t)$ of the affine face hulls and points $X_i(t,s)=a_i(t)+E(t)s$ on those faces, put $R=N^{\mathsf T}Dn$ and $Q_i(t,s)=D^2h_i(t)-\sum_j X_{i,j}(t,s)D^2 n_j(t)$. For $k>0$, the $Q_i$ are positive semidefinite and the actual marked surface densities relative to the common $dt\,ds$ are $J_i=\det Q_i/|\det R|$.

Write $Z=\{t:h_0(t)=(h_-(t)+h_+(t))/2\}$. At Lebesgue-almost every $t\in Z$, and at every point of an open tight chart, $a_0=(a_-+a_+)/2$. For every endpoint face pair at such a parameter, its physical midpoint is $X_0(t,s_0)$ with $s_0=(s_-+s_+)/2$, and $Q_0(t,s_0)=(Q_-(t,s_-)+Q_+(t,s_+))/2$. For $k>0$ this gives
$$
J_0(t,s_0)^{1/k}\ge \frac{J_-(t,s_-)^{1/k}+J_+(t,s_+)^{1/k}}2.
$$
If $m>0$, in particular $J_0(t,s_0)\ge ((J_-(t,s_-)^{-1/m}+J_+(t,s_+)^{-1/m})/2)^{-m}$, with zero on the right if either input is zero. For $m=0$ the conditional densities are singleton masses and $J_0\ge\min(J_-,J_+)$. For $k=0$ the fixed normal has unit Euclidean facet density, including unit endpoint counting mass when $d=1$.

Let $\ell$ have width one on $B$ and let $p$ be the scalar section-volume density of $\ell_\#\nu$, extended by zero off its support. Then $0\le p\le D$. $$
\nu\{x:t_*-a\le\ell(x)\le t_*\}\ge\alpha a/D\qquad (0\le a\le L).
$$
In particular, if $c\in B$ and $\ell(c_*-c)\ge0$, the cap $\{x:\ell(x-c)\ge0\}$ has mass at least $\alpha+(\alpha/D)\ell(c_*-c)$.

$$
\min\left\{\sum_{i>h}w_i,\ \sum_{i<-h}w_i\right\}
\ge\kappa_d\bigl[M-(2h+1)m\bigr].
$$
The constants satisfy $1/5<\kappa_d\le9/31<3/10$, with $\kappa_1=9/31$ and $\lim_{d\to\infty}\kappa_d=1/5$.

Let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume $M$ whose mixed-volume centroid has integer base coordinate $j$. Write $w_i=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_i)$ and $m=\max_{i\in\mathbb Z} w_i$. Take an outward vector $w$ with $|\det(P_j-P_i,w)|=1$. In the coordinates $P(t)+rw$, the first variation under an outward piecewise-affine roof $r=\varepsilon h(t)$ with $h(0)=h(1)=0$ is $D\Psi[h]=\int h\,d\nu$. The density of $\nu$ is $\alpha_i,\beta_s,\alpha_j$ on $(0,a),(a,b),(b,1)$, respectively. With $C=8+\prod_i f_i$, $E_\ell=2f_\ell^2+\prod_i f_i$ and $T_\ell=\sqrt{k/Q_\ell}$,
$$
2k\alpha_\ell=C+E_\ell T_\ell^2-Cf_\ell T_\ell,\qquad
\beta_s=\alpha_i+\alpha_j-\frac C{2k}.
$$
At either crossing $t_0$ of cap $\ell$, there is an atom of weight $(\partial_{\sigma_\ell}\Psi)/|v_\ell\cdot(P_j-P_i)|$, where $\partial_{\sigma_\ell}\Psi=-E_\ell/\sigma_\ell+C Q_\ell/(\sigma_\ell^2 M)$. The moments $\int(1-t)d\nu$ and $\int t\,d\nu$ both vanish.

Put $U(\theta)=\int[\min(t,\theta)-t\theta]\,d\nu(t)$. The unit-height triangular roof with peak $\theta\in(0,1)$ has derivative $U(\theta)/[\theta(1-\theta)]$, where
$$
U(\theta)=-\alpha_i\theta^2/2\quad(0\le\theta\le a),\qquad
U(\theta)=-\alpha_j(1-\theta)^2/2\quad(b\le\theta\le1).
$$
For $\theta=a+z(b-a)$ with $0\le z\le1$,
$$
2U(\theta)=-(1-z)\alpha_i a^2-z\alpha_j(1-b)^2+\beta_s(b-a)^2z(1-z).
$$
Both $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_j$ are positive. The derivative is nonpositive at every peak exactly when
$$
\beta_s(b-a)^2\le \bigl(a\sqrt{\alpha_i}+(1-b)\sqrt{\alpha_j}\bigr)^2.
$$

$$
\mu(T)\ge\left(\sum_i M_i/a_i-k+1\right)
\left(\sum_i\lambda_i a_i^{1/d}\right)^d.
$$
For two inputs the first factor is at least $\max(M_1/a_1,M_2/a_2)$. If all weighted combinations of nonempty input bases are integral, then also for possibly zero input masses,

The peak bound is attained for equal weights on arithmetic progressions of step $k$ on an integer line, with identical fibers within each input and homothetic convex fibers across inputs.

For $d=0$ and nonempty finite input sets with integral weighted combinations, $|T|\ge\sum_i|A_i|-k+1$ for positive weights. In particular $|T|\ge\max(|A_1|,|A_2|)$ for two inputs. For every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(j,y_j)$ there are $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $w\in\Delta$ such that
$$
\left|r_pT_d\cap\{X:a\cdot(p-j)+w\cdot X\ge q\}\right|
\le \left|\{X\in r_pT_d:(p,X)\in H\}\right|
\qquad(p\in P).
$$
In particular the infimum $h_\mu(j,y_j)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces containing $(j,y_j)$ equals
$$
\min_{a\in\mathbb R^n,\ w\in\Delta}
\sum_{p\in P}\left|r_pT_d\cap\{X:a\cdot(p-j)+w\cdot X\ge q\}\right|.
$$
The same formula holds when the tilt is restricted to the compact set of the bounded shared tilt lemma. The touching-majorant hypothesis holds if the displayed simplices are the actual fibers of one convex set at the bases in $P$.

Define
$$
C_j=\max_{p\in P}\max\{q,|q-r_p|\},
\qquad B_j^{(m)}=C_j\max_I\lVert V_I^{-1}\rVert_\infty,
$$
where the matrix norm is the maximum absolute row sum.

$$

=\left|r_pT_d\cap\{X:a\cdot(p-j)+w\cdot X\ge q\}\right|,
$$
where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-volume. If $n=1$, clipping $a$ to $[-B_j,B_j]$ suffices with $B_j=0$ for $P=\{j\}$ and otherwise

B_j=\max_{p\in P\setminus\{j\}}\frac{\max\{q,|q-r_p|\}}{|p-j|}.

42db79d64fa93f5f:01.statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, centrally symmetric about $g$, with volume $V$. If $X$ is uniform on $K$ and $Z$ is independent of $X$ with $Z$ and $-Z$ identically distributed, then the normalized halfspace depth of $X+Z$ at each $y$ is at least $f_K(y)/V$.

4338d43b80b00575:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope and $u$ a unit vector. Then $F(T)=|K\cap\{u\cdot X\ge T\}|$ is continuous and polynomial of degree at most $d$ between consecutive vertex heights in direction $u$, and constant outside their range. Write $f^\pm$ and $h^\pm$ for its one-sided first and second derivatives at a given $T$. For $t\downarrow0$,
$$
F(T+tq+t^2 r/2)=F(T)+tD(q)+t^2 E(q,r)/2+o(t^2),
$$
where $D(0)=0$, $D(q)=f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q$ if $q\ne0$, $E(0,r)=D(r)$, and $E(q,r)=h^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q^2+f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}r$ if $q\ne0$. At an inside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=-S\max(q,0)$. At an outside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=S\max(-q,0)$. At a proper cut the two first derivatives agree and equal minus the section area.

4338d43b80b00575:02.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite real base and $K_p$ positive compatible $d$-polytopes. Write $V_p=|K_p|$, $M=\sum_pV_p$, and $\beta$ for their maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth. Translate the origin into the relative interior of the base hull. At each deepest base $p_i$ take a positive critical circuit of closed caps
$$
a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot X\ge b_{ij},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad b_{ij}=a_{ij}\cdot p_i+u_{ij}\cdot x_i
$$
of old mass $\beta M$, with weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. Use fixed strictly cheaper whole-plane covers at the other bases. For affine $A,B$ set $L_t=1+tA+t^2B/2$. In each critical cap vary the base covector and threshold by
$$
a_{ij}(t)=a_{ij}+tc_{ij}+t^2e_{ij}/2,\qquad
b_{ij}(t)=b_{ij}+t(c_{ij}\cdot p_i+s_{ij})+t^2(e_{ij}\cdot p_i+r_{ij})/2 .
$$
Put $q_{ijp}=s_{ij}-c_{ij}\cdot(p-p_i)$ and $R_{ijp}=r_{ij}-e_{ij}\cdot(p-p_i)$. Let $F^0_{ijp}$ denote the old cap volume in $K_p$ and $D_{ijp},E_{ijp}$ its one-sided parallel cap coefficient functions at the old threshold. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
b_{ij,1}&=\sum_p\left[D_{ijp}(q_{ijp})-dA(p)(F^0_{ijp}-\beta V_p)\right],\\
b_{ij,2}&=\sum_p\left[E_{ijp}(q_{ijp},R_{ijp})-2dA(p)D_{ijp}(q_{ijp})+
(d(d+1)A(p)^2-dB(p))(F^0_{ijp}-\beta V_p)\right].
\end{aligned}
$$
Suppose $\sum_j\rho_{ij}s_{ij}\le0$ for every group, with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}r_{ij}\le0$ whenever the first sum is zero. Suppose also $b_{ij,1}\le0$ for every critical cap, with $b_{ij,2}<0$ whenever $b_{ij,1}=0$. Then for every sufficiently small positive $t$, the actual projective image under $(p,X)\mapsto(p/L_t(p),X/L_t(p))$ has maximum normalized depth strictly less than $\beta$. At a local positive affine projective minimum these jets are therefore infeasible for every choice of old circuits. For each fixed first jet the second-order feasibility is a finite union of linear systems with weak and strict inequalities, branched on the signs of $R_{ijp}$ where $q_{ijp}=0$.

Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities. For a compact convex nonempty set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ write $J(Q)=\max\{(\det A)^{1/d}:c+AB_d\subset Q,\ A\succeq0\}$, with $B_d$ the closed Euclidean unit ball and $A$ symmetric.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

The positive-mass feasible integer bases are exactly $\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$. For each of them the maximum of $J(Q_t(j))$ over $[0,T_j]$ is positive and attained at a unique $t>0$. The set $E$ of bases reaching the joint maximum satisfies
$$
E=\operatorname{vert}(\operatorname{conv}E)=\operatorname{conv}E\cap\mathbb Z^n,\qquad |E|\le2^n.
$$
The cardinality bound is attained by $[0,1]^n\times K$ with $K$ a positive-volume convex body.

For $j\in P$, every feasible density of mass $T_j$ and mean base $j$ fills $K_j$ almost everywhere. If $0<\varepsilon<|K_j|$ and $Z_\varepsilon=\{\int_{K_j}xg(x)\,dx:0\le g\le1,\ \int_{K_j}g\,dx=\varepsilon\}$, then $Q_{T_j-\varepsilon}(j)\supseteq Q_{T_j}(j)-Z_\varepsilon$, where subtraction means addition of the reflected set. In particular the maximizing mass is less than $T_j$ at these bases. When the $K_z$ are all positive integer fibers of one compact convex body, every positive-mass feasible integer base belongs to $P$ and hence has interior maximizing mass.

Writing $M=\mu(\mathbb R^{n+d})$ and $(g_z,g_x)=M^{-1}\int(z,x)\,d\mu$, one has $Q(M-t,Mg_z-v)=Mg_x-Q(t,v)$. The unique maximum over all feasible real constraint pairs is at $(M/2,Mg_z/2)$. If $g_z$ is integral, the integer program has the unique optimal base and mass $(g_z,M/2)$, with the center of every optimal ellipsoid equal to $(M/2)g_x$.

Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and let $\ell,u$ be real functions on a compact interval with $\ell$ convex, $u$ concave, and $\ell\le u$. Assume
$$
C=\{(z,x):z\text{ is in the interval},\ x_1\ge\ell(z),\ x_j\ge0\ (2\le j\le d),\ \textstyle\sum_j x_j\le u(z)\}
$$
is a compact convex body with positive mixed volume. Let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d)$ and let $\mu$ be the sum of $d$-dimensional volume on its integer fibers. On the $N$ positive-volume integer fibers write $r_i=u(i)-\ell(i)$, $m=\max_i r_i$, $M=\sum_i r_i^d$ and $Q=\sum_i r_i^{d+1}$. Let $H=\{x_1+az\ge b\}$ have boundary through the true centroid of $\mu$ and suppose $\ell(i)+ai-b\le0$ on each positive-volume fiber. With $U_i=u(i)+ai-b$, $v_+=\max\{v,0\}$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, the captured fraction satisfies
$$
\frac{\mu(H)}{\mu(S)}=\frac{\sum_i(U_i)_+^d}{M}
\ge\Gamma_d\frac{Q}{mM}
\ge\Gamma_d\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}+\frac{m^d}{(d+2)NM}\right)
>\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}.
$$
The centroid's base coordinate need not be an integer. Lower-endpoint equality $\ell(i)+ai-b=0$ is allowed.

45dc817a19bd7f21:01.statement:
In a nondegenerate tetrahedron orient a strict quadrilateral cut toward vertices $0,1$. Its diagonal point has homogeneous coordinates $(x,y,z,w)>0$. Write $S=x+y+z+w$, $P=x+y$, $R=z+w$, $a=xy$, $b=zw$, $k=a-b$, and $D=k^2+S(aR+bP)$. Set
$$
(D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3)=((x+z)(x+w),(y+z)(y+w),(x+z)(y+z),(x+w)(y+w))
$$
and
$$
(N_0,N_1,N_2,N_3)
=(x[S(2x+R)-D_0],y[S(2y+R)-D_1],z[S(P+2z)-D_2],w[S(P+2w)-D_3]).
$$
The section centroid has coordinates $\lambda_i=N_i/(3SD_i)>0$. Centrality, meaning every $\lambda_i\le1/3$, is equivalent to nonnegativity of $bS-kx,bS-ky,aS+kz,aS+kw$. After sorting $x\le y,z\le w$, the possible middle pairs of $\lambda$ are $\{0,1\},\{2,3\},\{1,2\},\{0,3\}$, allowing ties and breaking tied positions consistently with the within-pair orders. For a selected middle pair $\{j,k'\}$ put $B_{jk'}=12N_jN_{k'}-3S(D_jN_{k'}+D_{k'}N_j)$ and $c=4N_jN_{k'}/B_{jk'}$. On the central domain $B_{jk'}>0$. Let $F$ be the cap volume fraction and let $s$ be the section area divided by the tetrahedral volume times the projection of the ordinary centroid minus the section centroid onto the oriented unit normal. Then $27/64\le F-cs\le37/64$ is equivalent to the two homogeneous degree-ten expressions
$$
(64b(PS-a+b)-27D)B_{jk'}-192S(bP-aR)N_jN_{k'}\ge0,
$$
$$
(37D-64b(PS-a+b))B_{jk'}+192S(bP-aR)N_jN_{k'}\ge0.
$$
The order constraints can be imposed by comparing $N_iD_l$ with $N_lD_i$. In particular the negative pair $\{2,3\}$ is a middle pair in the chosen within-pair order exactly when $N_2(x+w)\ge N_0(y+z)$ and $N_1(x+w)\ge N_3(y+z)$.

Under the normalization $S=1$, the aggregate domain is exactly $0<P<1$, $0<a\le P^2/4$, $0<b\le R^2/4$. Define
$$
U=P(b+k^2)-2k(a+b),\quad V=b^2-bkP+k^2a,\quad
W=R(a+k^2)+2k(a+b),\quad Z=a^2+akR+k^2b.
$$
Centrality is equivalent to $2b-kP\ge0$, $V\ge0$, $2a+kR\ge0$, $Z\ge0$. Within this domain, the unordered negative pair is a middle pair exactly when
$$
(W-U)W+2(V-Z)D\le0,\qquad
(W-U)^2Z+(W-U)(V-Z)W+(V-Z)^2D\ge0.
$$
These conditions include all tied orderings. When that pair is selected, put $N=D-W+Z$ and $B=2D-3W+4Z$. Then $B>0$, $c=(4/3)N/B$ and
$$
F-cs=\frac{b(P-a+b)B-N(bP-aR)}{DB}.
$$
The positive within-pair case follows by reversing the split. These equivalences express the correction condition as polynomial signs on an exact domain.

499bc56f5e8f111d:03.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A,B,C$ be compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, with $B,C$ simplices, $|B|=|C|=V>0$, $|A|=a>0$ and $(A+C)/2\subset B$. Let $N=d+1$, $b=1/N$, $J=\lceil N/2\rceil$, $R=2\sqrt d$, $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$, and
$$
\delta=N^{-N/[2(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1)]}-b.
$$
Use the barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ of the standard simplex, and write
$$
c_i=|\{p\in A:\lambda_i(p)+\max_C\lambda_i\ge2b+\delta\}|,\qquad
\bar c=\frac1N\sum_i c_i.
$$
Here all volumes in the formulas use the normalized frame. Define $y$ by $\lambda_i(y)=b+(c_i-\bar c)/(N\Gamma V)$. With $g$ the centroid of $B$ and $\theta_i=\nabla\lambda_i/|\nabla\lambda_i|$, put
$$
\begin{gathered}
\eta=\min\{\delta/(24R\sqrt d),\,1/(8N\sqrt d)\},\qquad
G_d=\min_{\substack{|u|=1\\\min_i|u-\theta_i|\ge\eta}}
 \left(\frac{|B\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|}{V}-\Gamma\right),\\
E_d=2^d-d-1,\qquad k_d=J/N-\Gamma/2,\qquad
Q_d=d!\omega_{d-1}\sqrt d/(N\Gamma)+\Gamma/2,
\end{gathered}
$$
where $\omega_{d-1}$ is the unit $(d-1)$-ball volume. Then $G_d>0$ and
$$
0<a/V\le\min\{(\delta/8)^d,\,N\Gamma\delta/8,\,\Gamma/(4d),\,
                     \Gamma k_d/(2E_d),\,G_d/(2Q_d)\}
$$
implies $y\in\operatorname{int} B$ and raw depth at $(0,y)$ at least $\Gamma(V+a/2)$ over every closed ambient halfspace containing that point. The bound scales back to the original frame.

49e262af8d182671:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define
$$
E_K(y)=\min_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^d\\1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}}
\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx,\qquad
T_K(y)=\max_{\substack{0\le f\le1\\\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0}}\int_Kf(x)\,dx,
$$
where $f$ is Lebesgue measurable. Both extrema are attained, and the energy minimizer is unique. The maximizing density for $T_K(y)$ is the indicator, up to null sets, of a unique convex cap of centroid $y$. The cap is all of $K$ at its centroid. In particular $T_K(y)$ is the greatest volume of a convex subbody of $K$ with centroid $y$.

For every such $(K,y)$,
$$
0<T_K(y)\le E_K(y)<(d+1)T_K(y).
$$
Equality $T_K(y)=E_K(y)$ holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid of $K$. For each fixed $d\ge1$, the supremum of $E_K(y)/T_K(y)$ over these pairs is $d+1$, and no pair attains it. More precisely, if $K=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $y=(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1/(d+1)$, then
$$
\frac{E_K(y)}{T_K(y)}=(d+1)(1-d\varepsilon).
$$
For an arbitrary simplex of volume $V$ and an interior mark with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, $E_K(y)=V(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. In dimension one, for $K-y=[-\ell,r]$ with $\ell,r>0$, $T_K(y)=2\min(\ell,r)$ and $E_K(y)=4\ell r/(\ell+r)$.

Let $V=|K|$, $Q_t=\{z:(z,t)\in K\}$, and let $S(t),M_1(t),M_2(t)$ be the integrals of $1,z,zz^\mathsf T$ on $Q_t$. For $F(h,b)=|K\cap\{t+h\cdot z\ge b\}|/V$, the gradient and Hessian at $(h,b)=(0,0)$ are
$$
\nabla F(0,0)=\frac1V\binom{M_1(0)}{-S(0)},\qquad
\nabla^2F(0,0)=\frac1V
\begin{pmatrix}
-M_2'(0)&M_1'(0)\\
M_1'(0)^\mathsf T&-S'(0)
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The direction $(0,1)$ is stationary for the spherical through-origin cap fraction $p$ exactly when $Q_0$ has centroid $0$. At such a direction, the spherical Hessian in horizontal tangent coordinates is
$$
-\frac1V M_2'(0)
=\frac1V\int_{\partial Q_0}zz^\mathsf T\,\frac{N_t}{\lVert N_z\rVert}\,d\mathcal H^{k-1}(z).
$$

The three intervals are compatible exactly when U≥(a+b)/2 and |s|≤U/2−(a+b)/4. When compatible, their lifted convex hull is full dimensional and realizes exactly these three integer fibers.

5048c7e97ca98aef:02.reason: The exact profile, tie locus, and contact formula account for all containing closed halfspaces and all three fibers.
5048c7e97ca98aef:02.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a convex body whose only nonempty integer fibers are positive-length intervals at three consecutive bases. After an integer base translation, a possible base reflection, and a shear affine in the base, its fibers at $-1,0,1$ have the form
$$
K_-=[-a/2,a/2],\qquad K_0=[s-U/2,s+U/2],\qquad K_+=[-b/2,b/2],
$$
where $0<a\le b$ and $U>0$. These parameters are realizable exactly when $U\ge(a+b)/2$ and $|s|\le U/2-(a+b)/4$.

Write $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$ and $W=a+b+U$. For $y\in S$, let $h_S(y)$ be the infimum of the total fiber length captured by closed ambient halfspaces containing $y$. Thus $h_S$ is raw depth, and $h_S/W$ is normalized depth. With $g(x)=\min\{a,\max\{0,(a+b)/2-2x\}\}$, for every $x\in K_0$,
$$
h_S((0,x))=\min\{U/2+s-x+g(x),\ U/2-s+x+g(-x)\}.
$$
Set $\sigma=|s|$, $\alpha=(b-a)/4$, and $\beta=(b+3a)/4$. There is a unique maximizer on the middle fiber, $(0,x_*)$, with $x_*=0$ if $s=0$ and with the sign of $s$ otherwise. Its absolute coordinate and its raw depth $F$ are
$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{range}& |x_*|&F\\ \hline
0\le \sigma\le \alpha&\sigma&U/2+a\\
\alpha\le\sigma\le\beta&\sigma/2+(b-a)/8&U/2-\sigma/2+(b+7a)/8\\
\sigma\ge\beta&\sigma-a/2&(U+a)/2
\end{array}
$$
The formulas agree at their shared endpoints. On either endpoint fiber of length $c\in\{a,b\}$, the raw depth at height $x$ is $c/2-|x|$.

The global raw maximum is $Q=\max\{b/2,F\}$, and its normalized value is $Q/W$. The complete set of deepest points consists of $(0,x_*)$ when $U>b-2a$, of $(1,0)$ when $U<b-2a$, and of both when $U=b-2a$. Equality $U=b-2a$ is compatible precisely when $a\le b/5$ and $s$ obeys the compatibility condition above. In particular if $a=b$, the middle point is the unique deepest point.

For fixed $a,b,U$, $F$ and $Q/W$ are nonincreasing in $|s|$ on its feasible interval. At the largest compatible shift $|s|=U/2-(a+b)/4$ the middle raw maximum is
$$
F_{\mathrm{contact}}(a,b,U)=
\begin{cases}
U/2+a,&(a+b)/2\le U\le b,\\
(U+b)/4+a,&b\le U\le b+2a,\\
(U+a)/2,&U\ge b+2a.
\end{cases}
$$

5048c7e97ca98aef:03.reason: The normalized fixed-ratio optimization includes every minimizing shift and both middle lengths at the seam r=1/3.
5048c7e97ca98aef:03.statement:
Fix an endpoint ratio $r=a/b\in(0,1]$ in the three-positive-interval model of the preceding exact depth formula. Among all convex bodies with only these three nonempty integer fibers and with this endpoint ratio, the minimum of the normalized global maximum depth $Q/(a+b+U)$ is
$$
B(r)=
\begin{cases}
1/(4-2r),&0<r\le1/5,\\
(1+5r)/(6(1+r)),&1/5\le r\le1/3,\\
(1+3r)/(4+6r),&1/3\le r\le1 .
\end{cases}
$$
In the normalized coordinates with endpoint lengths $a\le b$, the complete set of minimizing middle parameters is as follows.
- For $0<r<1/5$, take $U=b-2a$ and any compatible $s$.
- For $1/5\le r<1/3$, take $U=(a+b)/2$ and $s=0$.
- For $r=1/3$, take either $U=(a+b)/2$ and $s=0$ or $U=b+2a$ and $|s|=U/2-(a+b)/4$.
- For $1/3<r\le1$, take $U=b+2a$ and $|s|=U/2-(a+b)/4$.

The function $B$ is continuous and strictly increasing, satisfies $B(r)>1/4$ for $r>0$, has limit $1/4$ as $r\downarrow0$, and has $B(1)=2/5$. Thus the unrestricted infimum within this three-positive-interval model is $1/4$, approached as the ratio tends to zero.

5059cb158ac8db8a:02.statement:
Take positive planar triangles $K_0,K_1,K_2$ at bases $0,1,2$ with $(K_0+K_2)/2\subseteq K_1$. Assume a nonnegative joint affine cap/body stress of the following form. The middle caps have fixed traces $\xi_i\ge\alpha_i$ on $K_1$, where $\xi_i$ are its barycentrics and the $\alpha_i>0$ sum to one. At most one endpoint $e$ carries an isolated canonical centroid circuit, with multiplier sum $L_e$ (zero when absent), whose caps are strictly empty on the other fibers. Its own proper section coareas $S_j$ and positive normal-balance weights $\rho_j$ satisfy $\lambda_jS_j=t_e\rho_j$ for a common $t_e\ge0$. All other cap multipliers vanish.

There is exactly one positively stressed compatibility facet, the middle edge opposite vertex 3, of length $\ell$, outward unit normal $n$ and multiplier $\eta>0$. Its endpoint contact means $m_0,m_2$ lie in the endpoint support faces in direction $n$, with middle contact mean $m=(m_0+m_2)/2$ on that middle edge. For independent affine fields $V_z$ on the three triangles the stipulated body identity is
$$
\delta M=\sum_j\lambda_j\delta C_j-
\eta\,[2 n\cdot V_1(m)-n\cdot V_0(m_0)-n\cdot V_2(m_2)] .
$$
Here $\delta C_j$ uses the ordinary captured boundary trace in proper positions and an effective subdensity in $[0,1]$ at a coincident supporting edge.

Put $\sigma=2\eta/\ell$. Then $m$ is the midpoint of the middle edge. For some $0<p<1/3$, $\alpha=(p,p,1-2p)$, $\sigma=(1-3p)/(1-p)$, and the middle multipliers satisfy
$$
\lambda_1=\lambda_2=\frac{1-2p}{(1-p)^2},\qquad
\lambda_3=\frac{1}{2(1-p)},\qquad L_1=\sum_{i=1}^3\lambda_i=\frac{5-9p}{2(1-p)^2}.
$$
If both endpoint support faces in direction $n$ are edges, then, with $\gamma=4/9$, $\gamma L_e\le1-2\sigma$ and $\gamma(L_1+L_e)<2$. If in addition the stress is normalized by $L_1+L_e=1/\beta$ for $\beta>0$, then $\beta>2/9$.

$$

have mass $\beta M$, pass through the same interior deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$, and have weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base assume there is a fixed finite cover of the entire fiber plane by caps of mass strictly below $\beta M$. $$
S_{ijp}=-F'_{ijp},\quad R_{ijp}=-F''_{ijp},\quad S_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}>0,\qquad
\kappa_{ij}=\frac{\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}}{\sum_l \rho_{il}/S_{il}}.
$$
Put $H^*_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $V_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $h_{ij}=\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}$, and $k_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}$. $$

g_i(A)=t_i(A)+d\beta\int A\,d\mu,

$$

\qquad
\Pr(Y\ge t)\ge\left[1-\frac{dt}{(d+1)\mu}\right]_+\qquad(t\ge0).

568f7cf028ec23b6:03.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A,K,B$ be compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interiors at the only sampled bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use summed $d$-volume. Suppose $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and the cap $u\cdot(x-y)+\alpha z\ge0$, $u\ne0$, locally minimizes capture under all small normal changes through $(0,y)$. Suppose its $A$ capture is proper and its $B$ capture has volume zero. Write $E_A,E_K$ for the proper sections, $t,s>0$ for their $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ areas, $c_A,c_K$ for their centroids, and $F$ for the possibly empty section on $B$. For every $w\in\mathbb R^d,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
$$
t[w\cdot(c_A-y)-\beta]+s\,w\cdot(c_K-y)+\int_F[w\cdot(x-y)+\beta]_+\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)\ge0.
$$
Consequently $F$ is a positive-area supporting facet, $M=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)\ge t$, and
$$
s^{1/(d-1)}\ge\frac{t^{1/(d-1)}+M^{1/(d-1)}}2\ge t^{1/(d-1)}.
$$

56a670ccbde263ec:01.statement:
Let $C$ be a full-dimensional $(n+d)$-simplex in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$. Choose $n+1$ vertices with affinely independent base projections and let $Q$ be their projected $n$-simplex. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ be the other projected vertices and $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ their barycentric coordinates. The map to $(z,x)$ fixes the base $z$ and is an affine bijection taking $C$ to
$$
\mathcal C=\{(z,x):x\in T_d,\ z\in\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\},\qquad S=\sum_jx_j,\quad T_d=\{x\ge0:S\le1\}.
$$
The image volume is $n!|Q|/(n+d)!$ and the absolute continuous-coordinate Jacobian is $J=n!|Q|/((n+d)!|C|)$. It multiplies full $d$-volume on each integer fiber and every mixed closed cap mass by $J$. For positive mixed total mass, it transports normalized depth and the mixed centroid. The continuous projection of raw mixed measure in these new coordinates has density
$$
N(x)=\left|\mathbb Z^n\cap\left(\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\right)\right|\qquad(x\in T_d)
$$
and zero outside $T_d$. For $n=1$ choose the extreme projected vertices $a<b$. The interval has endpoints $\ell(x)=a+\sum_j(h_j-a)x_j$, $u(x)=b+\sum_j(h_j-b)x_j$, with width $(b-a)(1-S)$. Its count is $\max(0,\lfloor u(x)\rfloor-\lceil\ell(x)\rceil+1)$. For $n=0$ use $|Q|_0=1$ and $N=1$ on $T_d$.

The divided difference is in $t$, with confluent values at repeated knots and the continuous slice limit at interior knots. For distinct heights the divided difference equals $\sum_i(h_i-s)_+^{m-1}/\prod_{j\ne i}(h_i-h_j)$. Off the height interval $w=0$. At each extreme height use the inward limit, which equals the actual closed endpoint volume and is positive precisely when $m$ vertices have that height. Also $\int_{\mathbb R}w(s)\,ds=V$.

Let $f_{h^{(i)}}$ be the scalar height density under uniform barycentrics with this duplicated list, with continuous values in the interior, zero outside, and inward values at the endpoints. Then the actual section moments satisfy
$$
J_i(s):=\int_{C_s}\lambda_i(s,x)\,dx
 =\frac{V}{N} f_{h^{(i)}}(s)
 =V[h_0,\ldots,h_{N-1},h_i](t-s)_+^m.

571b5ceb2d4e114a:03.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge3$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$. For each $p\in P$ let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let $E_q$ be the polytope of nonnegative coefficient vectors $(\lambda_p)_{p\ne q}$ with $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1$ and $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q$. The family is strictly compatible if for every $q\in P$ and every extreme point $\lambda$ of $E_q$, the Minkowski sum $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. An empty $E_q$ imposes no condition. Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ and assume its actual integer fibers are the given $K_p$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on those fibers, $M$ its total mass, $\beta$ the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth over the measured points, and $I$ the bases where this maximum is attained. Assume that $C$ is a local minimum of $\beta$ among all actual positive fiber families on this fixed $P$, in the fiberwise Hausdorff topology.

For each $p\in I$ fix a finite positive circuit of actual critical caps $H_{pj}=\{(z,x):a_{pj}\cdot z+u_{pj}\cdot x\ge b_{pj}\}$, with $\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1$, $\rho_{pj}>0$, and $\sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0$. Each circuit passes through an interior maximizing mark of its own fiber and its caps have raw mass $Q=\beta M$. Assume each old aggregate threshold mass is $Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ when its threshold is moved by $s\to0$ from either side, with $S_{pj}>0$. Write $\kappa_{pj}=(\rho_{pj}/S_{pj})/\sum_\ell(\rho_{p\ell}/S_{p\ell})$. Let a finite collection of nonempty relatively open boundary patches $U$ be given, each in some $\partial K_q$, with $U$ a $C^1$ hypersurface containing no nontrivial line segment.

There exists one probability vector $\pi$ on $I$ such that on every patch in the collection, at each point $x$ off all restricted cap planes, $\sum_{p\in I,j}\pi_p\kappa_{pj}\mathbf1_{H_{pj}}(q,x)=\beta$. For every listed unoriented restricted plane $L$ that meets the patch and intersects $\operatorname{int}K_q$, the total weight $\pi_p\kappa_{pj}$ of the restricted caps with plane $L$ is the same in either orientation.

If a patch in fiber $q$ is the whole boundary, let $F_q$ be the total stress weight of nonproper cap restrictions that contain the whole boundary off the planes, and $P_q$ the total stress weight of properly cutting restricted caps. Then $\beta=F_q+P_q/2$. For such a fiber with $q\in I$ one has $\pi_q\le2\beta$. If the collection includes the entire boundary of every deepest fiber, then $\beta\ge 1/(2|I|)$. The two-sided positive slope hypothesis holds automatically if every $K_p$ is strictly convex.

57984994edf4161f:03.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body of volume $V$, with ordinary deepest point $g$ and maximum raw ordinary depth $q$. Take compact convex bodies $A,C\subset K\cap(2g-K)$ of equal volume $a>0$, and take the hull of $A,K,K,C$ over the respective bases $0,1,2,3$. These are the exact sampled fibers. The only globally deepest mixed points are $(1,g),(2,g)$, the global raw maximum is $Q=q+a$, and $M=2(V+a)$.

There are finite positive ordinary critical circuits at $g$ with at most $d+1$ inward unit normals $u_j$, all through-$g$ cap masses $q$, and positive coefficients balancing the normals. For any such circuit, take a common sufficiently large $L>0$. The caps $u_j\cdot(x-g)-L(z-1)\ge0$ at the first middle fiber and $u_j\cdot(x-g)+L(z-2)\ge0$ at the second form regular globally critical menus. Each cap strictly contains its paying endpoint ($A$ or $C$), cuts its own middle fiber by the ordinary cap, and strictly misses the other two fibers. Their sole proper sections have full mixed centroid at the respective marked point. The respective menus cover all planes at $z\le1$ and $z\ge2$.

If $2g-A,2g-C\subset\operatorname{int}K$, every critical halfspace through $(1,g)$ strictly contains $A$ at $0$, and every critical halfspace through $(2,g)$ strictly contains $C$ at $3$.

57984994edf4161f:04.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body with volume $V$, ordinary deepest mark $g$ and raw ordinary maximum $q$. Place two copies of $K$ at bases $1,2$ and compact convex bodies $A,C\subset K\cap(2g-K)$ of equal volume $a>0$ at bases $0,3$. Use the two critical menus obtained by extending a positive balanced ordinary critical circuit at $g$ by common sufficiently large negative base tilt about $1$ and positive base tilt about $2$, respectively, with any probability weights in each. For arbitrary interior points $c_A,c_C$ of the endpoint bodies, one nonnegative jointly continuous field convex in the full physical coordinates at each unit normal pays efficiency exactly $1/2$ against both old boundary profiles. Its convex support cuts yield, for every $\epsilon\ge0$, endpoint homothets of ratio $(1+\epsilon)^{-1}$ about $c_A,c_C$, with both middle fibers fixed. Put $a_\epsilon=a/(1+\epsilon)^d$. The actual normalized maximum is $(q+a_\epsilon)/(2(V+a_\epsilon))$, strictly decreases, and has right derivative $-da(V-q)/(2(V+a)^2)$ at zero.

For $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}$ and the endpoints
$$
A=[1/5,3/10]\times[17/60,23/60],\qquad
C=[2/5,3/5]\times[37/120,43/120],
$$
the centroid of $K$ is outside both endpoints, the four fiber centroids are nonaffine in the base, and all four fibers weigh strictly less than half the total mass. There are exactly two deepest marks, at opposite base parities. The original values are $Q=209/900$, $M=51/50$, $\beta=209/918=2/9+5/918$, and the exact path has $\beta\downarrow2/9$.

57e3e17a84fce5c1:01.reason: In 0575f5f7358f0850 take m copies of A, each with M_i=M and a_i=a, and weights 1/m. Every output base is r plus the sum of m integer vectors, so it is integral. The peak factor is mM/a−m+1 and the root-power factor is a. This yields mM−(m−1)a when M>0, while M=0 follows by nonnegativity. Its rank-one equality with repeated identical fibers and the actual closed cap containment give precisely the source calibration and all orientations. 57e3e17a84fce5c1:01.statement: For d≥1,m≥2, let A be a finite union of compact convex fibers at integer bases in a single residue class modulo m. 57e3e17a84fce5c1:02.reason: The repeated-input arithmetic peak theorem counts a finite sumset by a linear support bound. It does not lower-bound dilation counts of an arbitrary lattice polytope using its affine rank and first two Ehrhart coefficients. This proof uses the saturated ambient affine lattice, a half-open cone partition and coefficient nonnegativity, with no accepted premise.
57e3e17a84fce5c1:02.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty lattice polytope of affine dimension $s$, and let $N=|Q\cap\mathbb Z^n|$. For every integer $m\ge1$,
$$
|mQ\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s,N):=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}.
$$
For $s=0$, both sides equal one.
