57e3e17a84fce5c1:03.reason: The admitted peak estimate only counts m-fold averages and gives m times residue mass minus (m−1) peaks. The whole convex hull yields strict-level fibers at every ambient lattice point, counted once, with the separate Ehrhart lower bound applied after the exact Q_t saturation. For m=2 and rank s≥2 the integrand improves on 2N−1. The only graph dependency is the numerical dilation estimate.
57e3e17a84fce5c1:03.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with $d\ge1$, let $r\in\mathbb Z^n$ and let $m\ge2$ be an integer. Write $w_p=\operatorname{vol}_d(E_p)$, $\mu(E)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}w_p$, $A_t=\{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}$, and $a_r=\max_{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n}w_p$ with empty maximum zero. For $0<t<a_r$ put $N_t=|A_t|$, $s_t=\dim\operatorname{aff}A_t$ and $Q_t=\operatorname{conv}((A_t-r)/m)$. Then
$$
|Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|=N_t,\qquad
\big|\{p\in\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}\big|\ge |mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s_t,N_t),
$$
where $B_m(s,N)=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}$. Consequently
$$
\mu(E)\ge\int_0^{a_r}|mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\,dt\ge\int_0^{a_r} B_m(s_t,N_t)\,dt.
$$
The integrals are zero when $a_r=0$. At $m=2$, the integrand $B_2(s,N)=(s+1)N-s(s+1)/2$ is at least $2N-1$, giving $\mu(E)\ge 2\sum_{p\in r+2\mathbb Z^n}w_p-a_r$. With $r=0$, both integral inequalities are equalities for $E=[0,m(N-1)]\times K$ with $N\ge2$ and for $E=(m\Delta_s)\times K$, where $K$ is a $d$-dimensional convex body and $\Delta_s$ the standard unimodular simplex in its integer coordinates. The inequalities apply to $E=C\cap H$ for any compact convex $C$ and closed ambient halfspace $H$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:01.reason: The boundary-contact cone proves divergence for convex Lebesgue supports, unlike the finite atomic calculation. The identities are useful separately from the interpolation theorem.
5811f0ad1132ce56:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$ put $L_a(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)$ and define
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{\{a:L_a>0\ \text{on }K\}}\int_K L_a(x)^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
The infimum is positive and attained at a unique admissible $a_*$, and $E_K(y)$ is the minimum $d$-volume of the images of $K-y$ under $w\mapsto w/(1+a\cdot w)$ over these $a$. For $L=L_{a_*}$ and $E=E_K(y)$,
$$
\int_K (x-y)L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_K L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=\int_K L(x)^{-d-1}\,dx=E.
$$
Thus $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E$ on $K$ is a probability density with barycenter $y$ and $\int_K L\rho\,dx=1$. Its restriction to $K$ extends to a smooth positive function on a neighborhood of $K$.

For every invertible linear $Q$ and every $b\in\mathbb R^d$, $E_{QK+b}(Qy+b)=|\det Q|E_K(y)$. If $K\subset H$ for another convex body $H$, then $E_K(y)\le E_H(y)$ with equality exactly when $K=H$. Writing $g_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K x\,dx$ for the ordinary centroid, $E_K(y)\le |K|$ with equality exactly when $y=g_K$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:02.reason: The general triangular substitution in the accepted proof applies verbatim to the conditional escort maps and their positive weighted average once the displayed map hypotheses are established.
5811f0ad1132ce56:02.statement: A bounded Borel triangular cube map with $C^1$ own-coordinate maps of positive derivative admits successive one-dimensional substitution with volume factor the product of those derivatives.

5811f0ad1132ce56:04.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, and choose $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_i$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Use the energy $E_K(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$. Put $M=\sum_i\lambda_i K_i$ and $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}M$ and
$$
E_M(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ \sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_i}(y_i)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when the centered bodies $K_i-y_i$ with $\lambda_i>0$ are positive scalar multiples of one another. In particular $y\mapsto E_K(y)^{1/d}$ is strictly concave on $\operatorname{int}K$.

If $H$ is a convex body containing $M$, the same lower bound holds for $E_H(y)^{1/d}$. Equality then requires both $H=M$ and the same marked homothety condition. Consequently, for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ with fibers $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, the function $(z,y)\mapsto E_{C_z}(y)^{1/d}$ is jointly concave on the convex domain $\{(z,y): y\in\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^d}C_z\}$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:09.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Put $p=(d+1)/(d+2)$ and let $E_K(y)$ be the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over affine denominators strictly positive on $K$. Then
$$
E_K(y)=\max_{\substack{\rho\ge0,\ \int_K\rho\,dx=1\\\int_K x\rho(x)\,dx=y}}
\left(\int_K\rho(x)^p\,dx\right)^{d+2}.
$$
The maximum is over ordinary Lebesgue densities on $K$ with the displayed mass and mean. Its unique maximizer up to Lebesgue null sets is $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E_K(y)$, where $L(x)=1+a_*\cdot(x-y)$ is the attained optimal denominator.

58714b1fac606069:05.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and $V=|T|$. Fix $R>0$, $t=R/3$ and $1/2<a<2/3$. For $0<r\le R$, let $F_{a,r}(u)$ be the area of the cap $ax_1+(1-a)x_2\ge u$ of $rT$, divided by $V$. If
$$
|t-(1-a)r|\le s\le\min(t,ar-t),
$$
then $F_{a,r}(t-s)+F_{a,r}(t+s)=J_a(r)+K_a(s-s_a(r))^2$, where
$$
J_a(r)=r^2-\frac{(2t-ar)^2}{a(2-3a)},\qquad
K_a=\frac{2-3a}{a(2a-1)(1-a)},\qquad
s_a(r)=\frac{a((1-a)r-t)}{2-3a}.
$$
For a finite nonempty set $I$ of positive integer reflected distances with nonincreasing radii $r_h$, suppose the actual cap $a x_1+(1-a)x_2+\beta z\ge t$ puts all pairs $\pm h$, $h\in I$, in this chamber, with $s=h|\beta|$. Set $B=\sum_{h\in I}h^2$. Their combined cap mass in units of $V$ is
$$
\sum_{h\in I}J_a(r_h)+K_a\left[
 B\left(|\beta|-\frac{\sum_{h\in I}h s_a(r_h)}{B}\right)^2
 +\sum_{h\in I}s_a(r_h)^2-\frac{(\sum_{h\in I}h s_a(r_h))^2}{B}
\right].
$$
The last two terms within the brackets have a nonnegative sum. If at least two distances have positive stationary shifts, those two shifts cannot be attained together by one tilt and the last two terms have a strictly positive sum.

58714b1fac606069:06.reason: For every m≥0 and 2/3≤a≤1, the same zero-tilt pair floors apply. The truncation theorem yields a/(2a−1) times c(1−c)²/(2m+1) when R=1. Under continuous dilation by R, write c_R=R/(3a)=Rc; the term becomes [a/(2a−1)]c_R(R−c_R)²/[R(2m+1)], while the first factor becomes a(1−1/(3a))³/(2a−1) times the original sum of squared radii. 5c1f3bb21840ea60:01.statement:
Let $T$ be a nondegenerate tetrahedron with barycentric coordinates $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_3$. For the strict split $\{0,1\}\mid\{2,3\}$, the section planes are in bijection with their interior diagonal intersection $e=(x,y,z,w)$, where $x,y,z,w>0$ and $x+y+z+w=1$. The corresponding oriented affine vertex values are $t=(1/x,1/y,-1/z,-1/w)$, with the first pair on the cap side. The cyclic section vertices are
$$
A=(x,0,z,0)/(x+z),\quad B=(x,0,0,w)/(x+w),\quad
C=(0,y,0,w)/(y+w),\quad D=(0,y,z,0)/(y+z).
$$
The barycentric section centroid is $\lambda=(A+B+C+D-e)/3$. Put $P=x+y$, $R=z+w$, $a=xy$, $b=zw$ and $\Delta=(x+z)(x+w)(y+z)(y+w)=(a-b)^2+aR+bP$. If $m=\sum_i t_i\xi_i$, the cap fraction $F=|T\cap\{m\ge0\}|/|T|$, normalized coarea $S=\mathcal H^2(T\cap\{m=0\})/(|T|\lVert\nabla m\rVert)$, effective section-normal vector and normalized scalar moment to the ordinary tetrahedral centroid $g$ are
$$
F=\frac{b(P-a+b)}{\Delta},\qquad
1-F=\frac{a(R+a-b)}{\Delta},\qquad
S=\frac{3xyzw}{\Delta},\qquad
S\nabla m,\qquad S\nabla m\cdot(g-\lambda)=\frac{3(bP-aR)}{4\Delta}.
$$
Here $\lambda$ denotes the physical point when it appears in a displacement.

Equivalently, allow arbitrary positive raw heights $t=(p,q,-r,-s)$. Define $\alpha=ps/[(p+r)(p+s)(q+s)]$ and $\delta=qr/[(p+r)(q+s)(q+r)]$. Then $F=p(\alpha+\delta)+q^2/[(q+r)(q+s)]$ and $S=3(\alpha+\delta)$. In the standard tetrahedron, the oriented cross products for $ABC$ and $ACD$ are $-\alpha\nabla m$ and $-\delta\nabla m$. In any tetrahedron, with $\tau=\alpha/(\alpha+\delta)$, the centroid is $\lambda=(A+C+\tau B+(1-\tau)D)/3$. The formulas allow repeated heights within either pair. Regarding $F$ as a function of all four signed heights, $\partial F/\partial t_i=S\lambda_i$. When the four heights are distinct, $F=\sum_{t_i>0}t_i^3/\prod_{j\ne i}(t_i-t_j)$.

5c4e6b5e87c9fb06:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $0<w<1$, and let $A,K,B$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with $wA+(1-w)B\subseteq K$. Put them at distinct endpoint bases and their $w,1-w$ weighted mean, with $K$ at the mean. Assume that each marked fiber volume is at most half their sum. For one closed ambient halfspace, let $p$ be the captured fraction in $K$ and let $f_A,f_K,f_B$ be the $d$th roots of the volumes of its strict complements on the three fibers. Write $c=|K|^{1/d}$, $t=\max(w,1-w)$, and let $\kappa_d(t)\in(t,1)$ be the unique solution of
$$
\left(\frac{k}{t}\right)^d-\left(\frac{1-k}{1-t}\right)^d=1.
$$
The endpoint roots satisfy $w|A|^{1/d}\le c\kappa_d(w)$ and $(1-w)|B|^{1/d}\le c\kappa_d(1-w)$. In particular
$$
[w f_A+(1-w)f_B-f_K]_+
\le c[\kappa_d(t)-(1-p)^{1/d}]_+ .
$$
For every $p\in[0,1]$ the displayed bound is attained. It remains the supremum when all three volume inequalities are strict. Thus $\eta_d(w)=1-\kappa_d(t)^d$ is the largest universal no-deficit threshold in either class, and it tends to zero as $t\uparrow1$.

For $w=1/2$, let $B_d=2\kappa_d(1/2)$, so $B_d^d-(2-B_d)^d=1$ and $\max(|A|,|B|)^{1/d}\le B_d c$. The threshold is $1/4$ for $d=1$ and at least $39/64>1/2>\gamma_d$ for $d\ge2$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. A positive midpoint deficit $\delta$ requires $0<\delta/c\le B_d/2$ and $p\ge 1-(B_d/2-\delta/c)^d$, with equality attainable. At $d=2,w=3/4$ the threshold is $(54\sqrt2-43)/128$, and an actual closed cut with middle fraction $4/9$ can give a positive deficit.

5cea8474957220e7:01.reason: The earlier 2f355ace664c0068 supplies the full median map and domination; its full coupling class permits a central-central block. The converse here uses the forced cross-block mass and the exact opposite central deficits. The direct block proof has no accepted dependency.
5cea8474957220e7:01.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex and let $\mu$ be a probability supported on its integer fibers. At an integer median $z_0$, let $L,R,w$ be the strict left, strict right, and central masses, with $L,R\le1/2$ and $w<1/2$. Form the probability half-marginals $\alpha,\beta$ by taking twice the strict left and right measures, respectively, and filling the deficits proportionally from the central measure $\mu_0$ so that $\alpha+\beta=2\mu$. Map each legal pair to the intersection of its segment with the median fiber, using its midpoint for a central-central pair. The target laws of probability couplings with zero central-central mass are exactly $2\mu_0+T_\#\rho$, where $T$ is the median segment map on strict-cross pairs and $\rho$ is any measure of mass $1-2w$ whose first and second marginals are dominated by the strict parts of $\alpha,\beta$.

In particular, suppose the source is summed Lebesgue volume on three consecutive fibers $A,B,C_+$ at $-1,0,1$ with volumes $a,b,c$ and total $M=a+b+c$, where $a,c\le M/2$ and $b<M/2$. With $m=(a+c-b)/2$, the unnormalized targets are precisely $\mathbf1_B\,dx+T_\#\pi$, with $T(x,x')=(x+x')/2$, $|\pi|=m$, $\pi_X\le\mathbf1_A\,dx$, and $\pi_Y\le\mathbf1_{C_+}\,dx$. Each has mass $b+m=M/2$ and is supported on $B$.

external_dependencies: Weak compactness of bounded measures on a compact metric space and the closed-set Portmanteau inequality.
Finite-dimensional convex separation for the closed downward payoff set.
5cea8474957220e7:02.reason: a16dfa31498230d5 and 0aaf1194bb28ee86 state the corresponding full-coupling conclusions. Arbitrarily chosen dominated endpoints and a fixed volume baseline are not those statements' optimization class. The proof reproduces compactness and downward-payoff separation for this class without using either fact as a premise.
5cea8474957220e7:02.statement:
Let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies, $d\ge1$, with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$ and volumes $a,b,c$. Suppose $0<m=(a+c-b)/2\le\min(a,c)$. Let $\mathcal P_m$ consist of measures on $A\times C$ with mass $m$ and marginals dominated by Lebesgue volume on their respective factors. For $\pi\in\mathcal P_m$ set $\lambda_\pi=\mathbf1_B\,dx+T_\#\pi$, where $T$ is the midpoint map. The maximum raw closed-halfspace depth of these targets over both $\pi$ and marks $y\in B$ is attained.

At any fixed $y$, put $W(y)=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal P_m}\inf_{H\ni y}\lambda_\pi(H)$, using closed halfspaces. For every $\varepsilon>0$ some nonempty finite list of through-$y$ caps $H_i$ has optimum $W_F=\max_\pi\min_i\lambda_\pi(H_i)$ in $[W(y),W(y)+\varepsilon)$. For every such finite list, write $b_i=|B\cap H_i|$ and $c_i=\mathbf1_{H_i}\circ T$. The attained dual is
$$
W_F=\min_{\theta_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\theta_i=1}
\left(\sum_i\theta_i b_i+\max_{\pi\in\mathcal P_m}\int\sum_i\theta_i c_i\,d\pi\right).
$$
For a list approximating $W(y)$ and any minimizing weights, every fixed-center optimizer for $W(y)$ is within $\varepsilon$ of the optimal weighted partial-transport cost, in the same raw units.

5cea8474957220e7:03.reason: The accepted probability permutation bound covers exactly the cyclic part after normalizing and multiplying by m^k. It does not compare selected endpoints to unused capacity. The restricted-product construction adds those three estimates.
5cea8474957220e7:03.statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta$ be finite positive measures on compact metric spaces $X,Y$. For $m>0$ let $\pi$ have mass $m$ and marginals dominated by $\alpha,\beta$. Suppose its integral of a bounded Borel cost $c$ is within $\varepsilon\ge0$ of the supremum over this partial-coupling class. Put $\ell=\alpha-\pi_X$, $r=\beta-\pi_Y$, $l=|\ell|$, and $s=|r|$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int[c(p',q)-c(p,q)]_+\,d\pi(p,q)\,d\ell(p')&\le\max(m,l)\varepsilon,\\
\int[c(p,q')-c(p,q)]_+\,d\pi(p,q)\,dr(q')&\le\max(m,s)\varepsilon,\\
\int[c(p',q')-c(p,q)]_+\,d\pi(p,q)\,d\ell(p')\,dr(q')&\le\max(ls,ms,ml)\varepsilon .
\end{aligned}
$$
At exact optimality each corresponding gain is nonpositive almost everywhere for the displayed measure. For $k\ge2$ and a permutation $\tau$ of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$, the integrated positive cyclic replacement gain is at most $k m^{k-1}\varepsilon$ under $\pi^{\otimes k}$.

5cea8474957220e7:04.reason: The related e2ef40d391cd1f07 §§1–2 uses arbitrary completion in the full class. This draft proves the extra block feasibility using the discarded pairs' central total, and proves the same symmetric union bound within the restricted class.
5cea8474957220e7:04.statement:
Let $\mu$ be normalized summed Lebesgue volume on the integer fibers $K_z$ of a compact mixed body with one integer coordinate, total raw volume $M>0$ and continuous dimension $d\ge1$. At an integer median $z_0$ with $\mu\{z=z_0\}<1/2$, form the usual probability half-marginals by proportional splitting of the central fiber. Consider only their couplings $\sigma$ with zero central-central mass and let $\nu_\sigma$ be their median-segment image on the continuous fiber. For any $h\in\mathbb R^d$ and any such coupling there is another such coupling $\sigma_h$ with
$$
\sup_D|\nu_{\sigma_h}(D)-\nu_\sigma(D-h)|
\le e(h):=\min\left(1,\frac2M\sum_z[|K_z|-|K_z\cap(K_z-h)|]\right),
$$
where $D$ ranges over Borel sets. The two laws share the translated image of the retained pairs as an exact submeasure. Thus both optimized normalized closed-halfspace depth at $y$ and each optimized finite cap-mixture capacity with fixed unit normals and nonnegative weights summing to one change by at most $e(h)$ under $y\mapsto y+h$. In particular they are Lipschitz uniformly over the mixtures.

If $r_0$ is the $\pi$-essential infimum of $c\circ T$, the cost formed with the open interiors of the $H_i$ is at most $r_0$ throughout $(U+V)/2$. In particular,
$$
|B\cap\{x:c(x)\le r_0\}|\ \ge\
\left(\frac{l^{1/d}+s^{1/d}}2\right)^d .

Fix a finite nonempty real base $P$ and $d\ge1$. Let the convex bodies $K_z$ be the actual sampled fibers of their canonical hull, and use their summed $d$-volume as mixed measure. $$
\begin{aligned}

5dd0d34dec315bd7:01.statement:

$$
|A\cap\{t\le2-2W\}|\le v,\qquad W\le\frac{2a}{h-\ell},\qquad |A\cap\{t\ge2\}|\ge a-v-2W^2.
$$

600f7b09ccd06ced:01.statement:
Let $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, $g\in\operatorname{int}B$, and let finitely many positive weights $\theta_j$ sum to one. For unit $u_j$ set $D_j=B\cap\{x:u_j\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}$, let $F_j$ be the cut section with $(d-1)$-area $s_j$, and write $h_j^\pm=h_{B-g}(\pm u_j)$. Suppose $\sum_j\theta_j|D_j|=\beta|B|$; this holds if the weighted original-boundary normal marginal of these caps is $\beta S_B$. Set $R=\sum_j\theta_js_j\delta_{-u_j}$ and $e_j^+=|D_j|-s_jh_j^+/d$, $e_j^-=|B\setminus D_j|-s_jh_j^-/d$. Both remainders are nonnegative. If $R=S_J$ for a positive convex body $J$, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta|B|&=V((-J)[d-1],B)+\sum_j\theta_je_j^+,\\
(1-\beta)|B|&=V(J[d-1],B)+\sum_j\theta_je_j^-.
\end{aligned}
$$
Without $J$ the two mixed volumes are respectively the integrals of $h_{B-g}(-v)$ and $h_{B-g}(v)$ against $R/d$. Equality in the captured-cap lower bound holds precisely when each $D_j$ equals the pyramid over $F_j$ with a farthest captured apex. For $R=S_J$,
$$
\beta\ge\alpha(B,J)(|J|/|B|)^{(d-1)/d}\ge (|J|/|B|)^{(d-1)/d},\qquad
\alpha(B,J)=\frac{V((-J)[d-1],B)}{|J|^{(d-1)/d}|B|^{1/d}}.
$$
Equality in the final volume lower bound also requires $-J$ and $B$ to be homothetic.

Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. The records of a probability law are the averages of $(P,C,M)$, and the law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero. Write $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$ and $p_0=(H/B)^d$.

For a probability law on finite slopes, let $\phi$ be the mixture of uniform probability laws on $[-s,s]$ with the given slope weights and with $\delta_0$ at $s=0$. $$
\begin{aligned}
\overline P/V &= p_0e(a_0)+1-v,\\
\overline C/C_0 &= e(a_0),\\
\overline M/C_0 &= -\frac HB\int_{b\le1} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The function $e$ is convex and differentiable on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$. Every such centered law satisfies $2v-1\le e(a_0)\le(2v-1)/v$.

61e9db32fbeb3f83:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$, and $\alpha=\eta(B)/|B|$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_B\,dx+k\eta$. For a closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$, write $v=(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$, $q=1+1/d$, and $\gamma_d=q^{-d}$. For real $k\ge1$ and fixed $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the sharp infimum of $v$ over $B,\eta,H$ is the attained minimum of $s+r$ under
$$
0\le s\le1,\quad 0\le r\le\min(\alpha,s),\quad s+\alpha-r\le1,\qquad
q(1+k\alpha)s^{q-1}\ge1+k r^q+k(s+\alpha-r)^q-k s^q.
$$
Every minimizing pair has $0<s<1$ and equality in the last constraint. A simplex with $\eta$ the volume restricted to its upper-tail quantile bands $[0,r]\cup[s,s+\alpha-r]$ attains every such pair. The endpoint optima at $\alpha=0,1$ are $\gamma_d,2\gamma_d$. Equivalently, for $r\in[0,\alpha]$ let $t(r)$ be the unique positive root in $s$ of the last constraint taken at equality, ignoring the other constraints. Minimize $r+\max\{r,t(r)\}$ over those $r$ with $\max\{r,t(r)\}\le1-\alpha+r$.

For a fixed nonzero linear functional $f$, let $A_z(q)=\{x\in C_z:f(z,x)\ge q\}$, $a_z(q)=|A_z(q)|$, $G_r(q)=\sum_{z\equiv r\bmod2}a_z(q)$ and $G(q)=\sum_r G_r(q)$. Put $\Phi_d(A,B)=2^{-d}(A^{1/d}+B^{1/d})^d$. Fix $s\le t$, $h=(s+t)/2$, and apply the consecutive-interval overlap coupling in each of the $p$ classes with $G_r(t)>0$ to the positive arrays at $s$ and $t$, both in the same lexicographic order. Within class $r$ every positive overlap $\pi$ of $z,w$ has a distinct integer midpoint $k=(z+w)/2$. Set $c_{rk}=\Phi_d(a_z(s),a_w(t))$ and $v_{rk}=\pi\Phi_d(G_r(s),G_r(t))$ there and zero otherwise. Writing $\Phi_r=\Phi_d(G_r(s),G_r(t))$ on surviving classes and $\Omega=\sum_r\Phi_r$, one has
$$
G(h)\ge\sum_k\max\{a_k(t),\max_r c_{rk}\}\ge Q:=\sum_k\max_r v_{rk}
=\Omega-\sum_k\big(\sum_r v_{rk}-\max_r v_{rk}\big).
$$
The maxima over no contributions are zero. For $p>0$, $\max_r\Phi_r\le Q\le\Omega$ and $Q\ge\Omega/p\ge\Omega/2^n$. Disjoint target sets across the paths give $Q=\Omega$. If a class with $G_r(t)=0$ has a nonempty $t$-trace, pairing a point of it with every positive $s$-trace gives an additional collection of targetwise contributions of sum $2^{-d}G_r(s)$, included by taking maxima. Absent traces do not supply such contributions.

6666351f7dbc3b14:02.statement:
For each fixed $n,d\ge1$, the best universal coefficient in
$$
G((s+t)/2)\ge 2^{-n}\sum_{r:G_r(t)>0}\Phi_d(G_r(s),G_r(t))
$$
is $2^{-n}$, even for full-dimensional simplices that are the convex hull of their actual mixed sets, with every parity surviving at $t$ and the same oblique functional $f=z_1+x_1$. More precisely, for integers $L\ge1$ take $N=2L+n+1$ and $C_N=\{z,x\ge0:\sum_i z_i+2N\sum_j x_j\le N\}$, with $s=0,t=2L$. Put $D=n+d$ and $\Omega_L=\sum_r\Phi_d(G_r(0),G_r(2L))$. Then
$$
2^{-n}\le\frac{G(L)}{\Omega_L}\le
2^{-n}\left(1+\frac{3n+1}{2L+n+1}\right)^D.
$$
For $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $L\ge D(3n+1)/\epsilon$ the upper bound is at most $2^{-n}(1+\epsilon)$. Also the targetwise collision quantity $Q$ of the preceding estimate satisfies $Q/\Omega_L\longrightarrow2^{-n}$ for any of the permitted lexicographic orders.

6683db9073239231:03.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and $V=|T|=1/2$. Suppose the positive integer fibers of an actual convex body are $r_kT$ at the bases $k$ in a nonempty finite integer interval, and let $\mu$ sum their ordinary planar areas. Assume that the radii form a concave sequence. Fix a base $j$ and put $q=r_j/3$, $z_k=k-j$, and $t_k=(1+\rho)q-\beta z_k$. Consider the shared caps
$$
H_{\rho,\beta}=\{(k,x):x_1+\rho x_2+\beta(k-j)\ge (1+\rho)q\},
\qquad 0\le\rho\le1,\quad \beta\in\mathbb R .
$$
Here the halfspace margin is ambient, with the integer base replaced by a real variable away from the source fibers. The absolute closed-halfspace depth at $(j,q,q)$ divided by $V$ is the minimum of $F(\rho,\beta)=\mu(H_{\rho,\beta})/V$. Clipping $\beta$ to $[-B_*,B_*]$ preserves $F$, where $B_*=1+\max_{k\ne j}(2q+r_k)/|z_k|$ or $B_*=1$ for a singleton. The exact coupled identities and tilt condition are given below.

If all $r_k$ are rational, this minimum can be found by enumerating a finite arrangement of rational trace lines and solving univariate polynomial equations of degree at most six, with exact real-algebraic sign and value comparisons. The minimum and one realizing pair $(\rho,\beta)$ lie in a common real number field of degree at most six over $\mathbb Q$.

For the actual three-fiber chain of radii $(1/2,3/2,3/4)$ with the middle anchor, there is a strict interior local minimum of the coupled objective at $\beta=-1/8$ and $\rho=1-\sqrt{102}/12$. Its value is $(\sqrt{102}-2)/8<81/80$.

668ad0ef7a63372e:01.statement: Let P=π(C)∩Z^n for compact convex C, and let a full-dimensional polyhedron L={z:a_i·z≤β_i, 1≤i≤s} with nonzero rows satisfy int(L)∩P=∅. 668ad0ef7a63372e:02.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be compact and convex, and put $P=A\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let the full-dimensional polyhedron $L=\{z:a_r\cdot z\le\beta_r\}$ have $2^n$ nonzero rows, with $\operatorname{int}L\cap P=\varnothing$ and one witness $p_r\in P$ on each row that strictly satisfies all other rows. Index the witnesses by their parities $r\bmod 2$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $[z]=z\bmod2$ and $R(z)=(z+p_{[z]})/2$.

Every $y\in\mathbb Z^n$ has exactly the $2^n$ distinct preimages $\{2y-p_r\}_r$, hence at most $2^n$ in $P$, and $R(P)\subseteq P$. Every full-lattice orbit terminates at a fixed witness. If $z_0=z$, $z_{j+1}=R(z_j)$, and $z_k=p_s$, then
$$
z-p_s=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^j(p_s-p_{[z_j]}).
$$
Thus the basin of $p_s$ lies in $p_s$ plus the nonnegative integer semigroup generated by the $p_s-p_r$. On that basin $a_s\cdot z\ge\beta_s$, with equality only at $p_s$. In particular $L\cap\mathbb Z^n=\{p_r\}_r$. On $P$ the potential $V(z)=\max_r(a_r\cdot z-\beta_r)$ is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at the witnesses and satisfies $V(R(z))\le V(z)/2$. If $P$ has a nonroot and $\delta$ is its least strictly positive potential, an orbit from a nonroot $z\in P$ takes at most $1+\lceil\log_2(V(z)/\delta)\rceil$ steps to terminate.

668ad0ef7a63372e:03.reason: The exterior row inequality applies to every base assigned to the given root. 668ad0ef7a63372e:03.statement:
Use the full-parity witness orbits with $A=\pi(C)$ for compact convex $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of original $d$-volume on its integer fibers. For a witness $p_s$ let $H_{sj}=\{(z,x):\ell_{sj}(z,x)>0\}$ be open ambient caps, with $1\le j\le k_s\le d+1$, $\ell_{sj}$ affine, and $\lambda_{sj}>0$ satisfying
$$
\sum_j\lambda_{sj}\ell_{sj}(z,x)=a_s\cdot z-h_s,\qquad h_s<\beta_s.
$$
If all $\mu(H_{sj})<T$ for $T>0$, then $\bigcup_jH_{sj}$ contains the whole continuous plane over every base in the basin of $p_s$, including the root. If $B_s$ is the set of basin bases in $P$, then
$$
\mu(B_s\times\mathbb R^d)\le\sum_j\mu(H_{sj})<k_s T\le(d+1)T.
$$

668ad0ef7a63372e:04.statement:
Use the full-parity witness orbits with $A=\pi(C)$ for compact convex $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and write $K_z=C_z$ and $f(z)=|K_z|_d^{1/d}$ on $P$. On a path $z_0=z,\ldots,z_k=p_s$,
$$
2^{-k}K_z+\sum_{j<k}2^{j-k}K_{p_{[z_j]}}\subseteq K_{p_s},
\qquad
f(z)+\sum_{j<k}2^jf(p_{[z_j]})\le 2^k f(p_s).
$$
The inequality allows nonempty zero-volume fibers. If every witness fiber has volume $v_0\ge0$, then every fiber on $P$ has volume at most $v_0$. If $v_0>0$ and the source $K_z$ has volume $v_0$, the used witness fibers and the intermediate fibers are translates of $K_z$, and each intermediate fiber equals its preceding Minkowski midpoint with the corresponding witness fiber.

668ad0ef7a63372e:05.reason: The terminal barycenter only gives the two coefficient moments. The signed coefficients and dyadic slack formula require the one-step volume-root inequality and repeated substitution. The cube-root product is an exact zero-slack witness showing divergence of original source mass relative to root volume under the stated geometry. The six-fiber example ff8dd8bb1c333bbf instead imposes cap budgets and refutes a cap-mass promotion, so it cannot be substituted for this scalar obstruction.
668ad0ef7a63372e:05.statement:
Use the full-parity witness orbits on the lattice projection $P$ of a compact convex body in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $n,d\ge1$. Let $f(z)=|C_z|_d^{1/d}$ and $g(z)=2f(R(z))-f(z)-f(p_{[z]})\ge0$. For $z_0=z,\ldots,z_k=p_s$ one has
$$
f(z)=2^kf(p_s)-\sum_{j<k}2^jf(p_{[z_j]})-\sum_{j<k}2^jg(z_j).
$$
For equal root volume roots $f_0$ the last sum equals $f_0-f(z)\le f_0$. For any finite nonnegative weights $w_z$ on $P$, define $A_w(t)=\sum_{z,j<k(z):z_j=t}2^jw_z$ and let $C_w(r)$ sum the coefficients of $f(p_r)$ on the right side, weighted by $w_z$. Then
$$
\sum_z w_z f(z)+\sum_tA_w(t)g(t)=\sum_r C_w(r)f(p_r),\qquad
\sum_r C_w(r)=\sum_z w_z,\qquad
\sum_r C_w(r)p_r=\sum_z w_z z.
$$
The $A_w$ are nonnegative, while $C_w(0)=(L+1)(1-L/2)<0$ for $P=\{0,\ldots,L\}$, roots $0,1$, unit weights and integer $L>2$. Furthermore for each fixed $n,d\ge1$ there are such forests with all slack zero, all root volumes equal, and arbitrarily large ratios of total actual volume to the sum of root volumes.

668d91587751e139:01.reason: The accepted unequal-radius envelope and exact inverse-optimizer argument give one-copy domination of the discounted, rather than bare, actual midpoint law in a fixed normal/parity class.
668d91587751e139:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, and let positive convex $d$-fibers be the exact sampled fibers of their canonical hull $C$. Write $\eta$ for their summed boundary measures marked by outward unit normal, with endpoint counting for $d=1$. Let $L=\min_i A_i>0$ on $C$ for finitely many affine functions, with $\ell=\min_C L$ and $U=\max_C L$. For each normal take one finite concave physical numerator $H$ with $W=H_+/L^d$ Borel and bounded on the actual and finitely many pair-average surface ranges. Put $\omega=W\eta$.

Suppose equal-mass endpoints $\gamma_\pm\le\omega$ have an old same-normal coupling $\pi_0$ with integer midpoints on the actual support graph. With $b=(w_-+w_+)/2$ and $a=[L(w_-)+L(w_+)]/(2L(b))$, there is a same-marginal same-normal coupling $\pi$ on the actual midpoint support graph with the following properties. In each normal and original parity class its conditional physical midpoint law $\rho=b_\#\pi$ dominates the old one in full convex order, and its discounted law $D=b_\#(a^d\pi)$ is dominated by one copy of the conditional $\omega$. Writing $E=b_\#((1-a^d)\pi)$ in that class gives $\rho=D+E$, $(\rho-\omega)_+\le E$ and $\rho\le(U/\ell)^d\omega$. For the total marked laws one has $D_{\rm tot}\le 2^n\omega$ and $(\rho_{\rm tot}-2^n\omega)_+\le E_{\rm tot}$. If the common total mass is $m>0$, then
$$
E_{\rm tot}(\mathrm{total})\le m[1-\exp(-d\Delta_0/m)]\le d\Delta_0,
$$
where $\Delta_0$ is the old integrated logarithmic Jensen gap of $L$ on the tuples. At $m=0$ the error is zero. A standard Borel old mark can retain its joint law with the normal and parity and its conditional midpoint mean.

If the old $L$-Jensen gap is zero almost everywhere, the new gap is zero almost everywhere and $\rho$ itself has the one-copy ceiling in each class and the $2^n$ global ceiling. The nonlinear logarithmic bound and the nonlinear power-weighted bounds of the companion entropy theorem are attained on a single class by equal cube fibers at bases $-1,0,1$, $H=1$, $L(z,x)=1+s-s|z|$ for $s>0$, and matching full face laws at the two outside bases with one common facet normal.

668d91587751e139:02.reason: The bound follows from the fixed-endpoint Jensen gap and convex order, followed by the logarithmic or power-weighted Jensen inequality.
668d91587751e139:02.statement:
Let $C$ be compact convex, $L=\min_i A_i>0$ on $C$ for finitely many affine functions, and $d\ge1$ an integer. Let two tuple laws $\pi,\pi_0$ on $C^2$ have the same endpoint marginals $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ of mass $m>0$. For $b=(w_-+w_+)/2$, write $\rho=b_\#\pi$, $\rho_0=b_\#\pi_0$ and suppose $\rho_0\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\rho$ in full physical coordinates. Put $V=(L(w_-)+L(w_+))/2$, $a=V/L(b)$ and $E=b_\#((1-a^d)\pi)$. If
$$
\Delta_0=\int\!\left(\log L(b)-\tfrac12[\log L(w_-)+\log L(w_+)]\right)d\pi_0,
$$
then $E(C)\le m[1-\exp(-d\Delta_0/m)]\le d\Delta_0$.

For $0<p\le1$ put $T_p=\int L^p\,d\rho$, $T_{p,0}=\int L^p\,d\rho_0$ and $c_p=\tfrac12\int L^p\,d(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)$. Then $c_p\le T_p\le T_{p,0}$ and
$$
\int L^p\,dE\le T_p[1-(c_p/T_p)^{d/p}]
\le T_{p,0}[1-(c_p/T_{p,0})^{d/p}]
\le (d/p)(T_{p,0}-c_p).
$$

For any nonnegative affine $q$ on $C$ put $F_q=q\log(q/L)$ with $0\log0=0$, $T_q=\int q\,d\rho=\tfrac12\int q\,d(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)$, and $\Delta_q(\pi')=\tfrac12\int F_q\,d(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)-\int F_q\,d(b_\#\pi')$. If $T_q>0$, then
$$
\int q\,dE\le T_q[1-\exp(-d\Delta_q(\pi)/T_q)]
\le T_q[1-\exp(-d\Delta_q(\pi_0)/T_q)]
\le d\Delta_q(\pi_0).
$$
At each tuple with $q_0=q(b)>0$ the tuple gap divided by $q_0$ is $-\log a+\mathrm{KL}((q_-,q_+)/(2q_0)\,\Vert\,(L_-,L_+)/(2V))$. The relative-entropy term vanishes exactly when $q_-/L_-=q_+/L_+$. For $T_q=0$ the weighted error and gaps are zero. All bounds use the same $\pi$. For $m=0$ all errors and bounds are understood as zero.

668d91587751e139:03.reason: The global assembly in the reviewed theorem uses compact Borel selection for the same discounted tests and actual support. It sums one-copy class bounds and retains the old marked conditional midpoint means by a measurable martingale.
668d91587751e139:03.statement: Under the fixed-normal hypotheses of §§1–4 for almost every normal and each of at most 2^n original parity classes, assume Borel kernels for the old tuple law, actual support relation, discount and reference, with compact feasible conditional repair classes. A measurable same-normal repair has the original endpoint marginals, D_tot≤2^nω, ρ_tot=D_tot+E_tot, and (ρ_tot−2^nω)_+≤E_tot. If m_tot>0 its total error is at most m_tot[1−exp(−dΔ_old,tot/m_tot)]≤dΔ_old,tot, with zero error at m_tot=0. Old source marks and their conditional midpoint means can be retained through a marked martingale and conditional endpoint resampling.

668d91587751e139:04.reason: The cube-facet construction in the theorem forces equality of the two input points by the exact quadratic moment identity. Its reference law is (1+s)^(−d) times the midpoint, with the displayed sharp logarithmic and nonlinear power bounds.
668d91587751e139:04.statement: For every integer d≥1 and b>0, take identical d-cubes at bases −1,0,1, a common facet normal with uniform facet mass m (one endpoint atom with m=1 if d=1), H=1 and L(z,x)=1+b−b|z|. Prescribe the full facet marginals at ±1 and the old diagonal coupling in their continuous coordinates. Every fixed-marginal midpoint law dominating the old one in physical convex order equals it. The middle reference is (1+b)^(−d) times this midpoint law; hence E=(ρ−ω)_+, Δ₀=m log(1+b), and E(C)=m[1−exp(−dΔ₀/m)]. Each nonlinear L^p error inequality is also attained for this one parity.

668d91587751e139:05.reason: The affine-weighted clause of the same theorem proves the exact relative-entropy gap, the equality condition for its entropy term and all three bounds for every nonnegative affine q.
668d91587751e139:05.statement: Under the fixed-marginal convex-order hypotheses of §§4–6, let q be any nonnegative affine physical function on C, F_q=q log(q/L) with 0 log 0=0, Δ_q(π')=½∫F_q d(γ_-+γ_+)−∫F_q d(b_#π'), and T_q=∫q dρ=½∫q d(γ_-+γ_+). Then for T_q>0, ∫q dE≤T_q[1−exp(−dΔ_q(π)/T_q)]≤T_q[1−exp(−dΔ_q(π₀)/T_q)]≤dΔ_q(π₀), with zero throughout when T_q=0. For positive q(b), the tuple Jensen gap divided by q(b) is −log a+KL((q_-,q_+)/(2q(b)) || (L_-,L_+)/(2V)); the KL term vanishes exactly when q_-/L_-=q_+/L_+. The same π satisfies every such inequality.

66cd3b069de31436:01.statement:
Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be finite and concave with integral one. Replace its endpoint values by the corresponding one-sided limits to obtain a continuous representative $\bar f$. Let $\nu$ be the positive Stieltjes curvature measure of the decreasing right derivative of $\bar f$ on $(0,1)$. Then
$$
\bar f(t)=\bar f(0)(1-t)+\bar f(1)t+\int_{(0,1)}(\min(t,p)-tp)\,\nu(dp).
$$
Equivalently, $\bar f=\int T_p\,d\mu(p)$ for a probability measure $\mu$ on $[0,1]$, where $T_0(t)=2(1-t)$, $T_1(t)=2t$ and $T_p(t)=2\min\{t/p,(1-t)/(1-p)\}$ for $0<p<1$. The endpoint masses are $\bar f(0)/2,\bar f(1)/2$ and the interior measure is $p(1-p)\nu(dp)/2$.

$$
\frac{|A\cap\{\ell\ge-t\}|}{w}
\ge \left(1-\frac{1-t}{H}\right)^2+
\frac{(1-t)(H-1+t)}{3(H-3)}
\left[r-\left(1-\frac3H\right)^2\right]_+.

670310a99fe94843:01.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, and let $q\ge1$ be the largest dimension of any nonempty integer fiber. Write $M$ for the total intrinsic $\mathcal H_q$ mass of its integer trace. For any nonempty set $P$ of bases of positive $q$-volume in one parity class put $w_p=\mathcal H_q(E_p)$, $M_P=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $a=\max_{p\in P}w_p$, and $s=\dim\operatorname{aff}P$. There is a triangulation graph $G$ with vertex set exactly $P$ and a root $p_*$ with $w_{p_*}=a$ such that
$$
\begin{aligned}
M&\ge M_P+\sum_{\{p,p'\}\in G}\left(\frac{w_p^{1/q}+w_{p'}^{1/q}}2\right)^q\\
 &\ge 2M_P-a+2^{-q}\left[\deg_G(p_*)a+\sum_{p\ne p_*}(\deg_G(p)-2)w_p\right].
\end{aligned}
$$
The triangulation makes the concave roof of the input volume roots affine on its simplices, and has a spanning tree ascending in volume toward $p_*$. For $s\ge2$ the excess above $2M_P-a$ is at least $2^{-q}[(s-2)M_P+2a]\ge s2^{-q}a$. The coefficient $s2^{-q}$ relative to $a$ is optimal for each $s\ge2$ and $q\ge1$. When $s=1$ the bracket is $a$ minus the opposite endpoint volume if the root is an endpoint, or twice $a$ minus the sum of endpoint volumes otherwise. For $s=0$, $M\ge a$. The theorem includes $q=d$ and every actual closed cap $E=C\cap H$, with the largest dimension and mass taken within $E$.

Assume the proper deepest-source and pure-base reserve conditions of the body-tied finite cover. Fix such a cover with finite groups, proper selected caps and finite old contact sets. Write $\rho_{ij}>0$ for its cap weights summing to one in group $i$.

Vary the nonvertical ambient facet offsets with signed derivatives $h$, retaining all ambient normals, pure-base offsets and selected cap normals. Write $s=\dot{\log\varepsilon}$ in the interior-scale case and set $s=0$ otherwise. On a sampled facet $F$, let $v_F$ be the maximum of the inward speeds $-h_f/|u_f|$ of active nonvertical ambient rows $f$ with continuous normal $u_f$, and let $D=\sum_F |F|v_F$. For each group let $\alpha_i=\min_a A_{ia}$, where $A_{ia}$ is the individual contact response of the body-tied continuation at fixed cap normals. For selected cap $ij$ write $b_{ij}=|u_{ij}|$, $S_{ij}>0$ for its proper-section coarea, $r_{ij}$ for its threshold derivative, and $B_{ij}$ for captured old-boundary loss excluding the supporting facets. Its actual loss is
$$
R_{ij}=B_{ij}+S_{ij}r_{ij}
+\sum_{\rm in}|F|\max(v_F,r_{ij}/b_{ij})
+\sum_{\rm out}|F|\min(0,v_F+r_{ij}/b_{ij}).
$$
Inside support means the captured halfspace contains the whole old fiber, and outside support means that it meets only its supporting face. The surface measure $|F|$ is counting measure in dimension one.

Choose one maximizing ambient row at each $F$, one minimizing contact in each group, and one branch for each inside maximum and outside minimum. Impose their weak branch inequalities together with $R_{ij}=L_i$ and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}r_{ij}=\alpha_i$. In each of the resulting finitely many closed polyhedral cones in $(h,s,r,L)$, the simultaneous linear inequalities $L_i-\beta D+M\tau s\ge1$ for all groups are infeasible. The scale term is omitted at fixed scale. Feasibility in any cone is equivalent to a strictly descending first-order test in the indicated directions.

6748c967393345b9:09.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$ be integers. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and finite, fix $p\in P$, and for each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact, and convex. Assume the anchored Minkowski inclusion
$$
\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_z\ge0,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p .
\tag{1}
$$
Use the given Euclidean base coordinates. The affine rank $r=\dim\operatorname{span}(P-p)$ may be any integer from $0$ to $n$. Write $h_z(u)=\max_{x\in K_z}u\cdot x$. For every $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ the inequalities
$$
h_z(u)\le h_p(u)+A\cdot(z-p)\qquad(z\in P)
\tag{2}
$$
have a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution $A_p(u)$. It lies in $\operatorname{span}(P-p)$, and the map $u\mapsto A_p(u)$ is continuous and bounded. The affine function $z\mapsto h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ yields a supporting inequality $u\cdot x\le h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ on $\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with equality at every point of the $u$-supporting face of $\{p\}\times K_p$.

$$
F(s)+F(-s)\ge2\gamma_d\qquad(s\ge0).
$$
For $d\ge2$ the same bound holds with $F(s)=\mathbb P(Z\ge s)$ for any compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law of $Z$ on the line. In particular, for any independent random vector $Y\in\mathbb R^d$ with a distribution symmetric about zero, every closed halfspace through $g$ has $\mathbb P(X+Y\in H)\ge\gamma_d$. If $Y$ has finite first moment, the convolution has centroid $g$.

For a product of convex bodies $P\times K$ with $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ centrally symmetric about $j\in\mathbb Z^n$, every closed ambient halfspace containing $(j,g)$ has normalized mixed-integer mass at least $\gamma_d$.

$$
\sum_{p\in P_i}\lambda_{ip}=A_i,\qquad
\sum_{p\in P_i}\lambda_{ip}p=A_i c_i.
$$

$$
\sum_{i,p}\lambda_{ip}a_i=0,\qquad
\sum_{i,p}\lambda_{ip}a_i p^{\mathsf T}=|L|I_n,\qquad

773c78a48aafd464:02.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be finite, with capacities $a_z>0$ for $z\in P$. Fix a mass $m\ge0$ and a vector $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and assume
$$
Q=\{b:0\le b_z\le a_z,\ \sum_{z\in P}b_z=m,\ \sum_{z\in P}z b_z=mg\}
$$
is nonempty. A point of $Q$ is extreme exactly when the columns $(1,z)$ at its partially filled sites $0<b_z<a_z$ are linearly independent. Every linear cost $\sum_z c_zb_z$ has an extreme minimizer, and this minimizer has at most $\operatorname{rank}((1,z)_{z\in P})\le n+1$ partially filled sites.

There are a scalar $\lambda$ and vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the minimum value is
$$
\lambda m+v\cdot(mg)+\sum_{z\in P}a_z\min(0,c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z).
$$
For this pair a feasible $b$ is optimal exactly when $b_z=a_z$ at each strict negative reduced cost $c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z$ and $b_z=0$ at each strict positive one. If $c_z=\|z-g\|_2^2$ and $m>0$, the reduced cost is the squared distance from $g+v/2$ minus a nonnegative squared radius. Every optimizer thus fills the strict interior sites of the corresponding closed ball, leaves its exterior sites empty, and can be fractional only on its sphere.

8027472c0c8717cd:02.statement:

$$

80791dd8739dad42:04.statement:
Take a finite complete sampled lattice base $P$ with actual compatible compact positive-volume convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, summed volume $\mu$, and a source $Y=(p,y)$ with $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$. Fix $h>0$ and a norm $\Gamma$ on continuous covectors. Write $V_z=|K_z|$ and let $B_p$ be the minimum of $\sum_{z:a\cdot(z-p)>0}V_z$ over generic base covectors $a$, meaning $a\cdot(z-p)\ne0$ for $z\ne p$. If $P=\{p\}$ put $B_p=0$.

For every $\Gamma$-unit $u$ a finite multiple of $a_*$ gives outside ramp mass exactly $B_p$ and leaves the own-fiber contribution $Q_p^{\rm own}(u)$ unchanged, so $Q\le B_p+Q_p^{\rm own}(u)$. For an actual active nonvertical cap $N=(a,u)$ of mass $Q$, write $Q_p^{\rm out}(N)$ for its outside ramp mass. Then
$$
0\le Q_p^{\rm out}(N)\le B_p,\qquad
\Delta_N=B_p-Q_p^{\rm out}(N)=B_p+Q_p^{\rm own}(u)-Q\ge0.
$$

If a finite actual active menu has $\Delta_N=0$ on every term and quantile probabilities $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, the caps can all be replaced by such finite saturating tilts with the same $u_j$ and remain active and quantile balanced. If $B_p>0$ the retargeted menu has unit capture efficiency for one nonnegative admissible field supported on an exposed target fiber of the complete base hull. If $B_p=0$, the own fiber is exposed and the projective field there pays capture efficiency at least $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ for every actual active menu at $Y$. Here efficiency means the boundary integral of field times ramp profile divided by its positive boundary integral.

8081cb180611f9d3:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V=1/d!$, and $u_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i u_i=1$. Put $F_r(s)=|rT\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge s\}|/V$ and $t=1/(d+1)$. For $k>0$ and $0\le\beta<kt$, set
$$
f_-(h)=F_{1-kh}(t-\beta h),\qquad f_+(h)=F_{1-kh}(t+\beta(h+1))\qquad(0\le h\le1/k)
$$
and extend both by zero for $h\ge1/k$. Each is nonnegative and convex on $[0,\infty)$. For either function $f$, the sum over nonnegative integers satisfies
$$
\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge \int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+f(0)/2,\qquad \sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge f(0).
$$
If $k\le1$ it follows that $\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge(1-k)\int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+(1+k)f(0)/2$.

Let $\Theta$ be uniform on the opposite facet $\operatorname{conv}(e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, with $\Theta=e_1$ if $d=1$, and put $U=u\cdot\Theta$. For $s>0$, $F_r(s)=\mathbb E[(r^d-(s/U)^d)_+]$, taking the integrand to be zero at $U=0$. Write $c=\beta/k$ and $B=t+\beta$. If $c>0$, then $\int_0^\infty f_\pm(h)\,dh=\mathbb E[J_\pm(U)]/[k(d+1)]$, where $J_-(U)=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_+(U)=0$ for $U\le B$. On their respective remaining domains,
$$
J_-(U)=1-\frac{t^{d+1}}{cU^d}+\frac{(t-c)^{d+1}}{c(U-c)^d},\qquad
J_+(U)=1+\frac{B^{d+1}}{cU^d}-\frac{(B+c)^{d+1}}{c(U+c)^d}.
$$
If $c=0$ the same integral formula uses $J_-=J_+=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_-=J_+=1-(d+1)(t/U)^d+d(t/U)^{d+1}$ for $U>t$.

8081cb180611f9d3:02.reason: The two exact integrals are included in the same draft as the parent affine-cap lemma. This accounts for both angular cutoffs, the c=0 case and ties, without a lower bound for an arbitrary angular law.
8081cb180611f9d3:02.statement: For the same f_± put c=β/k and B=t+β. For c>0 their integrals equal E[J_±(U)]/[k(d+1)], where J_−=0 for U≤t and J_+=0 for U≤B. Otherwise J_−=1−t^(d+1)/(cU^d)+(t−c)^(d+1)/(c(U−c)^d) and J_+=1+B^(d+1)/(cU^d)−(B+c)^(d+1)/(c(U+c)^d). For c=0 both use J(U)=1−(d+1)(t/U)^d+d(t/U)^(d+1) only on U>t and zero otherwise.

8095e181b6be7bf1:01.reason: Optimize the fixed row geometric means under the column budgets. Exact support inequalities and the explicitly feasible row witness give the attained support dual.
8095e181b6be7bf1:01.statement:
For $d\ge1$ and $m=d+1$, let $D_d$ consist of all $v\in\mathbb R_+^m$ for which there exists a nonnegative zero-diagonal column-stochastic $m\times m$ matrix $Y$ satisfying $v_i\le \operatorname{GM}_d((Y_{ij})_{j\ne i})$ for every $i$, where $\operatorname{GM}_d$ is the geometric mean of $d$ entries. The set $D_d$ is compact, convex, and downward in the nonnegative orthant. For every $c\ge0$ its support function satisfies the attained identity
$$
h_{D_d}(c)=\min\left\{\sum_j\lambda_j:\ \lambda\ge0,\ c_i\le d\left(\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j\right)^{1/d}\ \text{for every }i\right\}.
$$
In particular, $v\ge0$ belongs to $D_d$ if and only if
$$
\sum_jp_j^d-d\sum_i v_i\prod_{j\ne i}p_j\ge0\qquad\text{for every }p\ge0.
$$
This gives $D_1=[0,1]^2$ and $D_2=\{v\ge0:\sum_i v_i^2+2v_1v_2v_3\le1\}$. For positive $\lambda$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=dT$ and each $\lambda_i\le T$, the choice $c_i=d(\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j)^{1/d}$ gives an attaining primal matrix $Y_{ii}=0$ and $Y_{ij}=(T-\lambda_i)/\lambda_j$ for $i\ne j$.

810352ec6ea27062:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty finite set, and let the full-dimensional fibers $K_z$ at $z\in P$ be the actual sampled fibers of a convex set $C$. Fix the affine barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ of a nondegenerate simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and assume

$K_z=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b_i(z)\ \forall i\},\qquad 1-\sum_i b_i(z)>0.$

Write $v_j(z)$ for the vertex opposite facet $F_j(z)$, and let $B_i=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times F_i(z))$. For $p\in P$, the following are equivalent:
1. $(p,v_j(p))$ is not a vertex of some $B_i$ with $i\ne j$.
2. It is not a vertex of any $B_i$ with $i\ne j$.
3. There are other bases $z_r\ne p$ and positive weights $t_r$ summing to one such that

$p=\sum_r t_r z_r,\qquad b_l(p)=\sum_r t_r b_l(z_r)\quad\text{for every }l\ne j.$

In particular, the same representation works for all $d$ active offsets. For each $l\ne j$, the continuous-projection offset $\inf_{x\in C_z}\lambda_l(x)$ is affine on the convex hull of these $z_r$.

810352ec6ea27062:02.statement:

$$
W=\sum_l\theta_l\mathbf1_{H_l},\qquad
W_{\rm strict}(X)=\sum_{\{l:X\in\operatorname{int}H_l\}}\theta_l.
$$
An admissible potential is a continuous nonnegative function $\Phi(n,z,x)$ convex in $(z,x)$ for each fixed $n$, with $\int\Phi\,d\eta>0$. 81d3a9207b6b68f5:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite, $z\in\mathbb R^n$, and $w=(w_v)_{v\in P}\ge0$. For each nonempty $A\subset P$ with $z\in\operatorname{conv} A$, allow a mass $\lambda_A\ge0$ that charges each $v\in A$ its full value, subject to $\sum_{A\ni v}\lambda_A\le w_v$. The maximum $f_w(z)$ of $\sum_A\lambda_A$ is attained, and restricting to inclusion-minimal qualifying groups does not change it; these have at most $n+1$ points. With those groups, the exact attained dual minimizes $\sum_v w_v t_v$ subject to $0\le t_v\le1$ and $\sum_{v\in A}t_v\ge1$ for every group. If there are no groups both values are zero. At fixed $z$, $f_w(z)$ is nondecreasing, positively homogeneous, concave, piecewise linear and superadditive in $w$, with
$$
|f_w(z)-f_{w'}(z)|\le\sum_v|w_v-w_v'|.
$$
The maximum over any fixed finite nonempty target set is continuous. Thus any universal bound $\max_z f_w(z)\ge c\sum_v w_v$ over that fixed target set for positive weights extends to nonnegative weights.

81d3a9207b6b68f5:02.statement:

81d3a9207b6b68f5:05.statement:

Every lattice point in the last nonempty recorded hull supports a full-occurrence fractional convex-hull packing of value at least $\sum_j\delta_j$. 81d65baa0f0a1024:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $F=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i=1\}$, and let $g=(1/d,\ldots,1/d)$. Independently take $Z\sim\mu$ and a uniform vertex index $I$. For $0\le b\le1/d$ put $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$ and $a=1-db$. The largest constant for which
$$
\mathbb E\psi(Y_b)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)
\ge c_d(b)\bigl(\psi(g)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr)
$$
holds for every continuous concave $\psi$ on $F$ is
$$
c_d(b)=\frac{a-a^d/(1-b)^{d-1}}{(d-1)^2}.
$$
It is positive for $0<b<1/d$ and vanishes at both endpoints. The test $\psi(x)=\min_i x_i$ attains equality with a positive Jensen gap throughout the parameter interval. In particular,
$$
c_d\bigl(1/(d+1)\bigr)=\frac{1-d^{1-d}}{(d-1)^2(d+1)}.
$$

**Facet consequence.** On any facet of a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be normalized facet volume, $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ its barycentric coordinates, and $g_F$ its centroid. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=c_d(1/m)$, $N(s)=\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}$, and $E_d(\psi)=\int_F(N-m\Gamma)\psi\,d\mu$. The uniform point $Z$ and averaged point $Y_{1/m}$ on the facet obey
$$
E_d(\psi)=m\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb E\psi(Y_{1/m})-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr).
$$
For every continuous concave $\psi$ and every supporting affine majorant $\ell$ at $g_F$,
$$
\int_F(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu=\psi(g_F)-\int_F\psi\,d\mu\le\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\Gamma c}.
$$
The coefficient is sharp, and $E_d(\psi)=0$ exactly for affine $\psi$. In convex form, every continuous convex $f\ge0$ with $f(g_F)=0$ satisfies $\int_F Nf\,d\mu\le m\Gamma(1-c)\int_F f\,d\mu$.

81d65baa0f0a1024:03.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2(d+1)]$, and $V=1/d!$. Let $B=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d-1}:z_j\ge0,\ \sum_j z_j\le1\}$, with normalized volume $\mu$ and barycentric coordinates $s=(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1},1-\sum_j z_j)$. For a fixed continuous concave $\psi\ge0$ on $B$ and $\varepsilon>0$ put
$$
K_\varepsilon=\{(z,r):z\in B,\ \sum_jz_j-1\le r\le\varepsilon\psi(z)\}.
$$
This is a full-dimensional convex body, with $|K_\varepsilon|=V+\varepsilon dV\int_B\psi\,d\mu$. Let $\ell(z)=A+\sum_j B_jz_j$ be a fixed supporting affine majorant at the centroid of $B$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the simplex $S_\varepsilon$ given by
$$
q\ge0,\qquad z_j\ge0,\qquad q+\sum_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)z_j\le1+\varepsilon A,\qquad q=r-\sum_jz_j+1
$$
encloses $K_\varepsilon$. It satisfies
$$
|S_\varepsilon|=\frac{V(1+\varepsilon A)^d}{\prod_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)},\qquad
1-\frac{|K_\varepsilon|}{|S_\varepsilon|}
=\varepsilon d\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu+O(\varepsilon^2).
$$
For a full-dimensional body $K$, write $D(K)$ for maximum ordinary halfspace depth with respect to normalized volume. With $E_d(\psi)=\int_B[\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}-m\Gamma]\psi\,d\mu$,
$$
D(K_\varepsilon)=\Gamma+\varepsilon\frac{d}{m}E_d(\psi)+o(\varepsilon).
$$
For each fixed nonaffine roof the denominator in the following limit has positive linear coefficient, and
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{D(K_\varepsilon)-\Gamma}{1-|K_\varepsilon|/|S_\varepsilon|}
=\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu}
\ge\Gamma c.
$$
Equality in this limit is attained by $\psi=\min_i s_i$. If $\psi$ is affine, both linear terms vanish and the enclosing simplex formula still holds. The total variation distance of the two normalized uniform laws equals the displayed missing fraction, which therefore bounds their discrepancy over closed halfspaces. All error estimates are for the fixed roof and, where applicable, the fixed majorant.

$$
|B\cap H|+\eta(H)\ \ge\ \frac{\Gamma_d}{L}\bigl(|B|+L\eta(B)\bigr),
\qquad \Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.
$$

81d698898b296675:02.statement: Let an actual mixed-integer body have one integer coordinate and continuous dimension $d\ge1$. Suppose that at a mark on this fiber every containing closed ambient halfspace has original mixed volume at least the mass of its fiber trace under $\mathbf1_B\,dx+\eta$. Then $\eta(B)\le\min(\ell,r)$. If additionally $|B|+2\eta(B)$ equals the total original mixed volume, then $\ell=r$. An integer weighted median need not have this balance.

821242aee5d2f3e1:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real and $\rho>0$. For integers $m\ge0$ put $A_m=\sum_{j=0}^m(\rho+j)^d$. The sequence $(A_m^{1/(d+1)})_{m\ge0}$ is concave at every integer midpoint $m\ge1$. In particular, for $S_d(q)=\sum_{j\ge0}(q-j)_+^d$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$, every real $q>1$ satisfies
$$
S_d(q+1)^{1/(d+1)}+S_d(q-1)^{1/(d+1)}\le 2S_d(q)^{1/(d+1)}.
$$
For each fixed $d$ the exponent $1/(d+1)$ is the largest positive exponent that works uniformly over the sequences $A_m$.

821242aee5d2f3e1:04.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real and let $(a_i)_{i=\ell}^r$ be positive probability masses on consecutive integers with concave $d$th roots. Suppose $\mu=\sum_{i=\ell}^r i a_i$ is an integer. Both closed tails satisfy
$$
\sum_{i\ge\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1},
\qquad
\sum_{i\le\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1}.
$$
At every fixed $d$ this constant is the infimum of either tail among profiles with exactly integer mean.

For the geometric consequence, let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body with positive mixed $d$-volume $W$. If the base coordinate of its mixed-volume centroid is an integer, every closed vertical halfspace containing the centroid has mixed $d$-volume strictly greater than $W((d+1)/(d+2))^{d+1}$. This normalized bound is also sharp as an infimum.

825f4248238fa3c9:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for compact convex $C$, with positive mixed $d$-volume $W=\mu(S)$. Let finitely many open ambient halfspaces $U_j$ cover $S$, and suppose their closed versions each have mixed cap mass at most $\tau W$. $$
\left(\frac{a^{1/d}+b^{1/d}}2\right)^d\le |I\cup J|\tau W.

$$

8280d34e5808dfad:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Put $Q=E(0)$, $F_{\max}=\max_SF$, $F_*=\max_{\{D=Q\}}F$ and $D_{\mathrm{top}}=\max_{\{F=F_{\max}\}}D$. All these maxima are attained and $F_*,Q>0$. At distinct parameters $0\le\lambda_0<\lambda_1$, for any maximizing sources $Y_i$ at $\lambda_i$, write $\delta=F(Y_1)-F(Y_0)$ and $A=D(Y_0)-D(Y_1)$. Then $\delta\ge0$ and $\lambda_0\delta\le A\le\lambda_1\delta$. Every positive-parameter maximizer obeys $F_*\le F(Y)\le F_{\max}$ and $Q-\lambda(F_{\max}-F_*)\le D(Y)\le Q$.

The envelope is convex and $F_{\max}$-Lipschitz. Let $F(\lambda)$ be the largest actual active slope at $\lambda$ and $D(\lambda)=E(\lambda)-\lambda F(\lambda)$ its actual mixed depth. Then $F(\lambda)$ is nondecreasing, right-continuous, equals $E'_+(\lambda)$ and starts at $F_*$. With the right-continuous Lebesgue–Stieltjes convention,
$$
D(a)-D(b)=\int_{(a,b]}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)\quad(0\le a<b),\qquad
\int_{(0,\infty)}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)=Q-D_{\mathrm{top}}\le Q-F_{\max}^d.
$$
The limits at infinity are $F(\lambda)\to F_{\max}$ and $D(\lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{top}}$.

8280d34e5808dfad:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Take distinct maximizers $Y_i=(z_i,x_i)$ at $0\le\lambda_0\le\lambda_1$, with $\lambda_1>0$ and the two bases of equal parity. At equal parameters order the sources by nondecreasing own root. Write $F_i=F(Y_i)$, $D_i=D(Y_i)$, $\delta=F_1-F_0$, $A=D_0-D_1$, $Y_m=(Y_0+Y_1)/2$ and $\Delta=F(Y_m)-(F_0+F_1)/2\ge0$. For every nonvertical depth-attaining cap through $Y_m$, write $H=\{L\ge0\}$ with $L(z,x)=a\cdot(z-z_m)+u\cdot(x-x_m)$ and $\lVert u\rVert=1$. Then $L(Y_1)\ge0$, strictly if $\lambda_0>0$ and $\delta>0$. Set $T_H=\mu\{0\le L<L(Y_1)\}$; this is the exact mass removed by shifting the same cap to $Y_1$, and $D(Y_m)\ge D_1+T_H$. When $\delta>0$,
$$
T_H+\lambda_0\Delta\le A-\lambda_0\delta/2,\qquad
T_H+\lambda_1\Delta\le\lambda_1\delta/2.
$$
If in addition $\lambda_0>0$, then $0\le\Delta<\delta/2$, $F_0<F(Y_m)<F_1$ and $D_1<D(Y_m)<D_0$. For distinct parameters put $\lambda_*=A/\delta$ and $B=E(\lambda_*)-D_0-\lambda_*F_0$. Then
$$
T_H+\lambda_*\Delta\le A/2+B,\qquad
0\le B\le
\frac{\delta(\lambda_*-\lambda_0)(\lambda_1-\lambda_*)}{\lambda_1-\lambda_0}
\le(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)\delta/4.
$$
For equal parameters take $\lambda_*=\lambda_1$ and $B=0$. For $\delta=0$ both endpoint margins, $\Delta,T_H,A$ and $B$ are zero and one can take any $\lambda_*\in[\lambda_0,\lambda_1]$.

Write $s=L(Y_1)$ and suppose the endpoint fiber contains a centered ball of radius $r>0$. For $\kappa_j$ the unit $j$-ball volume, $\kappa_0=1$, one has
$$
T_H\ge \kappa_{d-1}\int_0^{\min(s,r)}(r^2-t^2)^{(d-1)/2}\,dt
\ge c_r\min(s,r/2),\qquad c_r=\kappa_{d-1}(\sqrt3 r/2)^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ the integral expression is $\min(s,r)$. An available radius is $r=F_1^d/(\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1})$ for $R=\operatorname{diam}C_{z_1}$. If $T_H\le\epsilon<c_r r/2$, then $|a\cdot(z_1-z_0)+u\cdot(x_1-x_0)|\le2\epsilon/c_r$. One can choose a common positive radius from the body's maximum fiber diameter and the positive slope floor $F_*$.

For a finite chain of selected sources at nondecreasing positive parameters $\lambda_j$, order equal-parameter sources by their own roots and assume successive bases have equal parity. Let $(T_j,\Delta_j,\lambda_{*,j})$ denote these quantities for each edge, and set $\eta=\max_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)$. Then
$$
\sum_j(T_j+\lambda_{*,j}\Delta_j)\le
\frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac14\sum_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)(F_{j+1}-F_j)
\le \frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac{\eta(F_N-F_0)}4 .
$$
The same upper budget bounds the original measure of the union of the slabs. Along canonical envelope selections the first term is half of the corresponding work integral. Parity subsequences use the successive gaps within each subsequence.

$$

$$

85a041ec649c5375:01.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $h_z=h_{K_z}$.

A finite global-cut action on $C$ uses a nonempty finite index set $I$. For each $i\in I$, its function $\ell_i(u,z)$ is continuous in $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and affine in $z\in\operatorname{aff}(P)$, with $\ell_i(u,z)\ge h_z(u)$ on $P$. Its field $V_i(u,z,x)$ is jointly continuous and nonnegative on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times C$ and convex in $(z,x)$ on $C$ for each fixed $u$. Fields satisfying these assumptions on a larger common convex domain can be restricted to $C$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap
\bigcap_{i\in I,\;u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_i(u,z,x)\le\ell_i(u,z)\}.
$$
Then $C_0=C$, and for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, $C_\varepsilon$ is a nested compact convex body in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}(P)$, its integer fibers $K_z(\varepsilon)=(C_\varepsilon)_z$ have nonempty interior exactly for $z\in P$, and it has no other integer fibers. The deformed fibers satisfy all the same anchored Minkowski inclusions.

At a regular $x\in\partial K_z$, with unique outward unit normal $\nu_z(x)$, define
$$
v_z(x)=\max\Bigl(\{V_i(\nu_z(x),z,x):i\in I,\ \ell_i(\nu_z(x),z)=h_z(\nu_z(x))\}\cup\{0\}\Bigr).
$$
About each fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, let $s_\varepsilon(x)$ be the fractional radial loss, so the new endpoint on the ray through $x$ is $o_z+(1-s_\varepsilon(x))(x-o_z)$. The ratios $s_\varepsilon(x)/\varepsilon$ are uniformly bounded in $x\in\partial K_z$ and, at each regular $x$, tend to $v_z(x)/[\nu_z(x)\cdot(x-o_z)]$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Thus
$$
|K_z|-|K_z(\varepsilon)|=\varepsilon\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$

Let $\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z(\varepsilon)\cap H_z|$, where $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$ for a fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$. On $\partial K_z$, let $\kappa_{z,H}$ be $1$ if $K_z\subseteq H_z$, $0$ if $\operatorname{int}K_z\cap H_z=\varnothing$, and $\mathbf1_{\operatorname{int}H_z}$ otherwise. The first case includes an inside supporting cut and a pure-base cut whose boundary contains the whole fiber. The second includes an outside supporting trace, even when that trace has positive surface measure. Then
$$
\mu_0(H)-\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\varepsilon L(H)+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad L(H)=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\kappa_{z,H}v_z\,dS.
$$
The first total loss is $D=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS$. The remainders can be taken uniformly on each fixed finite cap list. For $d=1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints.

867dbbe22c30cda2:03.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex body in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let a nonvertical plane through $Y=(z_0,x_0)$ cut the interior of its positive-volume own fiber. The full induced section measure agrees with its restriction to positive original $d$-fibers exactly when the original $d$-null fibers contribute no $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ section measure. It is possible for a regular global minimizing cut to have its derivative section centered at the mark but its full intrinsic mixed section centered elsewhere. 86934b651b11f7d5:01.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use planar area on each fiber. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and nonzero spanning vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Set $h_i=h_B(v_i)$, where $h_B(v)=\max_{x\in B}v\cdot x$, and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Assume each of the three closed ambient caps
$$
v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0
$$
attains the actual mixed depth at $(0,y)$, and cuts both $A$ and $K$ properly. The trace on $B$ is the supporting face $F_i=B\cap\{v_i\cdot x=h_i\}$. Let $a_i,k_i$ be the lengths of the $A,K$ cutting chords, respectively, divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $\lambda_i=1/(2a_i+k_i)$ and $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$.

Let $J$ be rotation through a right angle. Give the three cutting lines compatible coordinates by writing $x=y+r v_i/\lVert v_i\rVert^2+uJv_i$, using the appropriate constant $r$ on each line. Let $c_{A,i}$ and $c_i$ be the $u$-centers of the $A,K$ chords. Then $F_i$ contains a $u$-interval of length $a_i$ centered at $-c_{A,i}-(k_i/a_i)c_i$. In particular,
$$
k_i\ge a_i,\qquad
|c_i|\le \frac{a_i(k_i-a_i)}{k_i+2a_i}.
$$
For the single centrally symmetric body $(K-y)\cap(y-K)$, its Minkowski gauge $N$ satisfies
$$
2\lambda_i\le N(Jv_i)\le 6\lambda_i,\qquad
\lambda_i\le3\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j,\qquad
\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}\le\frac34.
$$

86934b651b11f7d5:02.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body and let the finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ cover $A$ and cut it properly. Write $w_i>0$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$ and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. If $\sum_{i:x\in H_i}w_i\ge\tau$ almost everywhere on $A$, then every $p\in A$ satisfies
$$
\sum_i w_i\bigl[dU_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)\sigma_i\bigr]\ge d|A|\tau.
$$
If all singleton-capture regions with indices in a set $E$ are null, a valid $\tau$ is the minimum of the singleton weights $w_i$ for $i\notin E$ and all pair sums $w_i+w_j$ with $i\ne j$, taking the minimum over the combined nonempty list.

86934b651b11f7d5:03.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ for $1\le i\le3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Put $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0$ have common raw mass $Q$ and proper $A,K$ cuts. Write $a=|A|$, $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}|$, and $a_i,k_i$ for the $A,K$ chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $s_i=2a_i+k_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, and
$$
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i,\qquad
\overline L(p)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)}{\Lambda}.
$$

For every $p\in A$, contract $A$ to $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ and keep $K,B$ fixed. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$ there is a $C^1$ meeting point $y(t)$ with $y(0)=y$ and a common cap budget $q(t)$ with $q(0)=Q$, obtained by substituting $y(t)$ for $y$ in the same three ambient caps. They cover the full middle plane, and $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$. If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and the two ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, the new global raw maximum is at most $q(t)$ for all sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Writing $M(t)=|A_t|+|K|+|B|$,
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{M(t)}\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{-M\overline L(p)+2aQ}{M^2}.
$$
In particular the optimized normalized depth strictly decreases if $\overline L(p)>2aQ/M$.

If the three original caps attain the true depth at $(0,y)$ and every singleton-capture region of the $A$ traces is null, then $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$ for every $p\in A$. The derivative above is then at most $(-Ma/2+2aQ)/M^2$. At a budget ratio $Q/M<2/9$ this last expression is less than $-a/(18M)$.

86934b651b11f7d5:05.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, let $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ for $1\le i\le3$ cover $A$, and assume the normals are pairwise linearly independent and all cuts are proper. Write $a=|A|$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$, $a_i=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i$. For arbitrary positive weights $\lambda_i$ put $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $\tau_2=\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i$, and $c_i=(\tau_2-\lambda_i)_+$. The region $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<b_j\}$ is the region captured only by $H_i$. For each $i$ with $r_i=|R_i|>0$, set $C_i=\overline{R_i}$ and, for $j\ne i$, let $\ell$ be the third index and put
$$
\tau_{ij}=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j,\ v_\ell\cdot x\le b_\ell\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert}.
$$
Then $C_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x\le b_j\}$. For every $p\in A$ and $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ the exact right loss is
$$
D_i(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{|R_i\setminus A_t|}{t}
=2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}(b_j-v_j\cdot p)\tau_{ij}\ge0.
$$
It satisfies $D_i(p)\le2r_i$ on $C_i$ and its minimum there is attained and equals
$$
2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
-h_{C_i}\Bigl(-\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr),
$$
where $h_C$ is the support function of $C$.

With null corners omitted, for every $p\in A$,
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-\sum_i c_iD_i(p).
$$
The right side attains its maximum at one common $p\in A$, with value
$$
2a\tau_2-2\sum_i c_ir_i+\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
+h_A\Bigl(-\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr).
$$
If just one positive-area corner $R_j$ has $c_j>0$, every $p\in C_j$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-2(\tau_2-\lambda_j)r_j$. If all deficient corners are null, $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge2a\tau_2$ for every $p\in A$.

In the actual mixed setting of the critical chord-weight theorem, these one-corner and all-deficient-null estimates imply a normalized loss of at least $(a-r_j)/2$ and $a/2$, respectively, after dividing by $\Lambda$. In particular $r_j\le a/9$ gives a normalized loss of at least $4a/9$ at every $p\in C_j$.

If two strictly excluded vertices satisfy the same coordinate bound, there is a feasible variation with strictly positive second derivative. The conclusions permit zero margins at other vertices. $$
\inf_{H\ni y}\frac{|T\cap H|}{|T|}=\min_i d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j .
$$
If $y$ is interior, every minimizing halfspace has boundary through $y$. Its unique strictly included vertex is $v_i$ for an index attaining $\max_j\lambda_j$, and its boundary meets each edge $[v_i,v_j]$, $j\ne i$, at $(1-d\lambda_j)v_i+d\lambda_j v_j$. $$

P_{ij}(c)=f(0)\frac{\phi(c_i)-\phi(c_j)}{c_i-c_j},

870e8284d5328056:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a compact convex body, $K\subset P$ nonempty compact, and $a_1,\ldots,a_N$ fixed unit vectors. At a positive-volume maximum, each genuine cut facet $F_i=L\cap\{a_i\cdot z=b_i\}$ whose relative interior lies in $\operatorname{int}P$ has $p_i\in\operatorname{relint}F_i\cap\operatorname{int}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $b_i=a_i\cdot p_i$. Identical active cuts have one common facet owner.

For any positive-volume $L=L(b)$ in this class, write $A_i=\mathcal H^{n-1}(F_i)$ and $c_i$ for its genuine cut facet areas and centroids. Write $\Gamma_P=\partial L\cap\partial P$, with outward unit normal $n_P(z)$ almost everywhere; integrals on it use $\mathcal H^{n-1}$. For $q\in\operatorname{int}L$,
$$
\sum_i A_i a_i+\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P=0,\qquad
\sum_i A_i a_i(c_i-q)^{\mathsf T}+\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P(z)(z-q)^{\mathsf T}=|L|I_n.
$$
In particular, with $\Phi_P(q)=\int_{\Gamma_P}(z-q)\cdot n_P(z)$,
$$
n|L|=\sum_i A_i(b_i-a_i\cdot q)+\Phi_P(q).
$$
All the scalar contributions are nonnegative; $\Phi_P(q)>0$ if $\Gamma_P$ has positive surface measure. At a maximum each scalar offset can be replaced by $a_i\cdot p_i$, without a centroid identity.

Moving only genuine cut planes by $b_i(t)=b_i+t(b_i-a_i\cdot q)$, keeping $P$ fixed, gives volume derivative $n|L|-\Phi_P(q)$. The outward path is infeasible for interior lattice exclusion at a maximum having a genuine facet. More generally, physically move the genuine planes by $z\mapsto z+t(Bz+v)$ for fixed $B,v$, still clipping to fixed $P$ and keeping any other planes fixed. The volume derivative is
$$
\sum_i A_i a_i\cdot(Bc_i+v)=|L|\operatorname{tr}B-\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P(z)\cdot(Bz+v).

This affine motion does not assert admissibility in the fixed-normal optimization. A cut coincident with an inherited positive-area face is counted only in $\Gamma_P$; the formulas move no such cut.

D=\frac{(1-p)^2}{1-x},\quad w=1+a,\quad v=p+z.
$$

$$

$$

\quad

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
Call the family strictly compatible if for each extreme point $\lambda$ of each nonempty $E_q$, the Minkowski combination $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. Under this condition there is a common $\kappa>0$ such that $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p+\kappa B_d\subseteq K_q$ for every such extreme point, where $B_d$ is the closed unit ball. 97eab0f821e54041:02.statement:

Fix $h$ with $u\cdot h>0$. Then $K(t)=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{v+th\})$ has added volume $\Delta(t)=|K(t)|-|K|>0$ for $t>0$. The function $\Delta$ is continuous and strictly increasing, with $\Delta(0)=0$, and $\sup_{x\in K(t)\setminus K}\lVert x-v\rVert\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$. In particular each sufficiently small prescribed positive added volume has a unique small positive parameter.

For a finite list of distinct points $v_i$ with these hypotheses and corresponding directions $h_i$, write $a_i=v_i+t_i h_i$. For all sufficiently small positive $t_i$ one has the exact disjoint union
$$
\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i:i\})\setminus K
=\bigsqcup_i\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i\})\setminus K\bigr).
$$

97eab0f821e54041:03.statement:

Assume $v_i$ has a unique unit supporting normal $u_i$ in $K_{p_i}$, whose support face is $\{v_i\}$, and fix $h_i$ with $u_i\cdot h_i>0$. For each fixed real vector $\xi=(\xi_i)$ and every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual convex body $C_\varepsilon$ with nonempty integer fibers of positive volume exactly at $P$, converging fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to $C$. The signed measure $\mu_{C_\varepsilon}-\mu_C$ is a sum of signed restrictions of mixed volume to pairwise disjoint regions shrinking to the respective $w_i$, each of exact signed mass $\varepsilon\xi_i$. In particular $M_\varepsilon=M+\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i$. For every fixed finite family of closed halfspaces $H$ whose boundaries avoid all $w_i$, one has
$$
\mu_{C_\varepsilon}(H)-\mu_C(H)=\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i\mathbf1_H(w_i)
$$
for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. The same identity holds for parallel threshold changes of order $O(\varepsilon)$, comparing the two measures at the same shifted threshold and keeping the old indicators on the right.

97eab0f821e54041:04.statement:
In the setting of the exact signed local mass theorem, write $D(C)$ for the maximum over the measured set of the infimum of normalized $\mu_C$-mass of closed ambient halfspaces containing the point. $$

\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1,\qquad \sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0,\quad \rho_{pj}>0,
$$

Assume every selected cap has old mass $Q$, its boundary avoids every selected $w_i$, and its old threshold function satisfies $F_{pj}(b_{pj}+s)=Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ with $S_{pj}>0$. a21ff89aef880b49:01.statement:
For integers $k,m\ge1$, let $X_k\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ and $Y_m\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$. Let $E_+,E_-$ be unit-mean exponentials, with all four variables independent. For $p\in[0,1]$ and $b=(k+p-1)/m\in[0,1]$, set
$$
V_{k,m,p}=X_k+pE_+-E_--bY_m,\qquad
G_{k,p}=\Pr(X_k+pE_+\ge E_-+k+p-1).
$$
The variance of $V_{k,m,p}$ is $\sigma^2=k+p^2+1+mb^2$ and lies in $[k+1,2(k+1)]$. As $k\to\infty$, the probability $\Pr(V_{k,m,p}\ge0)$ tends to $1/2$ uniformly over the admissible $m,p$. For fixed $k$, if $m_j\to\infty$ and $p_j\to p\in[0,1]$ along admissible parameters, then $\Pr(V_{k,m_j,p_j}\ge0)\to G_{k,p}$.

where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Here $q$ ranges over the finite nonnegative integers for which the coefficient constraints are feasible. For $k\ge2$, the fixed-$q$ minimum is
$$
A_{k,q}=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\frac{k-1}{q}\,G\right),
\qquad G\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)
$$
with $G$ independent. These minima strictly decrease as $q$ increases and converge to
$$
G_k=\Pr(X\ge E_0+k-1)
=e^{-(k-1)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{(k-1)^j}{j!}\left(1-2^{-(k-j)}\right).
$$
Thus the infimum over all finite $q$ and all feasible $b$ is $G_k$, and $P_k(b)>G_k$ for every such $b$ when $k\ge2$. In particular $G_2=5/(4e)$ and $G_3=27/(8e^2)$. When $k=1$ every residual coefficient is zero, and $P_1(b)=G_1=1/2$, including the empty list.

a754d14c81eb6c11:01.statement:
Let a planar compact convex body have exactly $N$ nonempty sampled integer fibers, at consecutive sites. Suppose all have positive length, with affine midpoint heights and affine widths. Use the sum of fiber lengths as mass, and closed ambient halfspaces for depth. Subtract the affine center graph, reverse the base when needed, and for a nonconstant width profile divide by its positive increment. Write the resulting lengths as $w_i=q+i$ for $0\le i<N$, with $q>0$. At base $j$ the midpoint attains the largest raw depth in its interval, namely
$$
D_j(q)=\min\left\{\sum_{i<j}w_i+w_j/2,\ \sum_{i>j}w_i+w_j/2,\ T_{j,k}(q)\ (k\ne j)\right\},
$$
where every sum uses $0,\ldots,N-1$ and
$$
T_{j,k}(q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i<k}\min\{q+i,(k-i)(q+j)/(2(k-j))\},&k>j,\\
\displaystyle\sum_{i>k}\min\{q+i,(i-k)(q+j)/(2(j-k))\},&k<j.
\end{cases}
$$
Each $D_j$ is concave and piecewise affine with rational coefficients. The normalized maximum $\max_j D_j/[Nq+N(N-1)/2]$ is piecewise linear-fractional with finitely many rational breakpoints and is monotone or constant on each piece. For constant positive widths the normalized maximum is $1/2$ for odd $N$ and $(N-1)/(2N)$ for even $N$.

a779c844eb8df3e4:02.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^r$, $r\ge1$, be a full-rank lattice of covolume $v$. Let $f\colon\mathbb R^r\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded and measurable with compact support and convex strict superlevels $\{f>t\}$ for all $t>0$. Put $T=\sum_{p\in a+L}f(p)>0$ and $M=\int_{\mathbb R^r}f$. There is an affine hyperplane $E$ spanned by $r$ affinely independent coset points such that
$$
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)\le r!M/v,\qquad
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\cap E}f(p)\ge (T-r!M/v)_+,
$$
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$. If the positive sample set has full affine rank, take $E$ from the greedy rule which repeatedly chooses a highest-valued sample outside the previously selected affine span, starting with a highest-valued sample and stopping at $r$ points. For $b=\max_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)>0$ the same $E$ satisfies
$$
M\ge \frac{v}{r!}\left[\sum_{p\in a+L}\min(f(p),b)-rb\right].
$$
If the positive sample set has smaller rank, one can choose $E$ containing all positive samples.

For a compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$, $s\ge1$, these conclusions apply to $f(u)=\operatorname{vol}_s(Q_u)$ with $M=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q)$, provided $T>0$. They apply separately to each closed halfspace intersection of $Q$ with positive sampled mass. In the counting case $s=0$, take $f=\mathbf 1_Q$ for compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r$. The coefficient $r!$ in the outside-mass bound is sharp for every $r\ge1$ and $s\ge0$, including full-dimensional bodies whose nonempty sampled fibers all have positive mass.

For s=0 use f=1_Q. The coefficient r! is sharp for every r,s in these classes, already for a unimodular simplex times any positive s-body (or the simplex alone for s=0).

a779c844eb8df3e4:05.statement:
Let $k\ge0$ and $r,s\ge1$ be integers, let $C\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, and sample at $(z,u)\in\mathbb Z^k\times(a+L)$, where $L$ has full rank and covolume $v$ in $\mathbb R^r$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^k$ let $Q_z=\{(u,x):(z,u,x)\in C\}$, $T_z=\sum_{u\in a+L}\operatorname{vol}_s((Q_z)_u)$, and $M_z=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q_z)$. Put $T=\sum_z T_z>0$ and $M=\sum_z M_z$ over all coarse integer slices. Let $J\ge1$ be any upper bound on the number of coarse levels with $T_z>0$.

Assume for each $1\le t\le r-1$ that every full-dimensional compact convex body in $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ with positive sampled mass on $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$ has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then $C$ has a sampled point for which every containing closed halfspace has sampled mass, divided by $T$, at least
$$
\frac{\Gamma_s}{J\,2^{r-1}}\left(1-\frac{r!M}{vT}\right)_+.
$$
In particular $J\le2^k$ and $M/(vT)\le1/(2r!)$ imply normalized depth at least $\Gamma_s/2^{k+r}$. For $k=0$ take $J=1$ to obtain the one-level estimate. For $r=1$ all these conclusions are unconditional, and the point can be chosen as the centroid of an actual largest-volume sampled fiber of $C$.
