a779c844eb8df3e4:06.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, with $s\ge1$, and let $a+L$ be a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$. Let $F\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be an affine subspace. Take $P$ to consist of either all the lattice bases in $F$ with nonempty $Q$-fibers or all the lattice bases in $F$ with positive $s$-volume $Q$-fibers. Assume the sum $T_P$ of the retained fiber volumes is positive. Put $A=\operatorname{aff}P$, $t=\dim A$, and
$$
Q_P=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times Q_p).
$$
For every $p\in(a+L)\cap A$ the fiber $(Q_P)_p$ equals $Q_p$ if $p\in P$ and is empty otherwise. The hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body in $A\times\mathbb R^s$. For any $p_0\in P$, the lattice there is $p_0+(L\cap(A-p_0))$, whose difference lattice is saturated in $L$ and has rank $t$. A lattice basis gives an affine identification with $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ and sample lattice $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$, preserving every fiber volume and the raw halfspace depth within the retained source. For every retained candidate, its raw depth in the original source is at least its retained raw depth. The same comparison holds if $Q$ is a fixed coarse slice of a larger original source.

For $t>0$, assume the sharp mixed-integer bound in dimensions $(t,s)$, namely that every full-dimensional compact convex body of positive sampled mass in those dimensions has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then some retained point has raw depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s T_P$ in the original source. At $t=0$ the same conclusion holds unconditionally.

$$

a9fd9b4c832ea48f:06.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a finite nonzero capacity measure on a compact subset of a Euclidean physical space, let $L_i$ be a finite list of affine margins, and set $W_\theta=\sum_i\theta_i\mathbf1_{\{L_i\ge0\}}$ for $\theta_i\ge0$. Assume there is a physical martingale from $\mu_\theta$ to $\eta$ and write $J_i=\int[L_i]_+\,d(\eta-\mu_\theta)$. The following conditions are equivalent.
- $\sum_i\theta_iJ_i=0$.
- $J_i=0$ for every active $i$.
- $\mu_\theta=\eta$.
- Every physical martingale between the two measures is concentrated on the identity.

The equivalence also holds for martingales required to preserve a given measurable label when at least one such martingale exists and the two measures are understood on the labelled space with $\mu_\theta=(W_\theta/\beta)\eta$. Identity here refers to the full physical coordinate.

external_dependencies: Weak compactness of probability measures on a compact metric space, and continuity of marginal pushforward under weak convergence.
Finite-dimensional linear programming strong duality for the finite primal and dual.
aadf3a80572ef300:01.reason: The barycentric density constructions in 793210f8a4be3647 produce a generally random barycenter from selected measures, not a coupling of all the fixed marginals with zero cost at a given point. The one-measure allocation in 81238d80ed62466f does not impose the full joint marginal constraints. The new compact feasibility test, exact unrestricted-potential atomic dual and two-sided quantization error follow directly from compactness and finite LP strong duality; no accepted premise is used.
aadf3a80572ef300:01.statement:
For $j=1,\ldots,m$ with $m\ge1$, let $K_j\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact sets, $\mu_j$ probability measures on $K_j$, and $\lambda_j>0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$. For $y\in\mathbb R^d$, the minimum $D_y$ of $\int|\sum_j\lambda_jx_j-y|^2\,d\gamma$ over couplings of the prescribed $\mu_j$ is attained and vanishes exactly when one coupling has constant barycenter $y$ almost surely. For finitely supported atomic laws $\mu_j=\sum_k w_{jk}\delta_{x_{jk}}$ the minimization is a finite linear program with nonnegative tuple masses and equality constraints for the specified marginals. Its dual is
$$
\max_{f}\sum_{j,k}w_{jk}f_{jk}
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_jf_{j,k_j}\le\left|\sum_j\lambda_j x_{j,k_j}-y\right|^2
\quad\text{for every tuple }(k_j),
$$
where the potentials $f_{jk}$ are unrestricted. Partitioning each $K_j$ into finitely many Borel cells and replacing each cell by a representative with its original mass changes the optimum by at most the maximum oscillation of the cost over product cells. In particular, cells of vanishing maximum diameter give converging values, and a finite dual bound larger than that oscillation certifies $D_y>0$.

For two equal-weight inputs this coupling exists exactly when $\mu_2=(x\mapsto2y-x)_\#\mu_1$. For $d+1$ equal-weight uniform inputs on $K_j=a_j+rT$, where $T$ is a full-dimensional simplex of centroid zero, $r>0$ and $\sum_ja_j=(d+1)y$, such a coupling exists. In the lifted setting it has barycenter $(p,y)$ whenever the attached bases obey $\sum_j\lambda_j z_j=p$.

aadf3a80572ef300:02.statement:
Fix a physical point $Y=(p,y)$ and a finite collection of tuple types, each with positive coefficients $\lambda_j$ summing to one and fixed bases satisfying $\sum_j\lambda_jz_j=p$. A tuple of type $(z_j,\lambda_j)_j$ is admissible if $\sum_j\lambda_jx_j=y$. Suppose the prescribed probability laws at the distinct bases of one type have an admissible coupling. For every containing closed halfspace $H$ and every nonnegative Borel profile $\Psi_H$ that equals one on $H$, the sum of the marginal profile integrals is at least one. For uniform laws on distinct original fibers of volumes $V_j>0$, the original raw cap credit on their union is at least $\min_j V_j$, including every base tilt.

For finitely supported atomic source measures, index the atoms by $a$ and let $w_a\ge0$ be their masses. Let $e$ run over all admissible atomic tuples of the given types, and let $m_{ae}$ count occurrences of atom $a$ in $e$. A simultaneous lower bound on every original containing cap is the exact packing optimum
$$
\max_{\gamma\ge0}\left\lbrace \sum_e\gamma_e:\ \sum_e m_{ae}\gamma_e\le w_a\text{ for all }a\right\rbrace
=\min_{f\ge0}\left\lbrace \sum_a w_a f_a:\ \sum_a m_{ae} f_a\ge1\text{ for all }e\right\rbrace .
$$
The same lower-bound principle holds for any finite family of finite measures on admissible continuous tuple sets, if the summed use of each original source measure, with multiplicities, is dominated by that source measure.

Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)\rbrace$ and use the actual product $[-1,1]\times T$ with its three integer fibers and original mixed area. For $h>0$, define the outward-smoothed capture at a mark $(p,y)$ with oblique cap direction $(a,u)$, $u\ne0$, by integrating

\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},
$$

For all sufficiently small positive $h$, the unique deepest mark for this smoothed depth is $(0,0)$. abd48c3f5afc0115:01.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty complete base in an affine lattice, and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be positive compact convex fibers with the anchored Minkowski inclusions $\sum_j\lambda_j K_{p_j}\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_j\lambda_jp_j=p\in P$ for convex weights. Let $C$ be the hull of their lifts, with real fibers $C_z$, and let $\mu$ be the sum of their $d$-volumes, with total $M$. Take $\ell>0$ continuous and concave on $\operatorname{conv}P$, $\varepsilon>0$, and a norm $\Gamma$ on continuous covectors. Put $f(z,y)=(\ell(z)E_{C_z}(y)/M)^{1/(d+1)}$, where $E_K(y)$ is the marked projective energy $\inf_b\int_K(1+b\cdot(X-y))^{-d-1}\,dX$ over denominators positive throughout $K$, extended by zero on own-fiber boundaries.

At a real mark $w=(p,y)\in C$, define its raw buffered depth as the minimum of its closed pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(p)$ for weights $|K_z|$ and the infimum of the masses of all caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(w)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0.
$$
The whole-base trace is allowed. Write $Q$ for the supremum at sampled marks and assume $0<Q<M$. Let $I$ be its deepest bases, and set $J=\{p\in I:b_{\rm base}(p)>Q\}$ and $A=I\setminus J$. The maximum is attained and its real superlevel is convex, so $I=P\cap\operatorname{conv}I$. Every deepest mark is own-interior. At every deepest mark in $A$ all own buffered traces are full. At every deepest mark in $J$ a nonvertical attaining cap exists and every such cap has a proper own trace.

Suppose $r=\sum_j\lambda_jp_j\in J$, with $\lambda_j>0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, $p_j\in I$. Choose any deepest marks $w_j=(p_j,y_j)$, and set $w_r=\sum_j\lambda_j w_j=(r,y_r)$. Every $p_j$ lies in $J$. More precisely, any active nonvertical cap at $w_r$ is the same active cap at each $w_j$. For one convex body $K_*$ containing zero in its interior, the whole fibers satisfy $K_{p_j}=y_j+\ell(p_j)K_*$ and $K_r=y_r+\ell(r)K_*$. Also $\ell(r)=\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(p_j)$ and $f(w_j)/\ell(p_j)=f(w_r)/\ell(r)>0$. After these rescalings the cap has the identical proper trace at every input and the target.

ace4ff0d14f43769:4.statement:
Let $m,s\ge1$ be integers, let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^s$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c$. Put $\gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, $Q_m=\{p\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_i |p_i|\le1\}$, $g(p)=(1+\sum_i p_i)/2$, and
$$
C=\{(p,u,x)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s:
p\in Q_m,\ |u-g(p)|\le\varepsilon,\ x\in K\}.
$$
The body $C$ is full-dimensional. The coarse rule requires $p\in\mathbb Z^m$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm c}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R^{1+s})$ and measure $\mathcal H_{s+1}|_{S_{\mathrm c}}$. The fine rule additionally requires $u\in\mathbb Z$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm f}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\times\mathbb R^s)$ and measure $\mathcal H_s|_{S_{\mathrm f}}$. For each rule normalize its measure by its own total mass. Define its maximum depth as the maximum over its admissible set of the infimum of normalized mass of all closed ambient halfspaces containing the point.

The coarse rule has $2m+1$ fibers of mass $2\varepsilon V$ and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm c}=\gamma_s$, attained at $(0,1/2,c)$. The fine rule has exactly $2m$ fibers of mass $V$, at $(e_i,1)$ and $(-e_i,0)$ for $1\le i\le m$, and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm f}=\gamma_s/(2m)$, attained at the centroid of each fiber. The ambient normalized laws are mutually singular. After projection to $(p,x)$, their total variation distance, defined by the supremum over measurable sets, is exactly $1/(2m+1)$, the coarse probability of the omitted base $p=0$.

The affine span of the fine bases has dimension $m$. Its integer points project bijectively to the odd-sum coset of the index-two even-sum sublattice of $\mathbb Z^m$. The fine mixed hull is $\operatorname{conv}(S_{\mathrm f})=\{(p,g(p),x):p\in Q_m,\ x\in K\}$ and has codimension one in $C$. Replacing $C$ by this hull preserves the fine set and fine measure and reduces the original coarse $\mathcal H_{s+1}$ mass to zero.

Thus for fixed $s$ and $\varepsilon$, a single added integer condition of projected index two gives $D_{\mathrm f}/D_{\mathrm c}=1/(2m)\to0$ with projected total variation tending to zero. In particular there is no positive dimension-independent retention factor for this comparison, even when the omitted coarse base marginal mass is arbitrarily small.

ace6d0d9c40d2c09:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $\Pi_j=\{x:u_j\cdot x=0\}$ be finitely many pairwise distinct unoriented hyperplanes with $u_j\ne0$. Define $q_j(K)=|K\cap\{u_j\cdot x\ge0\}|$ and $\sigma_j(K)=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap\Pi_j)/\lVert u_j\rVert$. Fix $i$ and suppose there is $P\in\partial K\cap\Pi_i$ whose union of all exposed faces containing $P$ misses every $\Pi_j$ with $j\ne i$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is a convex body $K_\varepsilon$ containing $0$ in its interior and tending to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, with
$$
|K_\varepsilon|=|K|,\quad q_i(K_\varepsilon)<q_i(K),\quad
\sigma_i(K_\varepsilon)>\sigma_i(K),
$$
with every other cap volume unchanged and every other central section unchanged as a set. If there are at least two planes, $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$ decreases strictly and every other weight increases. The hypothesis on $P$ always holds if $K$ is strictly convex.

Consequently, if there are at least two planes, in a fixed-volume class containing only constraints of the form $F(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\le c$ with coordinatewise nondecreasing $F$, among bodies with $0$ interior, at a local minimum of $\lambda_i$ every $P\in\partial K\cap\Pi_i$ outside the other planes must belong to a nontrivial exposed face meeting another plane. At a local minimum of $\min_j\lambda_j$ this holds for every index attaining the minimum. In the plane this applies to both endpoints of each relevant chord.

$$
E_{K_p}(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ \forall x\in K_p}\int_{K_p}[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
For each $b\in\mathbb R^n$ and unit continuous $u$, define the rightmost raw $Q$ quantile $\tau_{b,u}=\sup\{t:\mu\{b\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge t\}\ge Q\}$ and $c_{b,u}=\tau_{b,u}-b\cdot p-u\cdot y\ge0$. Then
$$
D_p-y=\bigcap_{b,u}\{h:u\cdot h\le c_{b,u}\}.
$$
The active indices $c_{b,u}=0$ are precisely the actual nonvertical minimizing caps through $(p,y)$ and have proper own sections. With the outward normal cone convention,
$$
y\in\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in D_p}E_{K_p}(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\in N_{D_p}(y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(a,0)\in\overline{\operatorname{cone}}\{(u,c_{b,u}):b\in\mathbb R^n,\ \|u\|=1\}.
$$
In particular an interior point of $D_p$ maximizes energy only at the own-fiber centroid; a singleton places no restriction on the optimizer vector.

The cone condition is equivalent to certificates with at most $d+1$ actual quantile caps for every $\varepsilon>0$:
$$

\left\|a-\sum_j\lambda_j u_j\right\|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
0\le\sum_j\lambda_j c_j\le\varepsilon.
$$
If a sequence of certificates with $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ has bounded total multiplier weight, then $a$ is a nonnegative combination of at most $d$ genuine critical normals. A Slater ball in $D_p$ ensures this boundedness. A finite local definition of $D_p$ by actual quantile inequalities also gives the exact representation. Conversely, if genuine critical continuous normals positively span $\mathbb R^d$, then $D_p=\{y\}$ and every vector has such an exact representation.

ad88f967d6335089:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, and let $P$ be all its nonempty integer-fiber bases. Assume each fiber is full-dimensional and an ambient cap through $(z_0,x_0)$, $z_0\in P$, with continuous normal $u\ne0$, cuts every fiber properly. Suppose its raw mass is a local minimum under variation of the real base-normal coefficient with $u$ fixed. If its actual captured fibers are $K_z=a_zD+v_z$ with $|D|_d=1$ and $a_z>0$, then $\sum_{z\in P}a_z^{d-1}(z-z_0)=0$, so $z_0\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$.

If the roots are affine on $P$, write $a_0=a_{z_0}$, $N=|P|$, $B=\sum_za_z^d$, $E=\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$, and let $\ell\in E$ satisfy $a_z=a_0+\ell\cdot(z-z_0)$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
B&=a_0\sum_z a_z^{d-1}\le Na_0^d,\\
Na_0^d-B
&=\sum_z(a_0-a_z)^2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)a_0^{d-2-j}a_z^j.
\end{aligned}
$$
Equality holds exactly when all $a_z=a_0$. The slope $\ell$ is the unique minimizer of $\sum_z[a_0+\eta\cdot(z-z_0)]^d$ over $\eta\in E$ with all roots positive, and a minimizer over the closure with all roots nonnegative. For the actual whole-fiber roots $r_z=|C_z|_d^{1/d}$, one has the first-moment bound $\sum_z(a_z^d/B)(r_z/a_z)\le r_{z_0}/a_0$.

If the original cap is locally minimizing under joint variation of the base and continuous normal and both $a_z$ and $v_z$ are affine on $P$, then $x_0$ is the ordinary centroid of its own cutting section.

ad88f967d6335089:03.reason: The finite linear equation $\Sigma\ell=\alpha(z_0-\bar z)$ gives the explicit positive admissibility region and exact $d=2$ value beyond the general stationary budget. The proof assumes only an affine positive array and its balance. The eight-site mass is algebraic here, independently of any proof of global optimality.
ad88f967d6335089:03.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite, $z_0\in P$, and $a_z>0$ affine on $P$ with $\sum_z(z-z_0)a_z=0$. Write $N=|P|$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_z z$, $E=\operatorname{span}(P-\bar z)$, $\Sigma=N^{-1}\sum_z(z-\bar z)(z-\bar z)^{\mathsf T}$ on $E$, $w=z_0-\bar z$, and $\Delta=w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}w$. For a singleton take $\Delta=0$ and omit the inverse term. With $\alpha=N^{-1}\sum_z a_z$ and $a_0=a_{z_0}$,
$$
a_z=\alpha[1+w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(z-\bar z)],\qquad
a_0=\alpha(1+\Delta),\qquad
\sum_z a_z^2=\frac{Na_0^2}{1+\Delta}.
$$
Conversely the displayed affine array for any $\alpha>0$ satisfies the balance and is admissible exactly when all brackets are positive. For $P=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$, $N\ge2$, this is equivalent to $|z_0-\bar z|<(N+1)/6$. At $N=2m,z_0=m-1$, feasibility is equivalent to $m\ge2$, and $\sum_z a_z^2=2ma_0^2(4m^2-1)/(4m^2+2)$. For $a_0^2=4/9$ the latter mass is $4m(4m^2-1)/(9(2m^2+1))$, equal to $112/33$ when $m=4$.

$$
M(b+\delta b)=\sum_z[a_z+h^{-1}\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)]^d.

ae6af582a4950210:02.statement:
Let $A_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite family of nonempty compact convex sets with positive weights $w_i$, and assume at least one member $A_*$ has nonempty interior. Using the envelopes $P_U(A_i)$ in the preceding definition, the objective $F(U)=\sum_i w_i|P_U(A_i)|$ attains a minimum over all simplex orientations. On the sublevel $F(U)\le M$, a member with an inball $B(x_i,\rho_i)$ has every envelope vertex $v$ bounded by
$$
\|v-x_i\|\le dM/(w_i\kappa_{d-1}\rho_i^{d-1}),
$$

$$
(w_*|A_i|/M)^{1/d}\le r_i\le (M/(w_i|A_*|))^{1/d}.

$$
G_{Hz}=[h_{K_z}(u)-\tau_z]T_{Hz},\qquad D_{Hz}=d q_{Hz}-G_{Hz}.

$$

\qquad (a,u)\ne(0,0).

b2439018eaa1681d:01.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base with compatible compact convex bodies $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Write $S=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_z$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and $dm=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$, with $M=m(S)$ and $dP_0=dm/M$. Let $L,U>0$ be continuous concave on $C$, with $\int\log L\,dP_0=\int\log U\,dP_0=0$. Suppose finitely many marks $Y_i\in C$, weights $\sigma_i>0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$, and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i}{L_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
$$
If $U(Y_i)/L_i\le e^\delta$ for every $i$, where $\delta\ge0$, then $b=\int(U/L)\,dP_0$ lies in $[1,e^\delta]$,
$$
D\bigl(P_0\,\big\|\,(U/(bL))P_0\bigr)=\log b,\qquad
\int_S |U-L|\,dm
\le M\max_S L\bigl(e^\delta\sqrt{2\delta}+e^\delta-1\bigr).
$$

On any $K_z$, write $B_z=\max_{K_z}U+\max_{K_z}L$, suppressing the base coordinate, and let $\omega_d$ be the unit $d$-ball volume. For every $\varrho>0$ with nonempty core,
$$
\sup_{\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K_z)\ge\varrho}|U(z,x)-L(z,x)|
\le \left(\frac{2\cdot 4^d B_z^d}{\omega_d\varrho^d}\int_{K_z}|U-L|\,dX\right)^{1/(d+1)},\qquad
\max_{K_z}U\le\frac{(d+1)M\max_S L}{|K_z|}e^\delta .
$$
The first estimate on the core applies to any two nonnegative continuous concave functions on a full-dimensional compact convex body, with the zero case $B_z=0$ understood directly. For bounded $\delta$, the certificate thus gives the modulus $O(\delta^{1/[2(d+1)]})$ on any fixed positive-radius core.

Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty and $d\ge1$. On this fixed base let compact convex bodies $K_{j,z}$ with nonempty interiors converge in Hausdorff distance, for each $z$, to a compact convex body $K_z$ with nonempty interior. Use the sampled volume $dm_j=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_{j,z}}$, mass $M_j$, fiber centroids $g_{j,z}$ and pooled covariance
$$
\Sigma_j=M_j^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_{j,z}}(X-g_{j,z})(X-g_{j,z})^{\mathsf T}\,dX,
$$
and their limiting versions $dm,M,\Sigma$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $N=d+1$. For any positive continuous concave $U$ on $C_j$ with $\int_{S_j}\log U\,dm_j/M_j=0$, define the raw buffered depth at a mark $(p,y)\in S_j$ as the infimum of the masses of closed pure-base caps containing $p$ and of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)+\varepsilon\bigl(U(p,y)E_{K_{j,p}}(y)/M_j\bigr)^{1/N}
\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_j u}\ge0,\qquad u\ne0 .
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is marked projective energy with its zero boundary value, the infimum of $\int_K[1+b\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over denominators strictly positive on $K$ at interior marks. Allow the whole-base trace, in particular in base rank zero. Let $Q_j(U)$ be the maximum raw depth on $S_j$, and define $Q(L)$ on the limit family in the same way.

Assume $L>0$ is continuous and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Suppose there are finitely many marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)\in S$, positive weights $\sigma_i$ summing to one, and probabilities $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfying
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML).
$$
Every $Y_i$ is assumed to have maximal raw depth $Q=Q(L)$, strictly below its own pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(p_i)$. If $U_j$ are admissible parameters with $Q_j(U_j)\le\inf_U Q_j(U)+o(1)$, then $U_j(z,\cdot)\to L(z,\cdot)$ uniformly on every compact subset of $\operatorname{int}K_z$ at the same coordinates. The zero extensions of $U_j$ and, separately, of $\log U_j$ on the sampled fibers converge in mixed $L^1$ to the corresponding zero extensions of $L$ and $\log L$. The energy-weighted factors $(U_j(z,y)E_{K_{j,z}}(y)/M_j)^{1/N}$ converge uniformly on the sampled coordinate spaces after zero extension, and so do the actual physical shifts uniformly in Euclidean unit continuous normals. Finally $Q_j(U_j)\to Q$ and $Q_j(U_j)/M_j\to Q/M$.

Each piece is strictly inside its own cap and strictly outside every other cap. Put $V_i=|A_i|$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}\{z_i:i\in I\}$ and
$$
f_I(z)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i V_i^{1/d}:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i z_i=z\right\}.

$$
|I|\tau M\ge\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n}\max\left(f_I(z)^d,\ \sum_{i\in I:z_i=z}V_i\right).
$$

$$
2\tau M\ge V_i+V_j+\left(\frac{V_i^{1/d}+V_j^{1/d}}2\right)^d .

For $k$ distinct same-parity bases with equal exclusive volumes $V$, it gives $V\le k\tau M/(2k-1)$.

b2bd978e973816b6:01.statement:
Let integers $m\ge k\ge2$ and $0<p<1$ be given. Let $X,Y,E_+,E_-$ be independent, with $X\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$, $Y\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$, and $E_\pm\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$. Write
$$
q=k-1,\quad c=1-p,\quad b=\frac{q+p}{m},\quad
A=q+(m+1)p,\quad B=m+p+q,\quad
D=qp^2+\bigl[(k+1)m+k^2-k+2\bigr]p+q(m+k+1).
$$
Set $P(p)=\Pr(X+pE_+\ge E_-+bY)$ and $Z=(X-E_-)/(E_++Y)$. Then
$$
f_Z(z)=\frac{m+1}{2^k}
\begin{cases}
(1-z)^{-m-2}, & z<0,\\[2pt]
\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^q 2^j\binom{m+j+1}{j}\frac{z^j}{(1+z)^{m+j+2}}, & z\ge0 .
\end{cases}
$$
The probability and its derivative are
$$
P(p)=\Pr(Z\ge b)+\int_{-p}^b\left(\frac{p+z}{p+b}\right)^m f_Z(z)\,dz,\qquad
P'(p)=\frac{J(p)}{(p+b)^{m+1}},
$$
where $J(p)=\int_{-p}^b(p+z)^{m-1}[q-(m+1)z]f_Z(z)\,dz$. Put
$$
S(t)=\sum_{j=0}^q2^j\binom{m+j+1}{j}(t-p)^jc^{q-j}.
$$
Let $Q$ be the unique polynomial with $(t^mQ(t))'=t^{m-1}[A-(m+k)t]S(t)$, where the prime in this equation is with respect to $t$. Then
$$
J(p)=\frac{(m+1)(A/B)^mQ(A/B)}{2^k c^{k+1}}
     +\frac{(-1)^k p^{m+k}D}{m c^{k+1}(1+p)^2}.
$$

$$

$$
W_i:=c_i+r_i S_i=\sum_z\eta_z p_{zi},\qquad
Z_i+r_i Z_i^s=\sum_z\eta_z z p_{zi},
$$

$$
X_i+r_i X_i^s-\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}=\Psi_i u_i.
$$

$$
\sum_i W_i u_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i u_i(Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T=0,\qquad
\sum_i W_i=\sum_z\eta_z,\qquad

$$

\ge \beta_j-(v_j\cdot u)b,

$$
V_u(s)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\mu\{u\cdot x+a\cdot(z-j)\ge s\}.

$$

At $t=D_j$, $J_t(u)$ is the mean of the full law.

For every sufficiently close array of actual convex fibers $J_0,\ldots,J_{m-1}$ and nearby caps with the same total $mV$ and respective exact cap masses $V,V$, every $J_j$ has volume $V$ and
$$
J_j=(1-j/(m-1))J_0+(j/(m-1))J_{m-1},\qquad 1\le j\le m-2 .
$$
In particular every directional support gap for these anchored inclusions vanishes and the array consists of translates of a common body along an affine path. No such array has an open neighborhood of independently perturbable compatible fibers. The endpoint cap fractions $1/m$ can be arbitrarily small.

b84198b3fe4ca80c:01.statement:

$$
U(z,t)=\sup\{s:|K_z\cap\{L(z,\cdot)\ge s\}|\ge t^d\}.
$$
The domain is convex and $U$ is finite, bounded, upper semicontinuous and jointly concave. For the cap $H=\{L\ge0\}$, its root $c_z=|K_z\cap\{x:L(z,x)\ge0\}|^{1/d}$ is concave on the projection of $C\cap H$ if that set is nonempty. On a positive fiber a proper cap has the unique root $U(z,c_z)=0$ and the zero and full cases are decided by the fiber support extrema. Its actual mixed cap mass is $\sum_z c_z^d$, summed over the integer bases in $P$.

$$
\int_{K_z} L(z,x)\,dx=d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt.
$$
At a mixed centroid $(j,y)$ with integer $j$, $L(j,y)=0$ and positive total mixed mass, the exact moment equations are $\sum_z(z-j)r(z)^d=0$ and $\sum_z d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt=0$. Null fibers contribute zero.

For $H_v=\{L(z,x)+v\cdot(z-j)\ge0\}$, the inverse is $U_v(z,t)=U(z,t)+v\cdot(z-j)$. At a parameter with no endpoint contacts on positive fibers, let $c_z$ now be the cap roots for $H_v$ and $\beta_z=-\partial_t U_v(z,c_z)$ at proper roots. These derivatives exist and are strictly positive. The mixed cap tilt gradient is
$$
\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{dc_z^{d-1}}{\beta_z}
=\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\partial H_v)}{\|u\|}.

$$

q'=\int_{F_A}T_pW_A\,ds+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}H_JW_K\,ds.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. $$

$$

b9b0fda52c8adffe:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $D$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $F$ be a compact convex subset of a hyperplane normal to the unit vector $e$, with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. Translate $F$ to height zero in this direction, let $I$ be the open height interval of $D$, and write $h=|I|$, $m=d-1$, $U=|D|$ and $D_t$ for the height-$t$ section identified with $e^\perp$. Then $(D+F)_t=D_t+F$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
|D+F|&\ge\int_I\bigl(|D_t|^{1/m}+f^{1/m}\bigr)^m\,dt\\
&=U+fh+\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}\binom mj f^{j/m}\int_I |D_t|^{(m-j)/m}\,dt .
\end{aligned}
$$
For $d=2$, $|D+F|=U+fh$.

In particular, suppose $A,K,B$ are convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, $u\ne0$, $D=A\cap\{u\cdot x\ge a_0\}$ is a proper positive-volume cap, and $B\subseteq\{u\cdot x\le b_0\}$ has a support facet $F=B\cap\{u\cdot x=b_0\}$ with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. For $q=|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge(a_0+b_0)/2\}|$, the first bound above applies to $2^dq$ with $e=u/\lVert u\rVert$ and $h=(h_A(u)-a_0)/\lVert u\rVert$, where $h_A$ is the support function of $A$. In particular $2^dq\ge U+fh$. If these bodies are the positive-volume fibers at $-1,0,1$ of a mixed body and the closed ambient cap with these three thresholds has raw mixed mass $Q$, then $2^d Q\ge (2^d+1)U+fh$.

For $d=2$, $B=T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1,\ i=1,2,3\}$ and $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1))$, the cap $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ has $2^d Q_i=4Q_i\ge5U_i+3(h_A(v_i)+1)$ for every proper positive $A$ trace of area $U_i$.

Suppose $C_z\subset y(z)+\ell(z)D$, with $D$ a convex $d$-body, $y$ affine, and $\ell(z)=a+bz>0$ on the base interval, where $b>0$. Put $D_z=(C_z-y(z))/\ell(z)$ and $A_\xi=\{z:\xi\in D_z\}$. Assume every nonempty $A_\xi$ contains a fixed interval with left integer endpoint $p_-$. Let
$$
f(\xi)=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z\text{ in the base}}\ell(z)^d\mathbf1_{D_z}(\xi),
\qquad G_b(\xi)=\int_{A_\xi}(\ell(z)-b)_+^d\,dz .
$$
Then $G_b\le f+(\ell(p_-)-b)_+^d$ pointwise. The function $g=(G_b-(\ell(p_-)-b)_+^d)_+$ is a pointwise minorant of $f$ with convex extended inverse $(d+1)$-st root. The corresponding result for negative slope uses reflection of the base and the reflected left integer endpoint.

$$
with the parameter in the actual relative linear span. Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $b$, $S_F$ the union of fibers over $P\cap F$, $C_F=\operatorname{conv}S_F$, and $\mu_F=\mu|_{S_F}$. $$
\int_{S_F}(W-Y)L^{-p-1}\,d\mu_F=0,\qquad
\int_{S_F} L^{-p-1}\,d\mu_F=\int_{S_F}L^{-p}\,d\mu_F=E(Y)>0.

bb74919333cc624f:04.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Let $E\subset K$ be measurable with volume $a$, and let $u\ne0$. $$
|K\cap H_0|+|E\cap H_t|+|K\cap H_{-t}|\ge \Gamma_d V+\lambda_d a.
$$
The coefficient is optimal already for a compact convex $E$. With fibers $E,K,K$ at consecutive bases $-1,0,1$ and measure given by the sum of their Lebesgue volumes, every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,g)$ has mass at least $\Gamma_d V+\lambda_d a$. The same holds after reversing the endpoint fibers. For convex $E$, these are the exact integer fibers of their lifted convex hull.

For a unit vector $u$ let $f(u)=|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge u\cdot g\rbrace|$ and $q(u)=|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge 2u\cdot g-\min_T u\cdot x\rbrace|$, and set $\rho_d=\min_u[f(u)-\Gamma+q(u)]$. Assume $\varepsilon>0$ and $a=\varepsilon^d<\rho_d$ and place $A=\varepsilon T,T,T$ at bases $-1,0,1$ in their actual lifted convex hull. With mixed measure the sum of the three fiber volumes, the unique deepest mixed-integer point is $(0,g)$ and its raw depth is $\Gamma+a$. The closed ambient halfspaces containing $(0,g)$ and attaining that depth are exactly
$$
\lbrace (z,x):\lambda_i(x)-Lz\ge b\rbrace,\qquad
0\le i\le d,\quad L\ge1-b,
$$
up to positive scaling of the defining margin. At $L=1-b$ the right trace is a vertex of $T$ and has zero $d$-volume.

bb78a1a25bcd2390:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T$ be a volume-one $d$-simplex with vertex $0$, centroid $g$, and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ with $\lambda_0(0)=1$. Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$, $c=(1-\Gamma)^{1/d}$, and let $\rho_d$ be the reflected simplex profile minimum. In the actual lift of $A=\varepsilon T,T,T$ at $-1,0,1$ assume $\varepsilon>0$ and $a=\varepsilon^d<\rho_d$. Use the finite cover of the mixed source by $\lambda_i(x)-2z\ge b$ and $\lambda_i(x)+2(z-1)\ge b$ for $0\le i\le d$. The one-cap residual-root obstacles are $(0,c,c)$, the unique sampled convex heights minimizing their sum of $d$th powers are $(c,c,c)$, and an exact KKT terminal row from $0$ is uniform on $-1,0,1$.

For each critical cap $\lambda_i(x)-Lz\ge b$ through $(0,g)$, define the correction cost to be the mean of the reciprocals of the first-exit fractions on this row, with fraction one for a destination retaining positive residual. The exact cost is $[2+(d+1)L]/3$ if $i\ge1$, and $[2+(d+1)(L+1-\varepsilon)]/3$ if $i=0$. The minimum over the full critical menu is $(d+2)/3$, attained at $L=1-b$ for every $i\ge1$. The corresponding closed and positive residual projections are respectively $[-1/d,1]$ and $(-1/d,1]$. Any such cap can be added to the cover or substituted for its corresponding same-direction left cap while retaining the residual program and the KKT row.

For $0<a\le\rho_d$ and each $L\ge2$, the caps $\lambda_i(x)-Lz\ge b$ are critical, with the same residual program and row when used in place of the left cover. For $i\ge1$ their costs are unbounded as $L$ grows even at fixed $d,a$, cap mass, source residual root, and original row. In the strict range the full-menu optimum also rules out a dimension-free bound, and for each fixed $d$ its excess over one cannot be bounded by a fixed multiple of the captured destination volume $a$.

bbc972e469554176:02.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex with $d\ge1$ and total mixed $d$-volume $M$. Fix a parity class whose $N\ge1$ positive-volume fibers have total volume $M_r$ and peak volume $a$. Suppose $M=2M_r-a$. If $N=1$ its only positive fiber is the only one in the whole trace. $$
E_{p_0+jv}=K_0+\frac{j}{2L}w\qquad(0\le j\le 2L).
$$
The selected class consists of the even indices. Zero-volume fibers may occur elsewhere. Conversely, each such configuration of positive-volume fibers gives equality for the indicated class. For $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, the centroid of the sole positive fiber when $N=1$, or the point $(p_0+Lv,g_0+w/2)$ for $N\ge2$ with $g_0$ the centroid of $K_0$, has raw closed-halfspace depth at least $\Gamma_d M$ and hence also at least $[N/(2N-1)]\Gamma_d M$.

bbd1a18ecbb9d3f0:01.statement:
Let $K$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with vertices $P_i$, $1\le i\le d+1$, and $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ sum to zero and satisfy $v_i\cdot(P_i-y)>0>v_i\cdot(P_j-y)$ for every $j\ne i$. Set
$$
H=\sum_i v_i\cdot(P_i-y),\qquad
a_i=\frac{v_i\cdot(P_i-y)}H,\qquad b_{ij}=-\frac{v_i\cdot(P_j-y)}H\quad(j\ne i).
$$
Then all these entries are positive, $\sum_i a_i=1$ and $\sum_{i\ne j}b_{ij}=a_j$. If $q_i$ is the volume fraction of the cap with margin $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ and $\sigma_i$ is the section's $(d-1)$-measure divided by $\|v_i\|$, then
$$
q_i=\frac{a_i^d}{\prod_{j\ne i}(a_i+b_{ij})},\qquad
\sigma_i=\frac{d|K|q_i}{Ha_i}.
$$
With $f_i=d a_i/q_i^{1/d}$ and $g_i=d a_i+\sum_{j\ne i}b_{ij}$, the inverse coareas are proportional to $f_i/q_i^{(d-1)/d}$, $f_i\le g_i$, $\sum_i g_i=d+1$, and
$$
d+1-\sum_i f_i\ge\frac1d\sum_i\ \sum_{\substack{j<k\\j,k\ne i}}\!
  \left(\sqrt{a_i+b_{ij}}-\sqrt{a_i+b_{ik}}\right)^2 .
$$
For $d=1$ the two row values are $f_1=f_2=1$.

Let $d\ge2$. On $d+1$ indices take positive $a_i,b_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$, with $\sum_i a_i=1$ and $\sum_{i\ne j}b_{ij}=a_j$. Set $f_i=d[\prod_{j\ne i}(a_i+b_{ij})]^{1/d}$. For every $i$,
$$
f_i+(d-1)\left(\frac{\sum_{j\ne i}f_j}{d}\right)^{d/(d-1)}\le d.
$$
Write $\bar f_j$ for the values after simultaneously averaging the rows and columns over permutations fixing $i$, and put $g=\sum_{j\ne i}f_j$, $\bar g=\sum_{j\ne i}\bar f_j$, $p=d/(d-1)$. The deficit is exactly
$$
d-f_i-(d-1)(g/d)^p
=(\bar f_i-f_i)+(d-1)\big[(\bar g/d)^p-(g/d)^p\big],
$$
with two nonnegative terms. Equality holds exactly when there are $A,B>0$ with $a_i=A$, $b_{ij}=B$ for $j\ne i$, and
$$
a_j+b_{ji}=1/d\quad(j\ne i),\qquad
a_j+b_{jk}=(1-A-B)/(d-1)>0\quad(k\ne i,j,\ j\ne i).
$$
For every prescribed $f_i\in(0,d)$ equality occurs for the normalized vertex evaluations of actual strict distinct-vertex simplex caps with interior common mark and nonzero spanning normals summing to zero.

bbd9056fa863fc6b:01.statement:
Let $1/2\le\theta<1$, $0\le b\le1-\theta$, $a\ge0$, and let $m\ge0$ be an integer with $am\le1$. For $0\le h\le m$ put
$$
\rho_h=1-ah,\qquad L_h=1-\frac{a(1-b)h}{\theta},\qquad B_h=1-\frac{ab}{\theta}-\frac{a(1+b)h}{\theta}.
$$
For every $x\in(0,1]$ the combined lists $(L_h)$ and $(B_h)$ have at least as many entries at least $x$ as $(\rho_h)$, counting multiplicities. Hence for every real $p>0$,
$$
\sum_{h=0}^m\big[(L_h)_+^p+(B_h)_+^p\big]\ \ge\ \sum_{h=0}^m\rho_h^p ,
\qquad v_+=\max(v,0).
$$
For $m=0$, equality in the power sum holds exactly when $ab\ge\theta$. For $m\ge1$, equality holds exactly when $m=1$, $a=1$ and $b=\theta=1/2$.

$$

bd3988521f16dd20:1.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:4.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:5.reason: The bump is $C^3$ at the joins. With $z=\cos^2(6\phi)$, $\psi+\psi''=432z-575z^2\ge-143$. The planar area formula follows from $\frac12\int\det(X_t,X_t')=\frac12\int (h_t^2-(h_t')^2)$. Integrating the even cosine powers gives $\int\psi=\pi/16$, $\int\psi^2=35\pi/768$ and $\int(\psi')^2=15\pi/4$. The normalized derivative uses $W=1/3$, $Q/|K|=1/2$ and $V'(0)=\pi/16$. The derivative concerns the upper cover.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:02.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be nonempty compact convex fibers. Write $L(z,X)=\ell(z)+c\cdot X$, where $\ell(z)=b+\beta\cdot z$ and $L>0$ on the placed fibers, hence on their convex hull. On the fixed fiber $z$, $T_z(X)=X/L(z,X)$ has signed Jacobian $\ell(z)L(z,X)^{-d-1}$. If $\ell(z)\ne0$, its inverse on the image is $X=\ell(z)Y/(1-c\cdot Y)$ and its image is convex. Positivity of $L$ allows collapse when $\ell(z)=0$.

Assume now that $\ell>0$ at every sampled base. The label-preserving images $J_z=T_z(K_z)$ are compatible, meaning $\sum_j\lambda_jJ_{z_j}\subseteq J_q$ for each anchored relation $q=\sum_j\lambda_j z_j\in P$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, if and only if for every such relation and $X_j\in K_{z_j}$,
$$
\frac{\ell(q)\sum_j\lambda_j X_j/L(z_j,X_j)}{\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(z_j)/L(z_j,X_j)}\in K_q.
$$
Equivalently, for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$ the support $\alpha_z(v)$ is the unique solution of $h_{K_z}(v-\alpha c)=\alpha\ell(z)$, and compatibility holds exactly when $\alpha_q(v)\ge\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_{z_j}(v)$ for every extreme anchored representation and every $v$. For polytopes the maximum defining $\alpha_z(v)$ occurs at an original vertex. If $K_z=\ell(z)K$ with $1+c\cdot X>0$ on $K$, then all $J_z$ coincide and are compatible.

A closed cap $a\cdot z+u\cdot X\ge h$ transforms on the positive chart into $a\cdot z-h+[\ell(z)u-(a\cdot z-h)c]\cdot Y\ge0$. This expression is affine if $u\beta^{\mathsf T}-ca^{\mathsf T}=0$. beffb23a92dd631a:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, with the origin in the relative interior of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. For each $p\in P$, let $K_p$ be a compact convex set of positive $d$-volume. Suppose the family is compatible, meaning that the convex hull of $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ has exactly $K_p$ as its fiber at $p$. Write $\mu=\sum_p\delta_p\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_p})$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For an affine $L$ positive on $P$, take the unweighted fiber-volume measure of the family obtained from $S$ by $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Assume its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth is locally minimized at $L=1$ among positive affine denominators. Write $\beta$ for this maximum at $L=1$ and $Q=\beta M$.

Index the deepest bases by $p_i$. At each one choose any exact positive circuit of nonvertical closed caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{(p,x):a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad \mu(H_{ij})=Q,
$$
whose boundaries pass through a common deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$ and whose weights satisfy $\rho_{ij}>0$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base use a fixed circuit covering the full fiber plane with each cap of mass strictly below $Q$. Such choices exist.

For each selected critical cap, let $\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}$, $\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}$ and $\theta^{\rm out}_{ij}$ be the sums of $(d-1)$-dimensional section area on its proper sections, inside supporting sections (the fiber is contained in the closed cap), and outside supporting sections (the cap meets the fiber in a supporting face of zero $d$-volume), respectively. These are measures on the lifted sections in the original coordinates, with zero-area sections contributing zero. For $d=1$ the section measure is counting measure.

For every such choice of circuits and every Borel system $\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ on the inside supporting sections, there exist outside densities $\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ and nonnegative multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$. Put
$$
\zeta_{ij}=\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}+\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}
                     +\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\theta^{\rm out}_{ij},
\qquad S_{ij}=\zeta_{ij}(\mathbb R^{r+d})>0.
$$
One such choice satisfies the linear identity
$$
-d\int A(p)\,d\mu
=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\left[-d\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
                             +\int \ell_{ij}(p,x)\,d\zeta_{ij}\right]
\tag{1}
$$
simultaneously for every signed affine $A$ and every signed cap velocity $\ell_{ij}(p,x)=\delta a_{ij}\cdot p+\delta u_{ij}\cdot x-\delta b_{ij}$ satisfying, for every $i$,
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}\delta u_{ij}=0,\qquad
\sum_j\rho_{ij}(\delta a_{ij}\cdot p_i-\delta b_{ij})=0.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular, the same certificate gives
$$
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta,\qquad
\int A(p)\,d\mu=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every affine }A,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=c_i\rho_{ij}\quad(c_i\ge0).
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently each group has either all multipliers positive or all zero. Equivalently, $\lambda_{ij}=\pi_i\kappa_{ij}/\beta$, where $\pi_i=\beta\sum_j\lambda_{ij}$ are nonnegative and sum to one, and $\kappa_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/\sum_l(\rho_{il}/S_{il})$. The same choice of outside allocations and multipliers works for all tests in (1)–(3) for the prescribed inside system.

c0611f2da2e55fa1:02.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope, $d\ge1$, whose nonempty integer fibers are all positive $d$-volume. Let $\eta$ be the sum of their boundary $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measures, with the regular outward continuous unit normal marked, and let $\Pi$ be a physical martingale coupling from a finite $\nu\ll\eta$ to $\eta$ preserving that mark. The target of the rows starting in $F$ is $\eta|_F-\zeta_F$, where $\zeta_F$ is exactly the target law of the rows starting outside $F$ and ending in $F$. Its mass is
$$
L_F=\eta(F)-\nu(F)=\Pi\{w\notin F,\ w'\in F\}\ge0.
$$

Without the correction, $\int_F\psi\,d\nu\le\int_F\psi\,d\eta$ for each finite nonnegative convex function on the affine plane of $F$.

$$
(\Psi^{-1})_\#(\eta|_F)=\mu_F=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_p}.
$$
The common mark $u$ is forgotten in this equality. If $\eta(F)>0$, $\mu_F$ is the intrinsic Hausdorff measure on the mixed trace of $D$. The ambient Jacobian of $\Psi$ is $\sqrt{1+|a|^2}$ and the corresponding base projection coarea Jacobian is its reciprocal. The displayed mixed fiber law has no slope factor. At $d=1$ the nonempty reduced fibers are singletons, with unit counting mass. The pullback laws satisfy $\widehat\nu_F+\widehat\zeta_F\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\mu_F$ in equal-mass convex order, with the correction of mass $L_F$.

If $d\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\,d\eta$ for a finite cap menu with actual bounded Borel body allocations and $\lambda_j\ge0$, the reduced source density is $\sum_j\lambda_j(\alpha_j\circ\Psi)$ relative to $\mu_F$. An ambient cap $c_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j$ pulls back to
$$

\ \ge\ b_j-(v_j\cdot u)b .

c0fc791108fc8765:01.statement:

The maps $y\mapsto a_y$ and $y\mapsto E_K(y)$ are smooth on $\operatorname{int}K$ and
$$

\nabla_y E_K(y)^{1/d}=\frac{d+1}{d}E_K(y)^{1/d}a_y.
$$
The optimal denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$ is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $K$ and strictly greater than $1/(d+1)$ on $\operatorname{int}K$.

c0fc791108fc8765:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Set $Q=\operatorname{conv}P$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. For the positive attained energy
$E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over denominators positive on $K$, put $F(z,x)=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ on $\Omega_C=\{(z,x):z\in Q,\ x\in\operatorname{int}C_z\}$.

Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, let $a_y$ be the optimizer at this mark in $K_p$, and put $F_0=F(p,y)$. The function $F$ is locally Lipschitz relative to $\operatorname{aff}(Q)\times\mathbb R^d$ on its domain near $(p,y)$, and there is a finite $B\in\operatorname{span}(Q-Q)$ such that
$$
F(z,x)\le F_0\left[1+B\cdot(z-p)+\frac{d+1}{d}a_y\cdot(x-y)\right]\qquad((z,x)\in\Omega_C).
$$
Every supergradient at $(p,y)$ has continuous component $\frac{d+1}{d}F_0a_y$. The associated affine chart
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+\frac{d}{d+1}B\cdot(z-p)
$$
is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $C$ and strictly greater on $\Omega_C$. The base point $p$ may lie on the relative boundary of $Q$. For arbitrary compact convex ambient bodies a finite boundary-base energy supergradient can fail, even with full-dimensional ball fibers.

Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume the sampled anchored Minkowski inclusions. \min_C L=\min_{x\in K_p}[1+a_y\cdot(x-y)]\ge\frac1{d+1}.
$$
For every threshold $0<\delta<1/(d+1)$, a tangent continuation of $t^{-d}$ below $\delta$ is inactive on a neighborhood of $C$ when evaluated at $L$.

$$

\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon h_{K_p-y}(u)L(z,x)^{-d}\le \ell(u,z)\}

c1694074e553a581:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, and let $y=(z_0,x_0)\in C$ with $z_0\in\mathbb Z$. Write $K_z$ for its continuous fibers. Set $N_k^\pm=(K_{z_0\pm k}-x_0)/k$ for integers $k\ge1$ and let $h_\pm(a)$ be the extended gauge of $C-y$ evaluated at $(\pm1,a)$. Then $N_k^\pm=\{a:h_\pm(a)\le1/k\}$ are nested decreasing. The strict-side volume pushforwards under $(z_0\pm k,x)\mapsto (x-x_0)/k$ have densities
$$
f_\pm(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^d\mathbf1_{N_k^\pm}(a)=F_d(\lfloor1/h_\pm(a)\rfloor),\qquad F_d(m)=\sum_{k=1}^m k^d,
$$
where $1/\infty=0$. They have convex superlevels, total masses $\sum_{k\ge1}|K_{z_0\pm k}|$, and first moments $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-1}\int_{K_{z_0\pm k}}(x-x_0)\,dx$.

For strict-side endpoint directions $a,b$ at distances $k,\ell$, their intersection with base $z_0$ has continuous coordinate $T=x_0+[k\ell/(k+\ell)](a+b)$. Thus its membership in a closed halfspace through $y$ depends only on the direction sum, and each subcoupling of the directional volume measures lifts to a subcoupling of the strict-side original volumes. In particular the largest subcoupling mass carried by $a+b=0$ is
$$
\int_{\mathbb R^d}\min\{f_-(a),f_+(-a)\}\,da
=\sum_{k\ge1}|K_{z_0-k}\cap(2x_0-K_{z_0+k})|.
$$
Only one copy of each reflected base pair is counted. If the strict-side total volumes are equal and positive, the choice $x_0=\sum_{\pm,k}(w_{\pm k}/k)c_{\pm k}/\sum_{\pm,k}w_{\pm k}/k$, with $w_{\pm k},c_{\pm k}$ the volumes and centroids of the positive-volume fibers, belongs to $K_{z_0}$ and makes the sum of the directional first moments zero.

Let $I_R(a,v)=\int_0^\infty R_{a,v}(x)\,dx$, $J_d(v)=\partial_a I_R(0,v)$ (the right derivative), and $G_d(v)=\int_0^\infty L_v(x)\,dx+I_R(0,v)-1/(d+1)$. Then $J_d$ and $G_d$ are continuous on $[0,1]$ and both vanish at $0$. For $0<v\le1$, with $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+dz/(d+1))^d$,
$$
G_d(v)=\frac{f(v)+f(-v)-2}{dv^2}-\frac1{d+1}.
$$
Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_d&=3d(3d+1)2^{d-3},&
T_d&=\frac{2^{d-3}(9d^2-7d+2)}{d+1},&
B_d&=(d+2)2^{d-4},\\
C_d&=\frac{V_d}{4}+\frac d8+\frac{T_d}{2}+B_d,&
K_d&=\frac{d(2d+1)}{(d+1)^2}\left(1+\frac1{d+1}\right)^{d-2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
\frac{D(a,atv)}{\Gamma}=-\frac{G_d(v)}a-J_d(v)-\frac12+\rho_d(a,v),
\qquad
|\rho_d(a,v)|\le C_d a,\qquad |J_d(v)|\le K_d v .
$$

c21aa22115d69526:06.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

With the constants $C_d$ and $K_d$ of the uniform deficit expansion, define
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac1{4[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]}\right\}.
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and $0\le\beta\le at$,
$$
\frac{D(a,\beta)}{\Gamma}\le -\frac12+[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]a.
$$
In particular $D(a,\beta)\le-\Gamma/4$ for all $0<a\le\varepsilon_d$ and $0\le\beta\le at$.

c22519c29667168e:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be nonzero vectors with $p_i,-p_i\in\partial K$ for every $i$. $$
\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|\ge \frac49|K|,
$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes planar area. The constant is sharp. Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a triangle with centroid $0$ and, after dropping zero weights and merging repeated oriented chords, the three $H_i$ are the vertex halfplanes through $0$ parallel to the opposite sides, with total weight $1/3$ on each. A balanced opposite pair, or a positive noncollinear triple with one weight $1/2$, has weighted cap area $|K|/2$.

c2528b1460a23da4:01.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty compact sets, $V$ a linear subspace, $q\ge0$ with $\mathcal H_q(A)<\infty$, and $Z=V+\operatorname{conv} B$. Suppose nonnegative Borel functions $F$ on $\mathbb R^m$ and $g$ on $A$ satisfy $F(a+b)\ge g(a)$ for all $a\in A$, $b\in B$. Then
$$
\int_{(A+B)\setminus Z}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge\int_{A\setminus V}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
For any one compact $P\subseteq A$ contained in an affine subspace $L$ this gives
$$
\int_{A+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge
\int_{P+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q+\int_{A\setminus L}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
The inequalities allow extended integrals and include $q=0$. If $A,B$ lie in $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, the translated source pieces lie in that lattice as actual sum points.

$$

\ge \int_{P+B}\Psi(\sigma)\,dx+\int_A\Psi(\rho)\,da.
$$
This includes unions, intersections, and positive excess above a threshold for the number of missed caps. For compact mixed-lattice source sets on one common integer parity class and finite source measure $\mathcal H_q(A)$, with Borel $K$ containing all actual midpoints, the factor is $2^q$, the integrals use $\mathcal H_q$, and the final integral is over $A\setminus\operatorname{aff}P$.

In the planar case with three nonzero spanning normals $v_0+v_1+v_2=0$, suppose the three caps $v_i\cdot x-z\ge0$ each have raw mixed area $Q$ in the actual fibers $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. c260aef7098c009e:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^2$ be compact and convex, with integer-fiber length measure $\mu$. Its positive fibers are intervals $K_i=[l_i,u_i]$ of widths $w_i=u_i-l_i$ on the finite consecutive index set $P$. Fix $j\in P$, put $d_i=i-j$, $M=\sum_iw_i$, and let
$$

$$
For $0<t\le T_j$ let $B_j(t)$ be the interval of continuous centroids of dominated sources $0\le f\le1$ of mass $t$ and base centroid $j$. Let $c_j(t)$ be its midpoint, including the singleton convention. Write $Q_v(t)$ for the maximum of $\sum_i(v_i m_i-m_i^2/2)$ over the same box with centered base moment zero and $\sum_i m_i=t$. With $U=Q_u$ and $V=Q_{-l}$,
$$
 B_j(t)=[-V(t)/t,U(t)/t],\qquad c_j(t)=\frac{U(t)-V(t)}{2t}.
$$
Each optimizer is unique and has the form $m_i=\operatorname{clamp}(v_i-b-\nu d_i,0,w_i)$ for finite multipliers $b,\nu$, where $\operatorname{clamp}(x,0,w)=\min(w,\max(0,x))$. The intervals are nested in decreasing order as $t$ increases and $c_j(0)=(l_j+u_j)/2$ gives a continuous extension.

The functions $U,V$ are continuous finite piecewise quadratics on $[0,T_j]$. On any open interval of one fixed empty/free/full pattern with free set $A$ of at least two indices, set $S=|A|$, $Z=\sum_{i\in A}d_i$ and $ZZ=\sum_{i\in A}d_i^2$. Then $Q_v'=b$ and $Q_v''=-1/(S-Z^2/ZZ)$. If only $j$ is free on an open interval, then $Q_v'=b$ and $Q_v''=-1$. Denote the boundary values at base $j$ of the optimizing upper and lower caps by $b_+=b_U$ and $b_-=-b_V$, respectively. Away from finitely many transition masses they determine the path by
$$
c_j(t)=\frac{1}{2t}\int_0^t[b_+(s)+b_-(s)]\,ds.
$$
If all endpoints are rational, the path has form $At+B+C_0/t$ on finitely many rational mass intervals with rational coefficients, with $C_0=0$ on the first interval. Its range has rational or quadratic-algebraic endpoints with decidable endpoint inclusion. At any rational raw mixed-depth level, one can decide exactly whether a positive-time path point reaches that level in the original measure, using all closed halfspace orientations.

c260aef7098c009e:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^2$ be compact and convex with original integer-fiber length measure $\mu$ of positive total mass $M$. Its positive fibers are $K_i=[l_i,u_i]$, with $w_i=u_i-l_i$ on a consecutive finite integer index set $P$. Fix $j\in P$. Let $T_j$ be the maximum mass of any dominated source of base centroid $j$, equivalently the maximum of $\sum_i m_i$ over $0\le m_i\le w_i$ with $\sum_i(i-j)m_i=0$. Let $c_j(T_j)$ be the midpoint of the interval of continuous centroids of all such maximal-mass sources.

The maximizing allocation $m^*$ is unique. If the original base centroid is $j$, it keeps all fibers. If the base centroid is larger than $j$, it keeps all fibers through $j$, fills the fibers to the right in order of increasing index until the moment is balanced, and discards the remaining right fibers. There is at most one partially filled terminal fiber. If the original base centroid is smaller than $j$, the reflected description holds. In the convex hull of the retained full intervals and the centered subinterval of the partial terminal fiber, if present, the positive integer fibers are exactly these retained intervals. This hull has mixed length $T_j$ and true mixed centroid
$$
\left(j,c_j(T_j)\right),\qquad
c_j(T_j)=\frac{1}{T_j}\sum_i m_i^*\frac{l_i+u_i}{2}.
$$
The original raw closed-halfspace depth at this point exceeds $T_j/3$ when the hull has more than one positive fiber, and is at least $T_j/2$ when it has one. In particular $T_j\ge 3M/4$ implies a positive-mass path point of original raw depth at least $M/4$.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:01.reason: The affine pullback and the representation-preserving evaluations prove exact anchored equivalence, compatible measured sections, Helly preservation, and depth monotonicity on each retained base.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:01.statement:
For a nonempty finite set $P$ in a real affine space, call $T\subseteq P$ closed if $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$. An anchored representation of $q\in P$ is $q=\sum_{p\in P}\lambda_pp$ with $\lambda_p\ge0$ and $\sum_p\lambda_p=1$. Let $L(P)\subseteq\mathbb R^P$ be the space of scalar functions preserving every such equality. For a basis $1,g_1,\ldots,g_{\ell-1}$ of $L(P)$, the map $\Phi_P(p)=(g_1(p),\ldots,g_{\ell-1}(p))$ is injective, with an affine projection back to $P$. Its image has affine dimension $\ell-1$, preserves exactly the anchored representations and the closed traces, and all representation-preserving functions on $\Phi_P(P)$ are affine restrictions. In particular its relative Helly number equals $h(P)$, the least number of ambient convex sets needed to certify an empty common trace on $P$ from any finite such system.

Fix $d\ge1$. A family of nonempty compact convex sets $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ is compatible if $\sum_p\lambda_p K_p\subseteq K_q$ for every anchored representation of $q$. This is equivalent to being the exact sections of the convex hull of their placed fibers at all sites of $P$. For families of positive $d$-volume let $D_P(K)$ be the maximum, over placed fiber points, of the infimum of normalized mass of containing closed halfspaces, using the sum of fiber $d$-volumes. Let $M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d$ for nonempty $T\subseteq P$. Then, with the same retained fibers,
$$
D_P(K)\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_T(K|_T)
\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_{\Phi_T(T)}(K|_T).
$$
Here $T$ has its inherited placement and the last depth uses its own canonical lift. The closed-minor operation followed by canonical lifting, iterated on an initial $P$, produces only lifts of its nonempty closed subsets up to affine equivalence. For a closed $T$, $h(T)\le h(P)$.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:03.reason: Choose a smallest bad canonical minor for the stated budget. Its proper-minor inequalities imply the uniform positive volume floor, allowing common shape normalization and an actual affine shear before taking the depth limit.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:03.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$ and $\tau>0$. For a finite nonempty base $P$ let $D_P(K)$ be normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth on the full compatible positive $d$-volume fibers $K$, and let $b_d(P)=\inf_K D_P(K)$ over all such families. Write $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Use one of the following budgets consistently on closed subsets and their canonical lifts.

- For an arbitrary finite base $P$, use its relative Helly number $q(P)=h(P)$.
- For a complete finite affine-lattice base $P$, use the number $q(P)=k(P)$ of occupied parity classes. Each closed subset uses the inherited affine lattice, and each canonical lift uses its complete integer graph realization with the inherited graph lattice.

Suppose $D_P(K)<\tau/q(P)$ for some positive compatible family. Then among the canonical lifts of nonempty closed subsets of $P$ with $b_d(\Phi_U(U))<\tau/q(U)$, choose one with the fewest sites. Write $B=\Phi_U(U)$ for any such choice, using the integer realization in the parity case. It is dependence-connected, $q(B)=q(U)\le q(P)$, every representation-preserving function on $B$ is affine, and $\dim\operatorname{aff}(B)\le h(B)-1$. In the parity case $B$ is complete in its inherited affine lattice, even if its affine rank exceeds the original rank.

On this $B$ the unrestricted infimum $\beta=b_d(B)<\tau/q(B)$ is attained by a compatible family of total volume one with every fiber of positive $d$-volume, and $\beta\ge\gamma_d/|B|>0$. More precisely, for every $0<\delta<\tau/q(B)$, the mass-one sublevel $D_B(K)\le\delta$ has a uniform positive lower bound on all fiber volumes and is sequentially compact for simultaneous fiber Hausdorff convergence after common continuous affine normalizations and affine shears on $B$. For every nonempty proper closed $T\subset B$ every member of this sublevel satisfies
$$
M_T\ \le\ \frac{D_B(K)}{\tau}\,q(T)\ \le\ \frac{\delta}{\tau}\,q(T)\ <\ \frac{q(T)}{q(B)},
\qquad M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d.
$$
For $\tau=\gamma_d$, the Helly case is the auxiliary finite-base reduction. In the parity case an actual mixed-integer body on $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with positive total mixed $d$-volume and normalized maximum depth below $\tau/2^n$ supplies a strict bad input on its complete positive-fiber base. This includes $\tau=\gamma_d$ and any fixed $c_0\in(0,1/e)$ by taking $\tau=c_0$.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:04.reason: Use the fixed-base slab and symmetric-difference estimates of the residual theorem without a recentering change. The accepted positive-family stability result also gives convergence at corresponding marks. Compactness and a fixed limiting maximizing mark give both limits of maxima.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:04.statement: On any fixed finite base, simultaneous Hausdorff convergence of positive compatible d-fibers to positive fibers implies continuity of their ordinary normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth. On fibers lying in R B_d, raw depth in one fiber is |P|κ_{d−1}R^{d−1}-Lipschitz; symmetric-difference mass bounds the additional family-change error.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:05.reason: The initial approximation argument applies on the given finite base. Form the placed hull of the inner nets and use its actual sampled sections. Their depth converges and the nonzero continuous normals of the non-pure-base facets yield the common inequalities.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:05.statement: Any strict bad positive compatible family on a fixed finite base admits a strict bad compatible polytopal approximation with finitely many shared inequalities n_f·x+a_f·b≤c_f having nonzero continuous normals, using actual sampled sections.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:06.reason: Inner polytopal approximation supplies a strict competitor with finitely many shared inequalities. An affine evaluation correction handles divergent thresholds in a fixed-count limit, so the compact sublevel minimum stays in that class.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:06.statement:
Use the assumptions and either budget of the smallest bad canonical minor theorem, and let $B$ be one of its selected bases. For a positive integer $N$ let $\mathcal R_N(B)$ consist of positive fiber families with a representation by $N$ shared affine inequalities
$$
K_b=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:n_f\cdot x\le t_f(b),\ 1\le f\le N\}\qquad(b\in B),
$$
where $n_f\ne0$ and $t_f$ is an affine function on the affine hull of $B$. Redundant and repeated inequalities are allowed. There is some finite $N$ for which $\beta_N=\inf_{K\in\mathcal R_N(B)}D_B(K)$ is attained with total mass one, positive volume in every fiber, and $\beta_N<\tau/q(B)$.

For any fixed finite base and fixed $N$, this class is closed under simultaneous Hausdorff limits whose fibers all have positive volume. A sufficiently small perturbation of all shared inequality coefficients of an $\mathcal R_N(B)$ family keeps each fiber positive and bounded and preserves compatibility. The minimum $\beta_N$ is a separate extremal value and satisfies $b_d(B)\le\beta_N$.

c29c6aecdf35b1de:01.reason: Finite indicator algebra. Only the cross-group overlap term is always nonnegative; the individual group deficits and boundary density can be signed.
c29c6aecdf35b1de:01.statement: For a finite grouped cap cover of a measured mixed set S with total mass M, let U_s be the union of the caps in group s and b_s their largest cap mass. For Γ=(d/(d+1))^d, the surplus B=Σ_s b_s−ΓM equals Σ_s[b_s−Γμ(U_s)]+Γ∫_S(m−1)dμ, where m counts the containing group unions. Equivalently use inclusion–exclusion on the U_s. With fixed maximizing caps B is their signed indicator sum minus Γ1_S. Replacing each maximizing cap by a probability average of its group gives a lower functional, equal to B when cap masses are equal within each group.

external_dependencies: Rado's centerpoint theorem for a finite Borel measure in ambient dimension three
c29c6aecdf35b1de:02.reason: 2acc8bc803acf1c0 gives the ordinary simplex sharpness result for the mixed product and agrees with the upper mixed depth restriction, but does not provide the real nonempty region and signed pointwise contradiction. Its caps are strict containing certificates and need not be supports of the actual depth region.
c29c6aecdf35b1de:02.statement:
Let $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a triangle of area $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, and use the mixed source of $[0,1]\times T$. For $1-1/\sqrt2<t<1/3$ take closed cap groups
$$
H_{0,i}=\{\lambda_i-t-z\ge0\},\qquad H_{1,i}=\{\lambda_i-t-(1-z)\ge0\},\qquad i=0,1,2.
$$
All cap masses are $(1-t)^2V$, and each group covers its own fiber alone. The polytope cut out by the six reversed weak inequalities is bounded and full-dimensional with exact base projection $[1/3-t,2/3+t]$. For every $(1-t)^2V<\alpha<V/2$, the real depth-$\alpha$ region is nonempty and lies in that polytope, so has no mixed-integer point. Yet no two choices of probability weights $\pi_{s,i}$ make $\sum_{s,i}\pi_{s,i}\mathbf1_{H_{s,i}}-(4/9)\mathbf1_S$ nonnegative pointwise on the mixed source $S$. At $t=3/10$ one may take $\alpha=99V/200$.

c29c6aecdf35b1de:03.reason: The accepted 261ee2b3de0b984a proves the generic step-density tent test; 82cb221614bc7dbf has the same three-step cap load on a different mixed source with ratio 181/450, not the sharp affine-canceling ratio 4/9. Here the signed-measure criterion supplies the cost sign, strict kernel positivity supplies the affine-only equality, and a realized small edge graph gives the exact physical variation. The related all-dimensional simplex facet inequality 8e69e6820cd6ee00:02 remains unaccepted and is not used.
c29c6aecdf35b1de:03.statement:
Let $T$ be a triangle with affine barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$. Fix $H_i=\{\lambda_i\ge1/3\}$ and set $E(K)=\frac13\sum_i|K\cap H_i|-\frac49|K|$. On any edge $F$ use the normalized linear parameter $s\in[0,1]$. Its boundary density $w$ is $-1/9$ on the outer thirds and $2/9$ on the middle third, up to endpoints and breakpoints, and it annihilates affine functions. Its Green potential is
$$
K(t)=\begin{cases}
t^2/18&0\le t\le1/3,\\
[6t(1-t)-1]/54&1/3\le t\le2/3,\\
(1-t)^2/18&2/3\le t\le1 .
\end{cases}
$$
For continuous concave $v$ the cost $\int_0^1wv$ is nonnegative, with equality precisely for affine $v$. For a Lipschitz concave $v$ vanishing at the edge ends, replace $F$ by its outward graph of height $\eta v$ while keeping the other edges. This yields a convex body $K_\eta$ for all sufficiently small $\eta>0$ and $E'(0+)=|F|\int_0^1wv$. For simultaneous realized edge speeds the first variations add, and affine speeds from moving endpoints give zero. No positive uniform coefficient times total curvature lower-bounds the response for concave Lipschitz tests.
