The six old fixed cap masses are equal at the old triangle. Equality of all six for the deformed product would need an additional symmetry or a cap reequalization argument.

c29c6aecdf35b1de:05.reason: 261ee2b3de0b984a gives the Green equivalence for piecewise constant densities tested on normalized whole-face tents, with an additional roof calculation. This proposition treats arbitrary finite signed measures after both exact affine moment cancellations and all continuous concave tests, via uniform concave splines. Its step-density verification is the existing Green calculation in unit coordinates and no old geometric assumption is needed.
c29c6aecdf35b1de:05.statement: Let $\rho$ be a finite signed measure on $[0,1]$ with $\int d\rho=\int s\,d\rho(s)=0$. Put $G(s,t)=\min((1-t)s,t(1-s))$ and $K_\rho(t)=\int G(s,t)\,d\rho(s)$. The condition $\int v\,d\rho\ge0$ for every continuous concave $v$ is equivalent to $K_\rho(t)\ge0$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. If $\rho$ has piecewise constant density, $K_\rho$ has zero endpoints, is piecewise quadratic, and satisfies $-K_\rho''=\rho$ as distributions in the open interval. Then positivity can be checked at breakpoints and the interior stationary points of the quadratic pieces.

c29c6aecdf35b1de:06.reason: The §1 cover identity is finite signed bookkeeping and gives no sign for this exact four-group geometry. The complete actual support, indispensability even in the twelve-inequality projection, strict contacts, square sign table and empty common-budget region are verified directly. The two-fiber charge obstruction has equal cap masses and a nonempty real depth region, so it does not yield the negative aggregate surplus here.
c29c6aecdf35b1de:06.statement:
There is an actual mixed source of six planar square fibers at bases $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)$ and a twelve-cap certificate, grouped into four positive rank-two circuits, whose reversed polytope is bounded, full-dimensional and has four indispensable projected facets for integer exclusion, each with strict cross-group contact. For centered square radii $r=1/1000$ on the first three bases and $R=1/100$ on the last three, set $v=4r^2$. In the order of the proof the four cap-mass rows in units of $v$ are $(3,0,0),(3,0,0),(3,0,1/2),(103,100,100)$ and the total mixed mass is $M=303v$. The cross-group correction is $4v$ and $\sum_s\max_j\mu(H_{s,j})-(4/9)M=-68v/3$. Keeping the caps and $R$ fixed, for $0<r<R/2$ the same incidences and the same half-square trace give
$$
\sum_s\max_j\mu(H_{s,j})-(4/9)M=(128r^2-4R^2)/3.
$$
The derivative is $256r/3$ and the sign crosses zero at $R/\sqrt{32}$. In the calibrated case the raw $104v$-depth region is empty.

external_dependencies: Cauchy projection formula ∫_(∂K)|e·n|dH_(d−1)=2|proj_(e⊥)K|_(d−1), in its line-fiber form from the area formula for orthogonal projection.
c2eb139e074f5fb3:01.reason: The elementary Cauchy projection formula applies to each positive cap body. At supporting facets, the two allocated terms either add to the original boundary contribution or reproduce twice the selected shadow. Existing physical Gauss–Green identities use signed normal flux and do not reconstruct the positive projected cap body or the selected outside shadow.
c2eb139e074f5fb3:01.statement:
Let $K_z$ be positive-volume compact convex $d$-bodies, $d\ge1$, at finitely many bases, and let $H=\{a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge c\}$. Use surface measure $dS$ summed over their boundaries and write $n_z$ for the regular outer continuous normal. For $u\ne0$, use the usual cap indicator $s$ on strict old boundary traces. On an inside supporting facet allocate body density $s=\alpha$ and section density $1-\alpha$, and on an outside supporting facet allocate body and section densities both $\alpha$, with Borel $0\le\alpha\le1$. Count proper sections in full and divide section areas by $\|u\|$ to define total coarea $T$. Lower-dimensional faces have zero section area. For $u=0$ use whole-fiber bits and $T=0$.

For a unit $e$ let $B(e)=\sum_z|\operatorname{proj}_{e^\perp}K_z|_{d-1}$. Define the allocated cap shadow $B_H(e)$ as the sum over bases of the ordinary projection volume of a positive-volume cap body, zero for an empty or lower-area trace, and $|e\cdot u|\int_F\alpha\,dS/\|u\|$ at an outside supporting facet $F$. A pure-base cap uses the whole-fiber shadow for each selected base. All areas in dimension zero are counting volumes. Then $2B_H(e)=\int s\,|e\cdot n_z|\,dS+|e\cdot u|T$. The complementary allocation uses body density $1-s$ and the same section measure, and $B_H(e)+B_{H^{\rm comp}}(e)=B(e)+|e\cdot u|T$. Both allocated shadows are at most $B(e)$ and at least $|e\cdot u|T$.

external_dependencies: Cauchy projection formula in its line-fiber form; support-function order for compact convex sets; rotational invariance of normalized sphere measure.
c2eb139e074f5fb3:02.reason: The single-cap draft identifies an exact positive shadow and both bounding quantities for every direction. Testing the stipulated normal marginal equality against |e·n| gives the averaged reserve. Support-function order and angular averaging give the two consequences. The accepted buffered separator a1081821f9c8a5b1 has extra positive response and source terms and does not by itself give this unmodified marginal equality for W.
c2eb139e074f5fb3:02.statement:
Use the bodies, actual cap records and consistent coarea allocations of the per-cap projection identity. For a finite menu indexed by $j$, use weights $\theta_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\theta_j=1$ and write $W=\sum_j\theta_j s_j$. Suppose $\int(W-\beta)b(n_z)\,dS=0$ for every continuous function $b$ on the unit normal sphere. Set $R(e)=\sum_j\theta_j T_j|e\cdot u_j|$. For every unit direction $e$,
$$
\sum_j\theta_j B_j(e)=\beta B(e)+\frac12R(e),\qquad
R(e)\le2\min(\beta,1-\beta)B(e).
$$
For the projection body $\Pi K_z$ with support function $|\operatorname{proj}_{e^\perp}K_z|_{d-1}$ on the unit sphere, this is the inclusion $\sum_j\theta_j T_j[-u_j,u_j]\subseteq 2\min(\beta,1-\beta)\sum_z\Pi K_z$. A group whose weights satisfy $\theta_{ij}T_{ij}=\kappa_i\rho_{ij}$ contributes $\kappa_i\sum_j\rho_{ij}[-u_{ij},u_{ij}]$. The scalar angular consequence is $\sum_j\theta_j\|u_j\|T_j\le\min(\beta,1-\beta)\sum_z\mathcal H^{d-1}(\partial K_z)$. The same formulas with integrals hold for a probability law of jointly measurable actual cap records and consistent allocations with bounded total coarea and bounded continuous normals. For the law the section body's support function is the integral of the segment support functions.

c2eb139e074f5fb3:03.reason: The accepted simplex-depth formula makes the canonical caps critical at the true centroid. On each old facet their average area fraction is exactly beta, so the new shadow identity applies and gives the factor-d loss in the scalar lower bound. The two opposite box caps independently saturate the universal directional coefficient. Neither calculation follows from the simplex depth value alone.
c2eb139e074f5fb3:03.statement: For the uniform menu of the $d+1$ canonical centroid caps of a $d$-simplex, use the preceding section projection notation, and put $a=d/(d+1)$ and $\beta=\Gamma_d=a^d$. Then $R(e)/(2B(e))=\Gamma_d/d$ in every unit direction. The bound $\beta\ge\sup_e R(e)/(2B(e))$ therefore has a factor $d$ loss on this menu for $d\ge2$, also when obtained by averaging directions. The universal coefficient $2$ in $R(e)\le2\min(\beta,1-\beta)B(e)$ is attained by a centered box with the two opposite coordinate caps of equal weight and the direction of their common axis.

c323819a201d7580:01.reason: The known affine cap isolators retain exact trace budgets for all 0<ε<1. Explicit multipliers verify the finite sampled-convex optimum and produce a genuinely failing original terminal row.
c323819a201d7580:01.statement:
Let $d,n\ge2$, let $T$ be a volume-one $d$-simplex with a vertex at $0$, and write $\lambda_i$ for its barycentric coordinates, $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$, and $c=(1-\Gamma)^{1/d}$. Assume $c<n/(n+1)$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. Form the actual lift with $T$ at every binary cube vertex and $A=\varepsilon T$ at $v_-=-\mathbf 1$. Write $a=\varepsilon^d$. Its integer fibers are exactly the assigned positive fibers. The total is $M=2^n+a$, the occupied parity count is $k=2^n$, and the largest fiber has volume $1<M/k$.

Define $\delta_0(z)=\sum_jz_j$ and for nonzero cube vertices $w$ define $\delta_w(z)=(n+1)\sum_{j:w_j=1}(1-z_j)+\sum_{j:w_j=0}z_j$. The caps $\lambda_i(x)-2\delta_w(z)\ge b$ for all $w,i$ cover the mixed source with budgets at most $\Gamma+a$. The one-cap residual-root obstacles are zero at $v_-$ and $c$ at every cube base. The sampled convex-threshold program minimizing the sum of the $d$th powers has unique optimal heights all equal to $c$ and value $(2^n+1)c^d$. It has an exact KKT terminal row from $0$ uniform on $0,v_-,u_1,\ldots,u_n$, where the $u_j$ are the coordinate unit vectors. For each of the original $w=0$ caps the residual-root mean under this unchanged row exceeds its source value by $[n-(n+1)c]/(n+2)>0$.

c323819a201d7580:02.reason: Exact binary depth and three-fiber equality on the diagonal triple force a canonical direction. The zero-volume traces at each off-diagonal unit base force the individual slope bounds. The original row fails for every member, with the same gap.
c323819a201d7580:02.statement:
Let $d,n\ge2$, let $T$ be a volume-one $d$-simplex with vertex $0$, barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, and centroid $g$. Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$ and $c=(1-\Gamma)^{1/d}<n/(n+1)$. Place $T$ at all binary cube vertices and $A=\varepsilon T$ at $v_-=-\mathbf 1$ in their actual lifted convex hull. Assume $\varepsilon>0$ and $a=\varepsilon^d<\rho_d$, the reflected simplex profile minimum. Then $(0,g)$ is the unique deepest mixed point with raw depth $Q=\Gamma+a$. The closed ambient halfspaces containing it and attaining that depth are exactly
$$
F_{i,\beta}=\lbrace(z,x):\lambda_i(x)+\beta\cdot z\ge b\rbrace,\qquad
0\le i\le d,\quad \beta_j\le-(1-b)\quad(1\le j\le n),
$$
up to positive scaling. At a supporting threshold a nonzero cube trace can be a vertex of zero $d$-volume.

For the finite cover and exact KKT row in the finite simplex cap-cover counterexample, every $F_{i,\beta}$ fails unchanged residual-root Jensen on that same row by $[n-(n+1)c]/(n+2)>0$. Adding any $F_{i,\beta}$ or replacing the original source cap of the same barycentric direction preserves the cover, residual obstacles, and KKT row. All fibers have mass less than $M/k$ for total $M=2^n+a$ and occupied parity count $k=2^n$. The sharp-threshold excess in raw depth is $Q-\Gamma M/k=a(1-\Gamma/2^n)>0$.

external_dependencies: Coarea formula for conditioning a continuous density on a proper linear section, used in §1.
c324e86ba3893a31:01.reason: The proof of 27d3881f8bfc290c identifies the relation between the zero density of the signed exponential sum and the uniform simplex projection density in its sign regime. 564e798ecec2b61f treats conditional means for individual signed phases and transfers in balanced coefficient lists. Neither gives the coordinate-eliminated density's product comparison or equality. The present coarea and scaling computation is self-contained.
c324e86ba3893a31:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $Y_0,\dots,Y_d$ be independent unit-rate exponentials, and let the real vector $c$ have both signs. Put $V=\sum_{i=0}^d c_iY_i$, let $f=f_V(0)$ be the continuous density value, and let $b$ be the barycentric centroid of the section $\{\xi\in\Delta_d:c\cdot\xi=0\}$ of the standard barycentric simplex, with its uniform $(d-1)$-dimensional measure. For any $j$ with $c_j\ne0$, define
$$
C=\{z\in\mathbb R_+^d:\textstyle\sum_{i\ne j}(c_i/c_j)z_i\le0\},\quad
\beta_i=1-c_i/c_j,\quad Z=|c_j|f .
$$
The coarea conditional density of $(Y_i)_{i\ne j}$ at $V=0$ is $p(z)=e^{-\beta\cdot z}\mathbf 1_C(z)/Z$. Its coordinate means are $\mu_i=db_i$. With $q$ the product of exponential densities of means $\mu_i$ on the orthant,
$$
\log\frac{d^d\prod_{i\ne j}b_i}{|c_j|f}=D_{\rm KL}(p\Vert q)\ge0.
$$
Equality holds precisely when $c_j$ is the only coefficient of its sign.

c324e86ba3893a31:02.reason: The entropy draft computes the exact cap probability and density by conditioning on $Y_0+Y_1\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(2,1)$. This is the explicit separation of the two right-hand quantities in its scope paragraph, with no independent graph dependency. It refutes the comparison to $|c_j|f$ in this proper cut.
c324e86ba3893a31:02.statement: For c=(1,1,−R), R>0, the proper-cap fraction F=Pr(V≥0) is (2R+1)/(R+1)^2 and f_V(0)=R/(R+1)^2. At R=10 and either positive index j, F(1−F)=2100/14641 exceeds |c_j|f_V(0)=1210/14641.

c324e86ba3893a31:03.reason: 1618ee1d863a817a refutes arbitrary merging monotonicity for the sign probability with balanced phase totals. 564e798ecec2b61f proves a largest-positive transfer result for that probability. The present operation merges two negative coefficients, allows unbalanced phase totals, and compares a ratio using all coarea conditional means. The two exact calculations are self-contained.
c324e86ba3893a31:03.statement:
For independent unit exponentials $Y_i$ and any coefficient vector $c$ with both signs, write $V=\sum_i c_iY_i$, $F=\Pr(V\ge0)$, and
$$
\mathcal R(c)=\frac{\prod_i\mathbb E[Y_i\mid V=0]}{F(1-F)}
$$
using coarea conditioning. Replacing the two negative unit coefficients by $-2$ and $0$ changes $\mathcal R$ from $81/64$ to $6/5$ for $c=(1,1,-1,-1)$, and from $161728/129375$ to $14/11$ for $c=(1,3,-1,-1)$. The changes have opposite signs.

external_dependencies: Blaschke selection for bounded nonempty compact convex sets
c344f12be982dcb7:02.reason: 89563f7ef7a4762f gives bounded residual shapes and depth convergence in the ordinary canonical affine placement, but making its added graph coordinates integer can increase rank. 04c4009af6a7a76c instead lifts joint BM slice laws to full continuous volume on an integer graph, and only in a special offset case stays over the original base; it does not supply compact prelimit shapes with positive limiting m-volume and fixed original rank. The new construction separates component linear maps in orthogonal continuous blocks and puts the extra graph coordinates in the continuous space.
c344f12be982dcb7:02.statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $m\ge1$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^k$ be finite and nonempty and span $\mathbb R^k$ affinely. For every $\ell$ let $(K_{\ell,z})_{z\in P}$ be a compatible family of convex $m$-bodies in $\mathbb R^m$: for every anchored representation $z=\sum_a\lambda_a z_a$ in $P$, with nonnegative coefficients summing to one, $\sum_a\lambda_a K_{\ell,z_a}\subseteq K_{\ell,z}$. Put $M_\ell=\sum_z |K_{\ell,z}|_m$ and assume $|K_{\ell,z}|_m/M_\ell\to p_z>0$ for each $z$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_s$ be the dependence components generated by the nontrivial anchored representations, let $L(P)$ be the scalar space preserving all anchored representations, and write $t=\dim L(P)-k-1$ and $D=sm+t$.

In d=1 K is its own enclosing simplex and the depth is 1/2.

c6aadce19d219a98:01.reason: The beta-step conditional and mixture laws agree with the finite source formula in every coordinate dimension, including the one-point simplex.
c6aadce19d219a98:01.statement: For an integer $m\ge1$, let $\mu_m$ be uniform probability on $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$. Independently draw $W\sim\mu_m$, a uniform index $J\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $R$ with density $m(1-r)^{m-1}$ on $(0,1)$. Write $e_j$ for the standard basis vectors. Then $X=(1-R)W+Re_J$ has law $\mu_m$. Given $J=j$, its law has density $mx_j$ relative to $\mu_m$. For $V=(mW+e_J)/(m+1)$, one has $\mathbb E[X\mid W,J]=V$ and hence $\mathbb E[X\mid V,J]=\mathbb E[X\mid V]=V$.

c6aadce19d219a98:02.reason: The minimum-cell coupling gives the sharp convex-order range and the exact martingale at the endpoint. The reviewed proof adds the affine and slice-affine equality criteria.
c6aadce19d219a98:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $Z$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, and let $I$ be independent and uniform on its vertex indices. For $0\le b\le1$ set $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$. Then $Y_b\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} Z$ if and only if $b\le1/d$, where the order means $\mathbb E\phi(Y_b)\le\mathbb E\phi(Z)$ for every continuous convex $\phi$ on $\Delta_d$. Equivalently the inequality reverses for every continuous concave test.

At $b=1/d$, there is a coupling $(Y,X)$ of $Y_{1/d}$ and $Z$ with $\mathbb E[X\mid Y]=Y$ in which the minimum coordinate value and its unique index agree almost surely. The common minimum has survival function $(1-ds)_+^{d-1}$ for $s\ge0$. In fact for every $b\ge1/d$, $\mathbb E\min_j(Y_b)_j=(1-b)/(d(d-1))$, whereas $\mathbb E\min_j Z_j=1/d^2$.

At $b=0$ every test gives equality. For $0<b<1/d$ equality holds precisely for affine tests. At $b=1/d$ equality holds precisely when the test is affine on every slice $\{x\in\Delta_d:x_i=t/d,\ x_j\ge t/d\text{ for all }j\ne i\}$, for every $i$ and $0\le t\le1$. In particular the minimum is a nonaffine concave equality test at the critical step. When $d=2$ and $b=1/2$ the whole laws agree. For $d\ge3$ the critical comparison is strict for every strictly convex test.

c6aadce19d219a98:03.reason: The stationarity proof uses the exact simplex density equation and dense-grid additivity, with the scope of independent absolutely continuous steps and at least three vertices.
c6aadce19d219a98:03.statement: For an integer $m\ge3$, let $W$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, let $J$ be uniform on its vertex indices, and let $B$ have an absolutely continuous probability density $w$ on $[0,1]$. Assume the three variables are independent. Then $(1-B)W+Be_J$ is uniform on $\Delta_m$ if and only if $w(b)=m(1-b)^{m-1}$ almost everywhere. If an atom at zero is allowed, any mixture of this beta law and the unit mass at zero is stationary. For $m=2$ the constant step $B=1/2$ is also stationary.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:01.reason: A fixed whitening converts the covariance norm to the Euclidean cap law. The fixed-face theorems supply contact rigidity and the maximal occupied-face midpoint argument counts the groups in the inherited lattice.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:01.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine lattice, equal to the lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and let $d\ge1$. At each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, with $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$ is a convex representation. Write $C$ for the canonical convex hull of the lifted fibers, $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$, and $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_z}\,dX)$ for the measured fibers. Put $M=\sum_z|K_z|$, let $g_z$ be the centroid of $K_z$, and define
$$
N=d+1,\qquad
\Sigma=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}\,dX,\qquad
\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},\qquad
f(z,x)=\left(\frac{E_{C_z}(x)}{M}\right)^{1/N}.
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over parameters with positive denominator on $K$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and is zero on the own boundary. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$, the raw buffered depth $b_\varepsilon(p,y)$ is the infimum of $\mu$-masses of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(Z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of the closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (with value $M$ in base rank zero). Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K)=\max_{p\in P,\ y\in K_p}b_\varepsilon(p,y)/M$. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and suppose every old buffered maximizing mark has a proper shifted own section in every nonvertical direction, meaning the shifted plane cuts its own fiber interior. Let $Q=M\beta_\varepsilon$ and $I$ be the sampled bases at which $Q$ is attained. Then $I$ is the full lattice trace of $\operatorname{conv}I$. There are at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ cap groups, with parity counted in the inherited affine lattice of $P$. Each group $i$ is associated with a face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ and an old maximizing source over a sampled base in $\operatorname{relint}F_i$. The sets $J_i=I\cap F_i$ cover $I$. Each group consists of at most $d+1$ nonvertical caps $\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}\}$ of actual mass $Q$, with $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$, $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, and weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one. They are proper on the group source's own fiber and their thresholds are right upper $Q$-quantiles. Define $P_i(z,x)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot(z,x)$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. Then
$$
P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon f(z,x)\ge0\qquad(z\in F_i,\ x\in C_z).
$$
For every real $z\in F_i$ the zero is a unique own-interior mark $y_z$, every selected buffered quantile constraint is an equality there, and the marks are affine on $F_i$. The bodies $C_z-y_z$ and the positive energy $E_{C_z}(y_z)=E_i$ are constant on that face, so $f(z,y_z)=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:02.reason: Local strictly decreasing right quantiles and the minimum across entire current assigned fibers give the exact moving cover. Positive Hausdorff continuity uses recomputed covariance and preserves the gap at the other bases.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:02.statement:
Take a positive compatible family and fixed energy-only buffered cap groups as in the preceding parity-face theorem. In particular, $\varepsilon>0$ is fixed, $Q$ is the old raw maximum, $I$ is the set of old deepest bases, $J_i$ cover $I$, and the selected caps have fixed normals $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$ and actual mass $Q$ at thresholds $c_{ij}$. Use the same $P_i,h_i,\rho_{ij}$ as in that theorem. Let $K_z(t)$ be positive compatible bodies on the same bases with $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance as $t\downarrow0$. Write $\mu_t,M_t,\Gamma_t,f_t,b_{\varepsilon,t}$ for their actual measure, mass, covariance norm, energy-only profile and raw buffered depth. Put
$$
A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}),\qquad
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}
[P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon A_i(t)f_t(z,x)].
$$
Then $A_i(t)\to1$, $\alpha_i(t)\to0$, and the minimizing marks approach the finite old contact set $\{(z,y_z):z\in J_i\}$. For each $i,j$ let $c_{ij}(t,q)$ be the right upper $q$-quantile of $\mu_t$ in the fixed normal $N_{ij}$. For small $t$ there is a unique solution $q_i(t)$ near $Q$ to
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}(t,q_i(t))=h_i+\alpha_i(t).
$$
It tends to $Q$, and for all small $t$ one has
$$
b_{\varepsilon,t}(z,x)\le q_i(t)\quad (z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)),\qquad
M_t\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))\le\max_i q_i(t).
$$

c6bafe9ff5de0861:03.reason: The two-sided radial shell estimate and the positive minimizing-denominator floor yield uniform energy differentiation on compact interior marks. Centered covariance differentiates on the same path.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and let finitely many convex bodies $K_z(t)\subset\mathbb R^d$ move through $K_z=K_z(0)$ as $t\downarrow0$. In each old body choose an interior origin $o_z$, and let $R_z,R_{z,t}$ be the old and moving radial functions about it. Suppose $|R_{z,t}-R_z|\le Ct$ and $(R_{z,t}-R_z)/t\to r_z$ almost everywhere on the sphere. At a regular old boundary point $X=o_z+R_z(\omega)\omega$ set $v_z(X)=-r_z(\omega)n_z(X)\cdot\omega$, with $n_z$ the outward unit normal. This is the signed inward speed. Use endpoint counting measure in dimension one. Let
$$
M=\sum_z|K_z|,\quad D=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS,\quad
J=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}v_z(X)\,dS
$$
with $g_z$ the old centroids, and define $M_t,\Sigma_t,\Gamma_t$ using actual moving masses and within-fiber centroids as in the invariant energy-only buffer. For a compact $U\subset\operatorname{int}K_z$, write $a_y$ for the unique old parameter minimizing the projective energy at $y$, and set
$$
C_z(y)=\int_{\partial K_z}[1+a_y\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}v_z(X)\,dS.
$$
Then, uniformly for $y\in U$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{K_z(t)}(y)&=E_{K_z}(y)-tC_z(y)+o(t),\\
f_t(z,y)&=f(z,y)+t\,\frac{f(z,y)}N
 \left[-\frac{C_z(y)}{E_{K_z}(y)}+\frac DM\right]+o(t),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $f_t(z,y)=(E_{K_z(t)}(y)/M_t)^{1/N}$. The right derivatives at zero satisfy
$$
\dot M=-D,\qquad \dot\Sigma=(D\Sigma-J)/M,\qquad
\dot\Gamma(u)=\frac{u^{\mathsf T}\dot\Sigma u}{2\Gamma(u)}\quad(u\ne0).
$$

c6bafe9ff5de0861:04.reason: Use the energy and covariance derivatives at all old contacts, then localize every new contact minimizer to the finite old zeros. This gives the derivative as their minimum.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:04.statement:
In the exact fixed-cover continuation for the energy-only covariance buffer, assume the compatible path also satisfies the bounded signed radial hypotheses of the uniform marked-energy and covariance lemma. Use its $D,J,C_z(y)$, and for group $i$ write $E_i=E_{K_z}(y_z)$ and $f_i=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$ for the old common energy and profile at its contacts. Put
$$
J_i^{\rm cov}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}J u_{ij}.
$$
Then $A_i(t)=1+t(D-J_i^{\rm cov})/(2M)+o(t)$, and
$$
\alpha_i(t)=t\,\dot\alpha_i+o(t),\qquad
\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon f_i
\left[\min_{z\in J_i}\frac{C_z(y_z)}{NE_i}
+\frac{J_i^{\rm cov}}{2M}-\frac{(N+2)D}{2NM}\right].
$$
In the variant with the old norm held fixed and the unnormalized profile $E^{1/N}$, use the corresponding old cap groups (equivalently rescale the old buffer parameter by $M^{-1/N}$). For its fixed parameter $\varepsilon$ the formula becomes $\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon E_i^{1/N}\min_{z\in J_i}C_z(y_z)/(NE_i)$.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:05.reason: The same regular moving traces give joint cap differentiation and exact inverse quantile differentiation. The strict descent test uses every group on the same actual path.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:05.statement:
Use the exact fixed-cover continuation and its finite-contact derivative on one actual compatible signed radial path for the energy-only buffer. Put $\beta=Q/M$ and $\dot M=-D$. Suppose for each selected old cap its actual tail has the regular joint expansion
$$
\mu_t\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}+t s\}
=Q-t(L_{ij}+S_{ij}s)+o(t),\qquad S_{ij}>0,
$$
uniformly on bounded $s$ intervals. Here $L_{ij}$ is the first loss of mass at the fixed threshold. A sufficient trace condition is that each selected plane on each old fiber be a proper section, a strict full or empty cut, or a supporting section of zero $(d-1)$-dimensional measure. Under this condition $S_{ij}$ is the sum of proper section measures divided by $\lVert u_{ij}\rVert$, and $L_{ij}$ integrates the signed inward speed on the captured old boundary.

Let $B_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}$ and $\theta_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/B_i$. Then the right derivatives of the continued budgets satisfy
$$
\dot q_i=-\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}-\frac{\dot\alpha_i}{B_i},
\qquad
\left.\frac{d}{dt^+}\right|_{0}\frac{q_i(t)}{M_t}
=-\frac{\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i-\beta D}{M}.
$$
If $\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i>\beta D$ for every old group on this one path, then $\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))<\beta$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$.

c71e38de38f9f3c8:01.reason: The accepted proof identifies the cap volume for arbitrary feasible edge intercepts, including those equal to one. The through-point relation Σ λ_j/t_j=1 and AM–GM give the bound and equality; t_j=dλ_j realizes it exactly when feasible. The accepted counterexample to a global one-vertex-only formula does not affect the sign-restricted result.
c71e38de38f9f3c8:01.statement: In a full-dimensional d-simplex B of volume V, d≥1, let f(y)=0 at an interior y. If f(v_i)>0 and f(v_j)≤0 for j≠i, the edge intercept fractions t_j=f(v_i)/(f(v_i)−f(v_j)) give cap volume V∏_{j≠i}t_j≥Vd^d∏_{j≠i}λ_j(y). Equality iff t_j=dλ_j(y) for each j≠i, which is feasible in this sign class iff all those barycentrics are ≤1/d. Vertices on the cutting plane are allowed.

c71e38de38f9f3c8:02.reason: Accepted f75e1f526e17ab44 treats intercepts after specifying a one-vertex cap. This result proves a uniform quantitative neighborhood of centers and unit normals where that hypothesis holds. Combining with the endpoint-credit theorem uses the smaller of the two oriented neighborhood radii; this proof of the sign pattern itself has no predecessor.
c71e38de38f9f3c8:02.statement: Let $B=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and $\lambda_i$ be its barycentric functions. Suppose $|\lambda_k(y)-1/N|\le1/(2N)$ for every $k$. For any $i$ and $\lVert v\rVert\le1/(8N)$ the margin $\lambda_i(x)-\lambda_i(y)+v\cdot(x-y)$ at vertex $i$ is at least $1/(4N)$ and at every other vertex at most $-1/(4N)$. In particular the same one-vertex sign pattern holds for every through-$y$ cap whose unit normal has distance at most $1/(8N\sqrt d)$ from $\nabla\lambda_i/\lVert\nabla\lambda_i\rVert$.

c71e38de38f9f3c8:03.reason: The accepted one-vertex intercept result supplies the middle-cap volume lower bound. Accepted 287cc87c3b427501 chooses a related mark via a differentiable section estimate and gives an all-direction existence theorem for unspecified smallness. The new explicit product estimate retains the finite quadratic coefficient, works for arbitrary credits, and gives the actual local result only with the same-batch incidence and endpoint hypotheses.
c71e38de38f9f3c8:03.statement:
Let $B$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V>0$, $d\ge1$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, and let $N=d+1$ and $\Gamma=(d/N)^d$. Given credits $0\le c_i\le a$ with $0\le a/(\Gamma V)\le1$, put $\bar c=N^{-1}\sum_i c_i$ and choose $y$ with $\lambda_i(y)=1/N+(c_i-\bar c)/(N\Gamma V)$. Then $y$ is interior and
$$Vd^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)+c_i\ge\Gamma V+\bar c-\frac{2^d-d-1}{\Gamma}\frac{a^2}{V}.$$
Every through-$y$ cap that isolates vertex $i$ on its positive side has volume at least the displayed product term. The inequality is equality in dimension one.

In dimension $d\ge2$, if $\sum_i c_i\ge Ja$ for $J=\lceil N/2\rceil$, $0\le\kappa<J/N$, and $a/V\le\Gamma(J/N-\kappa)/(2^d-d-1)$, this lower bound with credit is at least $\Gamma V+\kappa a$. In the standard frame of the uniform endpoint-credit theorem, use its credits and mass conditions, and also require $a/(\Gamma V)\le1/2$. The actual three-fiber mass is then at least $\Gamma V+\kappa a$ in the common oriented neighborhoods of unit radius $\min\{\delta/(24R),1/(8N)\}/\sqrt d$ about each vertex-side facet normal, for every real tilt.

c72585e587868cec:01.reason: The limit certificate gives v(0)=Q/M by its row Jensen argument or by the constant-body specialization of 569a05581be52e0e. The maximum of the finitely many raw upper bounds is Q−t min_i ell_i+o(t); dividing by M_t yields the displayed bound. Any finite list of complete paths gives the minimum of their upper bounds. This is the elementary upper companion to the scalar lower envelope; it requires the stated actual cover, not a separate path chosen for each group.
c72585e587868cec:01.statement: For the optimized normalized actual buffered depth v(t)=inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t on a positive compatible body path at fixed ε>0, any admissible comparison path U_t^a gives v(t)≤Q_t(U_t^a)/M_t. If U_0^a=L is a certified optimizer and continued groups for this same path cover the full sampled set together with persistent slack covers, with raw group masses Q−t ell_i+o(t) and M_t=M−tD+o(t), then limsup_{t↓0}(v(t)−Q/M)/t≤−min_i(ell_i−(Q/M)D)/M.

c72585e587868cec:02.reason: 569a05581be52e0e gives the pushforward and the logarithmic identity in its continuity proof. 20210aa9d661295a and 3dd858960f824a5d give the proper-cap and whole-fiber inputs, with b3c0088cf09b2894 for scalar continuity across actual bodies. The new use is a weighted inverse of actual mark-depth functions. 66947afeef056d3b optimizes log mass at fixed cap-bound marks and does not provide this through-mark depth comparison.
c72585e587868cec:02.statement:
Assume the actual compatible fixed-base bodies and old positive continuous log-normalized parameter $L$ satisfy the finite volume certificate hypotheses of 569a05581be52e0e at a fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular the contact probabilities $\rho_i$ have weights $\sigma_i>0$ summing to one, full means $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ and $L$-means $L_i=L(Y_i)$, and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Each $Y_i$ is an old maximizing mark with raw depth $Q$, strictly below its closed pure-base depth. Let $K_z(t)\to K_z$ be positive compatible bodies in the fixed-base fiber Hausdorff topology as $t\downarrow0$, with mixed volume $dm_t$ and total $M_t$. Define $v(t)=\inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t$ over current positive continuous concave, log-normalized parameters. Choose $U_t$ with $Q_t(U_t)/M_t\le v(t)+t^2$.

Choose a common inward fractional contraction $a_t\to0$, $0\le a_t<1$, of the old fibers about their old centroids $g_z$ so that its image $I_{t,z}$ is contained in $K_z(t)$. Let $T_t(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-a_t)(X-g_z))$ and $j_t=(1-a_t)^d$. Let $Y_i^t$ be the mean of $(T_t)_\#\rho_i$, and $B_i(t,s)$ its actual raw buffered depth with scalar parameter value $s$. On a common interval of raw depths about $Q$, for all sufficiently small $t$ there is a unique positive inverse $s_i(t,q)$ of this scalar depth. Define $H_t(q)=\sum_i\sigma_i\log(s_i(t,q)/L_i)$ and let $\chi_t$ denote its local inverse. If
$$
\xi_t=-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log U_t\,dX,
$$
then $H_t(Q_t(U_t))\ge\xi_t$ and $Q_t(U_t)\ge\chi_t(\xi_t)$.

Let $h_t=\sum_z|K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}|$ and let $B\ge1$ be a common sampled upper bound for $U_t$. Then $\xi_t\ge-h_t\log B/(Mj_t)$ and $v(t)\ge\chi_t(-h_t\log B/(Mj_t))/M_t-t^2$. More precisely, for positive continuous reference values $L_{\rm ref,t}$ on the sampled moving fibers that converge to $L$ along all convergent sampled marks, we have $\sup_{S_t}(U_t-L_{\rm ref,t})_+\to0$ and
$$
\xi_t\ge-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log L_{\rm ref,t}\,dX+o(h_t).
$$
If the moving endpoint on the ray through a regular old boundary point $X$ from $g_z$ is $g_z+(1-b_{z,t}(X))(X-g_z)$, assume $|b_{z,t}(X)|=O(t)$ uniformly and $b_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/[n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)]$ surface-almost everywhere, where $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. With $a_t=ct+o(t)$ and $H_z(X)=n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)$, containment gives $cH_z-v_z\ge0$ and
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\xi_t}{t}\ge
c_{\rm col}:=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)[v_z(X)-cH_z(X)]\,dS.
$$

If, independently, $H_t(Q+tr)=t(A_0 r+B_0)+o(t)$ uniformly for bounded $r$, with $A_0>0$, and $\liminf\xi_t/t\ge c_0$, then $\liminf (Q_t(U_t)-Q)/t\ge(c_0-B_0)/A_0$. If also $M_t=M-tD+o(t)$, then
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(t)-Q/M}{t}
\ge\frac{(c_0-B_0)/A_0+(Q/M)D}{M}.
$$

c72585e587868cec:03.reason: The accepted convergence yields the interior and uniform maximum bounds. One-sided boundary control follows by concavity along a segment to a fixed interior point and continuity of L. The lower envelope draft proves this together with the exact inverse comparison.
c72585e587868cec:03.statement: For the same near-optimizers, let h_t be total collar volume and B≥1 a uniform sampled parameter upper bound. Then ξ_t≥−h_t log B/(Mj_t). In particular v(t)≥χ_t(−h_t log B/(M j_t))/M_t−t².

c7a0c159c6cf35f0:01.statement:

At an angle $\theta$ let $J(\theta)=\{z:r_z(\theta)>0\}$, $A(\theta)=\{a:g_a(\theta)=0\}$, and
$$
L(\theta)=\{v:v_z=0\text{ for }z\notin J(\theta),\quad q_a\cdot v=0\text{ for }a\in A(\theta)\}.
$$
At $R$-almost every angle the whole exposed face in each fiber in $J(\theta)$ has a strict side for every cap, and $r(\theta)\in L(\theta)$.

The exact patterns $(A,J,(I_{jz})_{j,z\in J})$, where $I_{jz}$ is the strict inside bit of cap $j$, admit a countable exhaustion up to $R$-null sets by bounded nonatomic source measures $\nu$ dominated by every $R_z$ for $z\in J$. Each has a compact interval guard of length less than $\pi$, on which the inactive Jensen gaps have a common positive lower bound and the entire exposed faces for $z\in J$ have the prescribed strict cap signs with a positive margin. For each such source and $v$ in its fixed pattern kernel, there exists a compactly supported signed feasible support variation $t v_z\phi$ in that guard, feasible for both small signs of $t$. c7a0c159c6cf35f0:02.statement:

Compatibility is given by finitely many Jensen inequalities $g_a=\sum_z q_{az}h_z\ge0$ for the support functions. Write $R_z=h_z+h_z''$, $R=\sum_z R_z^{\rm diff}$ and $r_z=dR_z^{\rm diff}/dR$. $$
\sum_zW_zv_z^2\ge0\quad(v\in L(\theta)),\qquad
r(\theta)\in L(\theta),\qquad
\sum_z W_z r_z(\theta)v_z=0\quad(v\in L(\theta))
$$
for $R$-almost every $\theta$. In every guarded pattern with positive source mass the same quadratic form is nonnegative on the corresponding fixed kernel. For every compactly supported Green-potential acceleration within such a guard, with only the two endpoint moments imposed, the common weights annihilate its first-order area and cap response in the combination $\delta M-\sum_j\lambda_j\delta M_j$.

$$
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j\bigl(I_{jz}(\theta_0+)-I_{jz}(\theta_0-)\bigr)\rho_z(\theta_0)^2=0.

A transverse crossing of any cap with positive weight has a simultaneous crossing of another cap with positive weight and opposite sign.

c7b6ab042f325988:01.statement:
Let $K_z$ be the positive $d$-dimensional integer fibers of a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with volumes $V_z$. Fix any two couplings of the uniform fiber probabilities for the respective relations, and any joint gluing over their common uniform $K_s$ coordinate. Let $Y_1,Y_2$ be the resulting continuous barycentric outputs, both in $K_p$.

For a closed ambient halfspace $H$, let $F_r=\{(p,Y_r)\in H\}$, $f_r=\Pr(F_r)$, $o=\Pr(F_1\cap F_2)$, and let $U_z$ denote the captured volume at source base $z$. Put
$$
a=V_s,\quad b=\min_{z\in A}V_z,\quad c=\min_{z\in B}V_z,\quad
c_1=\min(a,b),\quad c_2=\min(a,c),\quad c_{12}=\min(a,b+c),\quad
\rho=c_1+c_2-c_{12}.
$$
Then $\rho\ge0$ and
$$
U_s+\sum_{z\in A}U_z+\sum_{z\in B}U_z\ \ge\
c_1f_1+c_2f_2-\rho o.
$$
This is the sharp pointwise cost rule based only on the two implications that a target hit forces a hit of a source in its relation. Compared to maximizing $\theta_1 f_1+\theta_2 f_2$ subject to $0\le\theta_1\le b$, $0\le\theta_2\le c$, and $\theta_1+\theta_2\le a$, the increase in the right-hand side is exactly $\rho[\min(f_1,f_2)-o]$. It is strictly positive precisely when $\rho>0$ and both directed crossing events have positive probability.

With $q_r(x)=\Pr(F_r\mid X_s=x)$, the bracket is at least $\min\{\mathbb E(q_1-q_2)_+,\mathbb E(q_2-q_1)_+\}$ for every gluing, and equals $\min\{\mathbb E[q_1(1-q_2)],\mathbb E[q_2(1-q_1)]\}$ under conditional independence. These assertions hold simultaneously on any prescribed finite cap family for one gluing.

c8365ce16304e154:01.statement:
Let $F\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a compact convex body with $x\in\operatorname{int}F$ and $p>1$. The minimum
$$
B=\min_a\int_F[1+a\cdot(z-x)]_+^p\,dz
$$
has a unique parameter $a_p$. For $h=[1+a_p\cdot(z-x)]_+$ one has
$$
\int_F(z-x)h^{p-1}\,dz=0,\qquad \int_Fh^p\,dz=\int_Fh^{p-1}\,dz=B>0.
$$
Among nonnegative probability densities on $F$ of mean $x$, $h^{p-1}/B$ uniquely minimizes the integral of the power $p/(p-1)$, with minimum $B^{-1/(p-1)}$. In dimension zero use the unit counting measure on the tangent point, the empty parameter and $B=1$.

Then the maximum mass of a density in $[0,1]$ on $F\times Q$ of finite first moments and centroid $(x,v)$ is
$$
T=\frac{(k+1)^k}{k!\,k^k}J_*(v)B.
$$
The unique optimizer almost everywhere is the indicator of the bounded cap $k n_v\cdot q\le (k+1)[1+a\cdot(z-x)]$ in $F\times Q$. Its normalized marginal on $F$ is $h^k/B$, the unique minimum-power density of mean $x$ with exponent $(k+1)/k$, and the conditional normal mean is $h(z)v$ wherever the marginal is positive. The unique minimizer of the hinge integral $\int_{F\times Q}[1+u\cdot(z-x)-b\cdot(q-v)]_+\,dz\,dq$ is $(u,b)=((k+1)a,k n_v)$, and its value is $T$.

$$

=\frac{(k+1)^k}{k!\,k^k}J_*(v)B.

$$

\frac{|A\cap H_{\ell,z_A}|_d}{a}\frac{|B\cap H_{\ell,z_B}|_d}{b}.

Any affine functional of the base and lift which is bounded above on the state space and attains its upper bound at the starting state stays at that bound along the chain.

c9f582e034f0948d:03.statement:
Let a compact convex hull $C$ realize positive $d$-dimensional compact convex sections at a finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, with summed fiber-volume measure $\mu$, total mass $M$ and maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth $\beta$. Put $Q=\beta M$ and select one critical circuit through an interior maximizing mark at each deepest base $p$. Write each original cap as $H_j(b_j)=\{(z,x):a_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$, with unit $u_j$, old mass $Q$ and positive circuit weights $\rho_j$ satisfying $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=0$. Consider compact convex inner deformations $C_t\subseteq C$ at the same bases, with positive fibers and persistent balls about the anchor marks. Write $\mu_t$ for the restricted measure, $R_t=C\setminus C_t$ and $\varepsilon_t=\mu(R_t)>0$, with $\varepsilon_t\to0$.

For each selected cap the inverse threshold $b_j^t(q)$ is well defined near $q=Q$, and $b_j^t(Q-\beta\varepsilon_t)-b_j=O(\varepsilon_t)$. If all selected deepest circuits satisfy
$$
\sum_{j\in C_p}\rho_j[b_j^t(Q-\beta\varepsilon_t)-b_j]<0,
$$
then the new actual maximum normalized depth is strictly below $\beta$ for all sufficiently small such $t$.

Let $S_j^+$ be the summed proper section area plus inside supporting section area of the old cap and $S_j^-$ the summed proper section area plus outside supporting section area, counting endpoints and proper point sections in dimension one. The signs refer to increasing and decreasing the cap threshold, respectively. Suppose, along the path or a sequence, $\mu(R_t\cap H_j(b_j))/\varepsilon_t\to\iota_j$ and for every fixed $A>0$,
$$
\mu\big(R_t\cap\{|a_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x-b_j|\le A\varepsilon_t\}\big)=o(\varepsilon_t)
$$
for each selected cap. Then
$$
\frac{b_j^t(Q-\beta\varepsilon_t)-b_j}{\varepsilon_t}\longrightarrow
\frac{(\beta-\iota_j)_+}{S_j^+}-\frac{(\iota_j-\beta)_+}{S_j^-}.
$$
Denote by $\Phi_{C_p}(\iota)$ the sum of these limits with weights $\rho_j$ over that circuit. Strict negativity of all these sums implies descent for all sufficiently small terms of the path or sequence. For $S_j^+=S_j^-=S_j$ a sum is negative exactly when
$$
\frac{\sum_j(\rho_j/S_j)\iota_j}{\sum_j\rho_j/S_j}>\beta.
$$
For binary incidences $I_j\in\{0,1\}$, with possibly unequal slopes, it is negative exactly when
$$
\frac{\sum_{I_j=1}\rho_j/S_j^-}{\sum_{I_j=1}\rho_j/S_j^-+\sum_{I_j=0}\rho_j/S_j^+}>\beta.
$$

c9f582e034f0948d:04.statement:
Let a finite compatible family of positive compact convex fibers have total summed fiber-volume $M$ and maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth $\beta$, and let $C$ be its lifted hull. For an exposing affine functional $\ell$ put $h=\max_C\ell$, $F=C\cap\{\ell=h\}$ and $C_t=C\cap\{\ell\le h-t\}$. Assume $F$ contains no whole measured fiber, and the removed mixed mass $\varepsilon_t$ is positive for small $t>0$.

Select one critical circuit at each deepest base. If all selected cap boundaries avoid $F$, use the constant binary incidence $I_j$ of $F$ in the cap. A strict binary-incidence score greater than $\beta$ at every selected circuit, with weights $\rho_j/S_j^-$ for inside vertices and $\rho_j/S_j^+$ for outside ones, implies strict descent along $C_t$. Here the score is the total inside weight divided by the sum of inside and outside weights. At an unrestricted fiberwise Hausdorff local minimum, for every exposed point $v$ in the measured family there is a deepest base at which every critical circuit whose boundaries avoid $v$ has score at most $\beta$. A circuit family that is empty satisfies the universal statement.

For positive polytopal fibers and $d\ge2$, the conclusion at a local minimum applies to all critical circuits at some deepest base, for each exposed vertex $v$ and each chosen exposing functional, if the score inequality is replaced by $\Phi_{C_p}(\iota)\ge0$ from the two-slope response and the incidences on cap boundaries are the actual tangent-cone fractions. For a general convex exposed point in $d\ge2$, any fixed finite selected menu satisfies the slab hypothesis, and the two-slope response applies on each sequence of positive trims along which its incidence vector converges. At a fixed-complexity local minimum the same necessary assertions require admissibility of the corresponding supporting-plane trims.

ca19899f75c1a20d:01.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a martingale coupling from a finite compactly supported measure $
u$ to $\eta$ in $\mathbb R^m$, and $\Phi$ a finite continuous convex function on $\mathbb R^m$. If $\int\Phi\,d

cb4b6b63cebf7744:01.statement:
Let $\mu$ be the sum of Lebesgue $d$-volume on finitely many compact full-dimensional convex fibers, $d\ge1$. For $L=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ with $u\ne0$, put $H=\{L\ge0\}$, $c=\mu(H)$, $\Psi=\int L_+\,d\mu$, and $T=\int L_+^2\,d\mu$. The last two functions are continuously differentiable in the affine margin parameters, with $D\Psi[\dot L]=\int_H\dot L\,d\mu$ and $DT[\dot L]=2\int_H L\dot L\,d\mu$. Call a cap regular if on every fiber the cut plane meets its interior, is strictly separated from it, or meets it in a supporting section of zero $(d-1)$-measure. At a regular cap let $\tau=\sum_z\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{K_z\cap\{L=0\}}/\lVert u\rVert$, with the base label attached, so $Dc[\dot L]=\int\dot L\,d\tau$. For a $C^1$ cost $\Phi(c,\Psi,T)$ its derivative is the affine moment of the signed measure
$$
\Phi_c\tau+\Phi_\Psi\mu|_H+2\Phi_T L\mu|_H.
$$
An invertible continuous affine change with common absolute fiber determinant $\Delta$ and a unimodular change of integer bases sends the moments of the same margin to $(\Delta c,\Delta\Psi,\Delta T)$. Multiplication of the margin by $s>0$ sends them to $(c,s\Psi,s^2T)$.

cb7ea417552f0084:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y,o\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $K_\varepsilon$ be nested compact convex bodies for $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $K_0=K$. Suppose that for some $C\ge0$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
o+(1-C\varepsilon)(K-o)\subseteq K_\varepsilon\subseteq K.
$$
For $x\in\partial K$, write the radial endpoint of $K_\varepsilon$ on the ray from $o$ through $x$ as $o+(1-t_\varepsilon(x))(x-o)$. At a regular boundary point $x$, let $n(x)$ be its unique outward unit normal and set $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on $\partial K$. Assume that for a bounded measurable $v$,
$$
\frac{t_\varepsilon(x)}{\varepsilon}\longrightarrow
\frac{v(x)}{n(x)\cdot(x-o)}
\qquad\text{for $dS$ almost every }x.
$$
Then $v\ge0$ almost everywhere. Take $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ for a fixed $w\in\mathbb R^d$. For a body $L$ and $q\in\operatorname{int}L$, let
$$
T_L(q)=\max\left\{\int_L f(x)\,dx:\ 0\le f\le1,\ f\text{ measurable},\
                       \int_L(x-q)f(x)\,dx=0\right\}.
$$
Set $T=T_K(y)$ and let $U$ be the compact nonempty set of minimizers of $G_0(u)=\int_K[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+\,dx$, where $[a]_+=\max(a,0)$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, $y_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{int}K_\varepsilon$. The following right derivative exists, and the minimum is attained:
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=\min_{u\in U}\left\{
-\int_{\partial K}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{1}
$$
When $y$ differs from the centroid $g_K$, $U$ is a singleton. When $y=g_K$, put $V=|K|$, $D=\int_{\partial K}v\,dS$ and $B=\int_{\partial K}(x-y)v(x)\,dS(x)$. For the Minkowski gauge $p_{K-y}(z)=\inf\{t\ge0:z\in t(K-y)\}$, (1) becomes
$$

cb7ea417552f0084:06.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, $n\ge0$, and let the positive-volume $d$-dimensional fibers $K_{z,\varepsilon}$, $z\in P$, be those of an actual nested convex deformation with fixed measured sites $P$. Assume each fiber satisfies the homothet and almost-everywhere radial speed hypotheses of the physical retained-mass derivative theorem, with old fiber $K_z$ and inward speed $v_z$. Let
$$
M_\varepsilon=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{z,\varepsilon}|,\qquad
M=M_0,\qquad D_{\rm mix}=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS .
$$
Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and prescribe $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ in that fiber. Let $U_p$ be the old optimizing hinge set for $T=T_{K_p}(y)$ and put $\tau=T/M$. The right derivative is
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}
\frac{T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y_\varepsilon)}{M_\varepsilon}
=\frac1M\min_{u\in U_p}\left\{
\tau D_{\rm mix}
-\int_{\partial K_p}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v_p(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{6}
$$
It is nonnegative exactly when every row in braces is nonnegative. Off the centroid there is a single row. At $y=g_{K_p}$ the criterion is exactly
$$
\tau D_{\rm mix}-D_p-p_{K_p-y}(-B_p-|K_p|w)\ge0,\qquad
D_p=\int_{\partial K_p}v_p\,dS,\quad
B_p=\int_{\partial K_p}(x-y)v_p\,dS .
\tag{7}
$$
When $K_p$ is a polytope and $y=g_{K_p}$, the minimum can be taken at the finitely many vertices of $U_p=\{u:1+u\cdot(a-y)\ge0\text{ for every vertex }a\text{ of }K_p\}$. These are linear response rows when the actual physical speeds and prescribed velocity depend linearly on deformation parameters.

One actual setting for such averaging is the single-baseline case of accepted fact 84cd8a85417b0d7a. Use one fixed continuous-in-normal, affine-in-base support baseline satisfying its majorization hypotheses; average the nonnegative convex cut fields on that baseline before constructing the body. For a Borel probability average, assume a nonempty compact metric field parameter space and joint continuity of the fields, and average prescribed velocities integrable in that parameter. The response in (6) is then the average of individual responses off the centroid; at the centroid it is the minimum of the averaged rows.

For a conditional use of (6), define depth as the infimum of the physical mixed masses of closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark, and deepest points as the maximum-depth points on $\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_{p,\varepsilon}$. For this maximum, define $T_L(q)$ at boundary marks by the same mass and moment constraints; it is zero there since a supporting hyperplane through $q$ is Lebesgue-null and every feasible density with barycenter $q$ must be concentrated on that hyperplane. Suppose the secondary maximum $S(\varepsilon)$ of $T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y)/M_\varepsilon$ among deepest points exists for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$. Assume a fixed nonempty finite list of paths $(p_j,y_j(\varepsilon))$, each deepest for all such $\varepsilon$, with $p_j\in P$, $y_j(0)\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_j}$ and $y_j(\varepsilon)=y_j(0)+\varepsilon w_j+o(\varepsilon)$. Assume every secondary maximizer for small $\varepsilon>0$ lies on a listed path. Let $\tau_j=T_{K_{p_j}}(y_j(0))/M$ and $b_j$ be the derivative (6) on path $j$. Then
$$
S(\varepsilon)=\tau_*+\varepsilon\max_{j:\tau_j=\tau_*}b_j+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad \tau_*=\max_j\tau_j .
\tag{8}
$$
This gives the finite right derivative at zero if and only if $\tau_*=S(0)$, equivalently if at least one listed path begins at an old secondary maximizer. Without this equality, (8) is the right-hand expansion about the branch limit.

Use $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$, and put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$. Assume $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, each $A$ cut $v_i\cdot x=-1$ is proper, and each ambient cap $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ captures zero area in $B$ and attains the genuine raw depth $Q$ at $(0,0)$, computed over all containing closed ambient halfspaces. Write $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, $b=|B|$, $M=a+k+b$, and let $u\le v\le w$ be the three sorted $A$ cap areas. Then $B\subseteq T$, and
$$
a\le w+v+u/4,\qquad k\le9Q/4-u-v-w/4,\qquad
w\le2Q/3,\qquad Q\ge4k/9.
$$
Consequently $Q/M\ge4k/(11k+9b)$, so $k\ge9b/7$ suffices for $Q/M\ge2/9$. If $Q\le2M/9$, then $Q\le4b/7$ and $k\le9b/7$. If $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$ is the aligned triangle, then $Q/M>4/17>2/9$.

cd3cb3fa09220cc8:01.statement:
Let $q(z)=Bz+c$ be affine and let finitely many separately movable cap occurrences have margins $u_i\cdot(x-q(z))$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}\{u_i\}$ in $\mathbb R^d$. They cover all of $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, and they still do after independent sufficiently small changes of their continuous normals and any change to one common affine meeting section. Keeping only a common ambient point does not give this conclusion.

On finitely many actual positive compact convex fibers, suppose the cuts of one such cap are proper or strictly full/empty. Let $R_i=\sum_z\int(x-q(z))\,d\tau_{iz}$, using full proper-section coarea $d\tau_{iz}=d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u_i\|$ and counting measure when $d=1$. A normal change with velocity $v_i$ at fixed $q$ has derivative $v_i\cdot R_i$, and $u_i\cdot R_i=0$. If $R_i\ne0$, there is a two-sided admissible angular motion of that cap alone that strictly decreases its mass to first order. Stationarity of a positively weighted cap sum under these independent motions forces $R_i=0$ for every positive multiplier.

cd833c78fb705a2e:01.statement:
Let $D\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^D$ with convex support $K=\operatorname{supp}\mu$, and suppose every affine hyperplane has zero $\mu$-mass. Assume there is a fixed $g>0$ such that every closed convex subset $L\subseteq K$ of positive $\mu$-mass contains a point $y$ satisfying $\mu(L\cap H)\ge g\mu(L)$ for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$.

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be a finite cover of $K$ by closed halfspaces with nonzero normals, with $m\ge1$, and let $A_i=\mu(H_i)$. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\mu(K)\le\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{g},
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
\tag{1}
$$

For ordinary volume on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$, write $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(K)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$. Then (1) holds with $g=\gamma_D$ and $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$. In particular, for $a=\min_i A_i$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a.
\tag{2}
$$
Arrange the cap masses in decreasing order and append zeros if $m<3$. For $D\ge2$,
$$
A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V,
\tag{3}
$$
where $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$. For $D=1$, $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

cd9374750b11bd94:04.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V>0$ and volume centroid zero. Let $0<r\le s$, and for $u\ne0$ define $F_u(t)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|/V$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

For every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)\ge\Phi_d(r,s).
$$
If $d\ge2$ and $s>r$, then $\Phi_d(r,s)>2\Gamma_d r^d$. For each fixed $u\ne0$ the minimum of the left side over $t\in\mathbb R$ is at most $r^d$. It equals $r^d$ and is attained at a finite threshold if $s\ge dr$, which includes every $0<r\le s$ in dimension one.

For the supplied array with just $rK$ at base $-1$ and $sK$ at base $1$, the raw source depth at $(0,0)$ is at least $V\Phi_d(r,s)$, and is exactly $Vr^d$ if $s\ge dr$. Here raw source depth is the infimum, over closed ambient halfspaces containing $(0,0)$, of the sum of the volumes captured from the two supplied sources.

cd9374750b11bd94:05.reason: The two retained endpoint copies are at distinct integer bases and the centroid midpoint of their Minkowski sum lies in the retained middle copy. Each containing halfspace pays the accepted two-endpoint bound and the full-mass centroid bound on the disjoint middle fiber.
cd9374750b11bd94:05.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional, compact and convex with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Suppose that for $p\in\mathbb Z^n$, $v\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}$, $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb R^d$ and $0<r\le s$, the actual fibers $C_{p-v}$ and $C_{p+v}$ contain $a_-+rK$ and $a_++sK$, respectively. Put $g=(a_-+a_+)/2$ and $q=(r+s)/2$. Then $g+qK\subseteq C_p$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

Every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(p,g)$ captures total $d$-volume at least
$$
V\bigl[\Phi_d(r,s)+\Gamma_d q^d\bigr]
$$
from the three retained copies on the distinct bases $p-v,p,p+v$. In particular this lower bounds the raw depth of $(p,g)$ for $C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

cda9653e9d3e6d40:04.statement:
At an attained all-positive minimum of normalized mixed closed-halfspace depth $\beta>0$ in the fixed lattice-complete nonhollow projection, bounded individual-facet class of 2ed51dd7d9c37042, use its compressed assigned cover with at most $2^n$ deepest-origin circuits and separate slack local circuits on the other bases. The initial continuous normals are unit, and the moving ones need only be nonzero.

There is one joint objective-one stress with nonnegative cap multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$ zero on slack budgets and nonnegative assigned multipliers $\eta_{ip}$ zero on strict coverage rows. Its cap covectors use full proper section measure and a common measurable allocation on each coincident facet for the body and the section. Let $S_{ij},Z_{ij},X_{ij}$ be the total mass and base and continuous first moments of each resulting full mixed section measure. For $t_i=\sum_p\eta_{ip}$ there are vectors $q_i$ with
$$
\lambda_{ij}S_{ij}=\rho_{ij}t_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij}Z_{ij}=\rho_{ij}\sum_p\eta_{ip}p,\qquad
\lambda_{ij}X_{ij}=\rho_{ij}q_i,\qquad

$$
For each stressed group $t_i>0$, all its cap multipliers are positive and the effective sections have one common full centroid on every group plane, with coordinates $(\sum_p\eta_{ip}p/t_i,q_i/t_i)$. Its continuous coordinate differs from the continuous coordinate of the $\eta$-weighted average of any assigned globally deepest marks by an element of $\bigcap_j\ker u_{ij}$. If the continuous rank is $d$, the two points coincide and their normalized ambient depth is exactly $\beta$. For lower rank the asserted comparison is modulo this common kernel.

cdad0ee8b68e978a:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_1,\dots,H_N$ cover $K$ up to a Lebesgue-null set. Write $J_+=\{j:|K\cap H_j|_d>0\}$. Then $K\subset\bigcup_{j\in J_+}H_j$. The same holds if some $H_j$ are the whole space or the empty set.

In particular, if $|K\cap H_i|_d=0$ and $F_i=K\cap\partial H_i$ is a supporting face, then for every nonnegative $\mathcal H^{d-1}$-measurable $w$ on $F_i$,
$$
\int_{F_i}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
\le\sum_{j\in J_+}\int_{F_i\cap H_j}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ use counting measure. This applies separately on every positive fiber of a finite closed ambient mixed cover.

ce2469e6ba848252:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite, with compact convex positive $d$-volume fibers, and let $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, with unit $u_i\in V\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, define finitely many closed caps covering the whole continuous space over each base in $P$. In the attained-span chart, allow free offsets and base tilts, independent normal variations on the unit sphere in $V$, and one common ambient rotation. Suppose there is a consistent Fritz–John stress with objective multiplier zero, cap-budget multipliers $r_i\ge0$, coverage multipliers $\eta_z\ge0$, and selected effective coarea measures $\tau_i$ on the actual sections $\{L_i=0\}$, with moments $(S_i,Z_i,X_i)=\int(1,z,x)\,d\tau_i$. At each $\eta_z>0$ let the coverage feature be represented by a probability law $\nu_z$ on active saddle pairs $(x,\lambda)$ with $x\in V$, $\lambda$ in the cap-index simplex, $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$, $L_k(z,x)\le0$ for every $k$, and $\lambda_iL_i(z,x)=0$. Write $p_{zi}=\int\lambda_i\,d\nu_z$ and $q_{zi}=\int\lambda_ix\,d\nu_z$. Then
$$
r_i(S_i,Z_i,P_VX_i)=\sum_z\eta_z(p_{zi},zp_{zi},q_{zi}),
\qquad
\sum_i r_i S_i u_i=0,\quad
\sum_i r_i u_i Z_i^\top=0,\quad
\sum_i r_i X_i u_i^\top=0.
$$
For every $i,k$ one has $r_i\int L_k\,d\tau_i=\sum_z\eta_z\int\lambda_iL_k(z,x)\,d\nu_z\le0$, with equality for $k=i$. When $r_iS_i>0$, the section barycenter in $\mathbb R^n\times V$ is an average of its assigned contacts and lies in all closed cap complements. Its base coordinate need not be integer. The individual continuous-moment identity is asserted only after projection to $V$.

For a cap $i$ of mass strictly between $0$ and $M$, suppose its selected effective trace $\tau_i$ is the full geometric coarea trace on the retained bases and $S_i=\tau_i(\mathbb R^{m+d})>0$. Rotate continuous coordinates so $u_i=e_d$ and write $x=(\xi,t)$. The shear $t'=t+a_i\cdot z-b_i$ and deletion of $t'=0$ turn the section into a convex body in $\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^{d-1}$, whose mixed $(d-1)$-volume is exactly the image of $\tau_i$. If an unnormalized nonzero continuous normal is used for the defining cap, the coarea trace is the corresponding constant $1/\lVert u_i\rVert$ times mixed section volume after dividing its margin by $\lVert u_i\rVert$. Each cap $k$ restricts in the unit-normal coordinates to
$$
(a_k-u_{k,d}a_i)\cdot z+u_{k,\perp}\cdot\xi\ge b_k-u_{k,d}b_i.
$$
If the depth bound $\gamma_{d-1}/2^m$ holds for ordinary mixed $(d-1)$-volume on convex bodies in this reduced dimension, where $\gamma_0=1$, then some $k\ne i$ satisfies $\tau_i(H_k)\ge(\gamma_{d-1}/2^m)S_i$. ce31fbbf06cede9c:03.statement:
Let \(n\ge0\) and \(d\ge1\). Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(K_p\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in P\), be convex bodies satisfying the anchored inclusions
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i}\subseteq K_q
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_i\ge0,\quad\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in P.
$$
Put \(S=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_p\), let \(\mu\) be the sum of fiber volumes on \(S\), and let \(D_\mu(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)\) over closed ambient halfspaces. Write \(Q=\max_{Y\in S}D_\mu(Y)\), \(D=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n+d}:D_\mu(Y)\ge Q\}\), and
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{a:\ 1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ \forall x\in K}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx
\quad (y\in\operatorname{int}K).
$$
Then \(Q>0\) is attained, \(D\) is compact and convex, and every \((p,y)\in D\cap S\) has \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\). The positive number
$$
R=\max_{(p,y)\in D\cap S}E_{K_p}(y)^{1/d}
$$
is attained. Its attaining bases \(J\) satisfy \(J=\operatorname{conv}(J)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), with a unique attaining mark \(y_p\) at each \(p\in J\). For every \(p_i\in J\) and positive weights \(\lambda_i\) summing to one with \(q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in\mathbb Z^n\),
$$
q\in J,\qquad y_q=\sum_i\lambda_i y_{p_i},\qquad
K_q=\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i},\qquad
K_{p_i}-y_{p_i}=K_q-y_q\quad\text{for every }i.
$$
If \(k(J)\) is the number of occupied parities modulo \(2\mathbb Z^n\) and \(M_J=\sum_{p\in J}|K_p|\), then \(Q\ge (d/(d+1))^d M_J/k(J)\).

Z_i=K\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{x:v_j\cdot x<0\},\qquad r_i=|R_i|.

For any such cover, in the normalization $h_D(u_i)=1$ there is a width contact stress with objective multiplier $\alpha_0=1$ and all cap-budget multipliers zero. On each fiber $p$ use the simplex centroid $g$, probability weights $1/(d+1)$ on that fiber's canonical caps, and $\eta_p=(d+1)\gamma_d v$. c_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi},\qquad
P_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}p,\qquad
m_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}g+\Psi_iR_j,
$$

\kappa=\frac{v_*+t}{1+e_*},\quad

d2b290ebd8e35052:05.statement:
Let $L_i(z,x)=v_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, $1\le i\le k$, be ambient affine cap margins on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$. Suppose the continuous normals form a minimal positive dependence, with weights $\lambda_i>0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$. Then their rank is $k-1$, so $k\le d+1$. After rescaling the margins by the respective $\lambda_i$, there is a single affine shear $x'=x+Az-y$ fixing $z$ such that the rescaled margins are
$$
\lambda_iL_i(z,x)=\lambda_i u_i\cdot x'+\ell(z),\qquad
\ell(z)=k^{-1}\sum_i\lambda_i(v_i\cdot z-b_i).
$$
This shear preserves the mixed lattice, each cap incidence, and full mixed volume on the fibers.

At a fixed base $z$, the open caps cover the entire continuous plane exactly when $\ell(z)>0$. For $\ell(z)=0$ the closed caps cover the plane, and the open caps miss exactly the common kernel of the continuous normals in the new coordinates. For $\ell(z)<0$ the closed caps miss $x'=0$. If $k=d+1$ and $\ell(z)>0$, the intersection of the closed caps in that fiber is the scale-$\ell(z)$ copy of the simplex at common term $1$.

Let $n,d\ge1$ and $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of positive summed full mixed volume $\mu$. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, let $h(y)$ denote its ambient raw closed-halfspace depth, and suppose $h(y)<T$ for every $y\in C\cap\Lambda$, where $T>0$. If $D_T=\{y:h(y)\ge T\}$ is nonempty, then for every $\eta>0$ there is a bounded full-dimensional polytope $Q_\eta$ disjoint from $\Lambda$, with
$$
D_T\subset\operatorname{int}Q_\eta\subset Q_\eta
\subset\{y:\operatorname{dist}(y,D_T)<\eta\},
$$
whose defining outward closed caps are nonvertical and have mass $<T$. Along $\eta\downarrow0$, every sequence of points in these polytopes, including attained projected-facet contacts, has all its cluster points in $D_T$.

d2f8ecd6d2f1309c:01.reason: The exact local anchored inverse 0a03438ff4e94ff8 starts at an interior concurrent mark and common raw mass. d2f8ecd6d2f1309c:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of volume $V$. Let the nonzero normals $u_i$, $1\le i\le m$, have rank $m-1$ and a dependence $\sum_i\rho_i u_i=0$ with every $\rho_i>0$. Suppose the closed caps $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ cover $\mathbb R^d$ and every $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$ is in $(0,V)$. There is a unique $t_*\in(0,\max_i A_i]$ at which moving the thresholds to give volumes $A_i'=\min(A_i,t_*)$ makes the planes concurrent. These caps are contained in the originals, remain proper, and cover $\mathbb R^d$. For every real $r<m$,
$$
\sum_i A_i'-r\min_i A_i'\le \sum_i A_i-r\min_i A_i,
$$
strictly if the original planes were not concurrent.

In particular, for $0\le r\le m-1$, a bound $\sum_i A_i-V\ge r\min_i A_i$ for every concurrent proper cover of $K$ with the given normals implies the bound for all whole-space closed covers with those normals, including zero and full caps. Equality for an original proper cover requires concurrency. The coefficient $r=m-1/\gamma_d$ with $m=d+1$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ lies in this range.

d2f8ecd6d2f1309c:02.reason: The tightening draft gives the transfer for proper covers and rules out nonconcurrent proper equality by strictness since $r\le m-1<m$. For a zero cap the union bound suffices. For a full cap subtract its mass $V$ and bound the remaining $m-1$ volumes below by the minimum. This is an immediate consequence of the same functional monotonicity, with these two boundary cases. For the displayed coefficient, $(1+1/d)^d\le d+1$ (equality at $d=1$, and $<e<3\le d+1$ when $d\ge2$), and $(1+1/d)^d\ge1$. Accepted ac7ba1e1e0ebc955 (2) already proves that numerical bound for any ordinary cover of $K$, so in this specialization the new information is proper equality concurrence.
d2f8ecd6d2f1309c:02.statement: For the same minimal positive circuit pattern and 0≤r≤m−1, a bound ∑A_i−V≥r min A_i for every concurrent proper cover implies the same bound for every whole-space cover with that pattern. d332d092619053f4:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K_1,\ldots,K_r$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$. Write $S_K$ for the pushforward of $\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{\partial K}$ by the almost everywhere unique outer unit normal. For $\lambda_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, let $M=\sum_j\lambda_jK_j$. For any finite nonnegative Borel measure $\nu$ on the sphere and constants $a_j\ge0$ with $S_{K_j}\ge a_j\nu$ for every $j$,
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j a_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\nu.
$$
For $\sigma=\sum_j S_{K_j}$ and $f_j=dS_{K_j}/d\sigma$, one also has
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j f_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\sigma.
$$
In particular, every common submeasure of $S_A,S_B$ is dominated by $S_{(1-t)A+tB}$ for $0\le t\le1$. This applies to the greatest common submeasure $S_A\wedge S_B$, whose density relative to $S_A+S_B$ is the minimum of the two densities. The coefficient one in the common-submeasure conclusion is sharp, and homothetic bodies attain equality in the density bound.

d358c029b6047209:01.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $d\ge0$. In any fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates, let $\pi_I$ delete integer coordinates indexed by $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$. For a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, including the empty set, put $A_I(K)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I K)$, where $\mu_{j,d}$ sums $d$-volume over the $\mathbb Z^j$ fibers. Use $\mu_{0,d}=\operatorname{vol}_d$ and count the nonempty singleton in dimension zero. Then
$$
|\mu_{n,d}(K)-\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(K)|\le \sum_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}} A_I(K).
$$
In particular, every closed ambient halfspace $H$ satisfies $\mu_{n,d}(C\cap H)\ge \operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(C\cap H)-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}A_I(C)$. Lower-dimensional sets and boundary fibers are included.

d358c029b6047209:03.statement:
Let $n\ge1,d\ge0,D=n+d$ and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body. Work in fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates and use the actual projected mixed volumes $A_I(C)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I C)$. Put $M=\mu_{n,d}(C)>0$, $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(C)$, $E=\sum_{I\ne\varnothing} A_I(C)$, $V_i=\operatorname{vol}_{D-1}(\pi_{\{i\}}C)$, and $\Gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$, $\Gamma_0=1$.

For the ordinary centroid $c$ and any real displacement $y=c+(\delta,0)$, every containing closed halfspace $H$ has ordinary cap volume at least $\Gamma_DV-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i$, and $V_i\le\sum_{I\ni i}A_I(C)$. In particular, round the integer coordinates of $c$ independently to nearest integers with deterministic ties, leaving the other coordinates fixed. At the resulting $y$ every containing closed halfspace has raw mixed mass at least
$$
\Gamma_DV-E-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i\ \ge\
B_\delta:=\Gamma_D M-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}
(\Gamma_D+1+\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|)A_I(C).
$$
If $B_\delta>0$, this $y$ belongs to the actual mixed set $S$ and to its convex hull. Let $B$ be the same expression with $\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|$ replaced by $|I|/2$. If $B\ge2^{-n}\Gamma_d M$, the rounded point attains at least $2^{-n}\Gamma_d$ normalized depth. In all cases the maximum normalized depth on $S$ is at least
$$
\max\{\Gamma_d W/M,\ \max(0,B)/M\},
\qquad W=\max_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z).
$$

Use unit counting mass on $S$ and take depth at a site to be the minimum mass of a closed ambient halfspace containing it. d46094c158197e98:01.reason: ec2b7d125fe6a3f0 with r=1 and v=h gives A≥h(T−W) by retaining the heaviest actual sampled site, but it does not integrate the adjacent volume roots or retain their sharp total-variation correction. The direct proof derives all parts without a graph prerequisite.
d46094c158197e98:01.statement:
Let $s\ge1$ be an integer, $Q\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact convex, and sample on a grid of spacing $h>0$. Enumerate the $N$ nonempty sampled fibers, including null ones, at consecutive grid sites. Write $w_j$ for their $s$-volumes, $T=\sum_j w_j$, $W=\max_jw_j$, and $A=\operatorname{vol}_{s+1}(Q)$, setting $T=W=0$ for an empty sample set. Then
$$
A\ge h\sum_{j=0}^{N-2}\Phi_s(w_j^{1/s},w_{j+1}^{1/s})
 \ge h\left(T-W+\frac{\operatorname{TV}(w)}{s+1}\right)\ge h(T-W),
$$
where $\Phi_s(a,b)=\sum_{k=0}^s a^kb^{s-k}/(s+1)$ and $\operatorname{TV}(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-2}|w_{j+1}-w_j|$. When $N\ge1$ the variation bound is equivalently
$$
A/h\ge T-\frac{s-1}{s+1}W-\frac{w_0+w_{N-1}}{s+1}.
$$
The coefficient $1/(s+1)$ is sharp.

for a fixed positive-volume $s$-body $K$ and vector $v$. For $T>0,N=1$, equality holds exactly when $Q$ consists of its unique sampled fiber. For $T=0$, equality holds exactly when $A=0$.

d485228e666ca27b:03.statement:
Let finitely many positive compact polytopal fibers $K_z$ be represented by the same nonvertical ambient inequality list $n_f\cdot x+a_f\cdot z\le b_f$, with each $n_f$ initially unit. Also fix a nonvertical ambient cap with margin $v_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x-b_j$ and initially unit $u_j$. In a joint coefficient direction write $r_f=\delta b_f-\delta a_f\cdot z-\delta n_f\cdot x$ and $\tau_j=\delta v_j\cdot z+\delta u_j\cdot x-\delta b_j$. For a fiber facet $F$, let $O(z,F)$ be its owners, the rows whose equality supports $F$. The one-sided total volume derivative is
$$
M'(\delta)=\min_{g\in G_0}g(\delta),\qquad
G_0=\left\{\delta\mapsto\sum_{z,F}\int_F\sum_{f\in O(z,F)}\omega_f r_f\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}:\ \omega_f\ge0,\ \sum_f\omega_f=1\right\}.
$$
All allocations are measurable. For each cap the one-sided derivative is at most $\max_{g\in G_j}g(\delta)$, where the compact convex set $G_j$ consists of
$$
\delta\mapsto \sum_{z,F}\int_F\sum_{f\in O(z,F)}\alpha_{jf}r_f\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
 +\sum_z\int \tau_j\,d\nu_{jz}.
$$
On a facet portion strictly inside the cap, $\alpha_{jf}\ge0$ sum to one, and strictly outside they vanish. A proper cap section contributes ordinary $(d-1)$-area to $\nu_{jz}$, and strict full, strict empty and lower-dimensional contact sections contribute zero. On a coincident facet $F$, the section measure is $\sigma_j\mathcal H^{d-1}|_F$ from the same allocation as the body term. If the body lies inside the cap, $\alpha_{jf},\sigma_j\ge0$ and $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}+\sigma_j=1$. If it lies outside, $\alpha_{jf}\ge0$ and $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}=\sigma_j\in[0,1]$. Use counting measure on endpoints and proper sections when $d=1$.

d485228e666ca27b:04.statement:
Fix $n,d,N\ge1$ and a nonempty finite lattice-convex $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ with $z_0\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}P\cap P$. Let a compatible family attain minimum normalized maximal closed-halfspace depth $\beta$ in the shared-plane class with $|K_{z_0}|_d=1$, and assume all its fibers are positive. Denote its total summed $d$-volume by $M$. Select whole critical groups from fiberwise maximizing marks and assign each $p\in P$ to one selected group covering the whole plane over $p$. At most $2^n$ deepest-origin groups suffice on the deepest bases. Assign each nondeep base to its own additional slack group. No group of mass below $\beta M$ covers a deepest base. Each group $i$ has positive fixed circuit weights $\rho_{ij}$, unit initial continuous normals $u_{ij}$, and projected margins $C_{ip}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}(v_{ij}\cdot p-b_{ij})\ge0$ for its assigned bases.

There are nonnegative cap multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$, zero for slack caps, nonnegative multipliers $\eta_{ip}$ of the assigned coverage inequalities, zero for strict inequalities, and one objective allocation $\omega$ and cap allocations $(\alpha_{ij},\nu_{ijz})$ of the owner-derivative lemma. For every shared body plane $f$ the measure $dW_f=(\omega_f-\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}\alpha_{ijf})\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ summed over its facet traces at their integer bases satisfies $\int dW_f=\int z\,dW_f=\int x\,dW_f=0$. Write $S_{ij},Z_{ij},X_{ij}$ for the mass, base first moment, and continuous first moment of $\sum_z\delta_z\otimes\nu_{ijz}$. For some $q_i\in\mathbb R^d$ and $t_i=\sum_p\eta_{ip}$ the same choices satisfy
$$
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=\rho_{ij}t_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} Z_{ij}=\rho_{ij}\sum_p\eta_{ip}p,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} X_{ij}=\rho_{ij}q_i,\qquad
\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta.
$$
For each stressed group $t_i>0$, all its caps carry stress and have a common effective-section centroid on their cap planes. Its base is $\sum_p\eta_{ip}p/t_i$, and its continuous coordinate differs from the $\eta$-weighted average of deepest marks at these bases by a vector in $\bigcap_j\ker u_{ij}$. In rank $d$ the two points coincide and their ambient depth, normalized by $M$, is $\beta$.

d494e7e71949ac0b:03.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. If $Z$ has a compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law on $\mathbb R$, then for every $s\ne0$,
$$
\mathbb P(Z\ge s)+\mathbb P(Z\ge -s)>2\Gamma_d.
$$
In particular, if $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a convex body with volume $V>0$ and centroid $g$, then for each $u\ne0$ and $s\ne0$ the two closed caps $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}$ and $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge -s\}$ have total volume greater than $2\Gamma_d V$.

d494e7e71949ac0b:04.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer, $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ a convex body, $\mu_K$ its normalized volume, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Define
$$
p_K(y)=\inf_{\substack{u\ne0\\s\in\mathbb R}}\frac{\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge s\}+\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge -s\}}{2}.
$$
The maximum $D_{\rm pair}(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y)$ exists, satisfies $D_{\rm pair}(K)\ge\Gamma_d$, and equals $\Gamma_d$ exactly for simplices.

For fixed $0<r\le R$ and $\varepsilon>0$, consider the bodies with $rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d$ whose Hausdorff distance to the set of full-dimensional simplices is at least $\varepsilon$. If this class is nonempty, then $D_{\rm pair}(K)-\Gamma_d$ attains a strictly positive minimum on it.

For uniform laws on convex bodies, the ambient supremum equals the maximum over the body. For fixed d≥3 and 0<r≤R, D_pair is Hausdorff-continuous on rB⊂K⊂RB. d4b2499d695ba5c9:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $k=d-1$ and $\delta>0$. Put $f(s)=s^{-d}$ for $s\ge\delta$ and continue by its affine tangent for $s\le\delta$. Let $q(s)=-f'(s)/d=\max(s,\delta)^{-d-1}$ and $R(s)=f(s)/q(s)$. Thus $R(s)=s$ above $\delta$ and $R(s)=(d+1)\delta-ds$ below it. Let $F_A,F_B$ be compact convex $k$-bodies in parallel affine planes, and let $F_K$ be a compact convex $k$-body in the midpoint plane containing $(F_A+F_B)/2$. All face measures are intrinsic $\mathcal H^k$. Fix $a,y$ with $L_K(m)=1+a\cdot(m-y)\ge\delta$ on $F_K$. Put $L_A^t(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)-t$, $L_B^t(x')=1+a\cdot(x'-y)+t$, $A(t)=\int_{F_A} f(L_A^t)$, $B(t)=\int_{F_B}f(L_B^t)$ and $M=\int_{F_K}f(L_K)$.

The minimum of $A(t)+B(t)$ is attained. At every minimizing $t$, omit its superscript and put $J=\int_{F_A}q(L_A)=\int_{F_B}q(L_B)>0$. There is one coupling $\pi$ of the probability laws $q(L_A)\,d\mathcal H^k/J$ and $q(L_B)\,d\mathcal H^k/J$, supported on $F_A\times F_B$, such that the pushforward under $(X,Y)\mapsto Z=(X+Y)/2$ satisfies
$$
\zeta=Z_\#\left(J\frac{R(L_A(X))+R(L_B(Y))}{2}\,\pi\right)\le f(L_K)\mathcal H^k|_{F_K},
\qquad
\zeta(F_K)=\frac{A(t)+B(t)}2.
$$
The midpoint map is injective on the parametrized interior coupling constructed in the proof. In particular $\min_t[A(t)+B(t)]\le 2M$, with sharp factor two even for $a\ne0$. When $a\ne0$, each $t$ is realized by physical center parameters $c_A=y+ta/\lVert a\rVert^2$, $c_B=y-ta/\lVert a\rVert^2$ with average $y$. When $a=0$ the scalar theorem permits the stated denominator offsets independently of center shifts.
